title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午浙江當大比士維
時巡按御史張文煕寔監臨
之旣入院簡諸執事若提調
屬諸藩使吳自新顧養謙監
試屬諸臬使馮時雨楊標分
司校事以九校官而以溥與
===
敎諭程端容陳文銓陳承芳
區大憲訓導趙思基王天麟
張炳龍起春署其裁焉於是
合督學憲臣劉東星所選士
凡二千七百有奇三試之得
九十人以
獻有司者按故事宴而成之於
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序
萬曆壬午，浙江當大比士。維時巡按御史張文煕寔監臨之。旣入院，簡諸執事：若提調屬諸藩使吳自新、顧養謙，監試屬諸臬使馮時雨、楊標，分司校事以九校官，而以溥與敎諭程端容、陳文銓、陳承芳、區大憲，訓導趙思基、王天麟、張炳、龍起春署其裁焉。於是合督學憲臣劉東星所選士凡二千七百有奇，三試之，得九十人以獻。有司者按故事宴而成之。於
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination
In the renwu year of the Wanli era (1582), it was time for Zhejiang to hold the great triennial examination of scholars. At that time, Regional Inspector Zhang Wenxi 張文煕 served as Supervising Official. Once he had entered the examination compound, he selected the various functionaries: the duties of Proctor were entrusted to the Provincial Administration Commission officials Wu Zixin 吳自新 and Gu Yangqian 顧養謙; the duties of Surveillance Commissioner of the Examination were entrusted to the Provincial Surveillance Commission officials Feng Shiyu 馮時雨 and Yang Biao 楊標; and the tasks of reading and grading the papers in the various wards were assigned to nine examining officials, with myself, Pu 溥, together with Instructors Cheng Duanrong 程端容, Chen Wenquan 陳文銓, Chen Chengfang 陳承芳, and Ou Daxian 區大憲, and Assistant Instructors Zhao Siji 趙思基, Wang Tianlin 王天麟, Zhang Bing 張炳, and Long Qichun 龍起春 appointed to oversee the adjudication. Thereupon, gathering the scholars selected by the Education Intendant and surveillance official Liu Dongxing 劉東星, numbering over two thousand seven hundred in all, we examined them in three sessions and obtained ninety men to present to the Throne. In accordance with precedent, the authorities held a banquet to bring the ceremony to completion. Thereupon…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是溥拜稽首颺言曰綦重哉
選爾諸士乎爾諸士今者之
遭固卽古所謂賓興者也古
者賓興一物不備則不得爾
諸士操寸管而得之何異穎
脫我聞曰以此思易則難者
至以此思難則易者至爾諸
===
士姑毋自榮侈有執鞭弭而
策爾者至焉已何者士平居
博衣峩冠哆口而談當世之
務具曰能矣及一旦猝及之
或艱投之吾不知整暇得似
平日否也不幸一不當事機
呼吸之間存亡互異股且立
punctuated: 是溥拜稽首颺言曰：「綦重哉，選爾諸士乎！爾諸士今者之遭，固卽古所謂賓興者也。古者賓興，一物不備則不得；爾諸士操寸管而得之，何異穎脫？我聞曰：『以此思易，則難者至；以此思難，則易者至。』爾諸士姑毋自榮侈，有執鞭弭而策爾者至焉已。何者？士平居博衣峩冠，哆口而談當世之務，具曰『能矣』。及一旦猝及之，或艱投之，吾不知整暇得似平日否也？不幸一不當事機，呼吸之間，存亡互異，股且立
translation_en: … Thereupon I, [Jiang] Pu, bowed and touched my forehead to the ground, proclaiming aloud: "How supremely weighty is the selection of all you scholars! What you scholars have encountered today is indeed what in antiquity was called 'elevating the worthy as honored guests' (binxing). In antiquity, in elevating the worthy as honored guests, if even a single quality was lacking, one would not be chosen; yet you scholars wield a short writing brush and attain it—how does this differ from an awl's point piercing straight through a bag? I have heard it said: 'If by this one considers things easy, then difficulties will arrive; if by this one considers things difficult, then ease will arrive.' For the moment, you scholars should not pride yourselves in extravagance; there will soon come that which holds whip and bow-ends to spur you on! Why do I say this? In ordinary life, scholars wear broad robes and tall caps, opening their mouths wide to discuss the affairs of the present age, and all say, 'We are capable!' Yet once emergencies suddenly befall them, or hardships are cast upon them, I do not know whether their composure and readiness can match that of ordinary days. Should they unfortunately fail just once to meet the critical juncture of events, in the space of a single breath survival and ruin are reversed, and their legs will immediately [tremble]…"

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
弁卽屬者士譁於伍隨之以
羣不逞訌然横作有司者旋
報讋定
國家承平二百餘年安於覆盂
意外之虞萬萬無之然是時
亦可謂猝矣爾諸士曷以應
斯夫浙固龍子之所宮也自
===
神禹告功至大越上茅山萬
玉帛不戒自集汪罔氏殱焉
何其震也厥後無餘都秦餘
望南千有餘歲而至句踐句
踐欲雪吳恥敎士十年有君
子六千人君子云者卽吳所
名賢良齊所名節制士盡姑
punctuated: 弁。卽屬者士譁於伍，隨之以羣不逞訌然横作，有司者旋報讋定。國家承平二百餘年，安於覆盂，意外之虞，萬萬無之，然是時亦可謂猝矣，爾諸士曷以應斯？夫浙固龍子之所宮也。自神禹告功，至大越上茅山，萬玉帛不戒自集，汪罔氏殱焉，何其震也！厥後無餘都秦餘望南，千有餘歲而至句踐。句踐欲雪吳恥，敎士十年，有君子六千人。君子云者，卽吳所名賢良、齊所名節制，士盡姑
translation_en: … [legs will tremble at once, and hands will] shake. Just recently, soldiers clamored in the ranks, followed by crowds of malcontents who rose up in clamorous lawlessness, though the authorities soon reported that they had been cowed and pacified. The Dynastic State has enjoyed peace for over two hundred years, as stable as an overturned bowl, and unforeseen dangers are utterly out of the question; yet that moment could certainly be called sudden! How would you gentlemen respond to such a thing? Now, Zhejiang is indeed the palace of the Dragon's Son. Since the divine Yu reported the completion of his labors, arriving at Great Yue and ascending Mount Mao, the myriad lords with their jade and silk assembled of their own accord without being summoned, and the Wangmang clan was executed there—how awe-inspiring that was! Thereafter, Wuyu established his capital south of Qinyuwang, and after more than a thousand years it came down to Goujian. Goujian wished to wipe away the shame inflicted by Wu; he trained his troops for ten years and had six thousand "gentlemen" (junzi). Those called "gentlemen" were precisely what Wu called "the worthy and good" (xianliang) and what Qi called "disciplined troops" (jiezhi)—warriors who were all natives of the region [east of] Gu…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蔑以東禦兒以南產也今尺
籍隸者何獨非其人然考其
時越人士乃無擇老幼咸願
畢力以致義烈於其主蓋至
於報吳存國會齊晉諸侯於
泗上天王賜胙命伯而後知
六千人者眞君子哉何其訓
===
之而卽順用之而輒效也爾
諸士知有紙上陳言耳其所
稱說千歲以前事若數一二
別白黑可謂較甚然吾不敢
遽準何者人無難於懸斷難
於嘗試事無難於隨順難於
猝乘故應猝者貴豫明試者
punctuated: 蔑以東、禦兒以南產也。今尺籍隸者，何獨非其人？然考其時，越人士乃無擇老幼，咸願畢力，以致義烈於其主。蓋至於報吳存國，會齊、晉諸侯於泗上，天王賜胙命伯，而後知六千人者眞君子哉！何其訓之而卽順，用之而輒效也！爾諸士知有紙上陳言耳，其所稱說千歲以前事，若數一二、別白黑，可謂較甚；然吾不敢遽準。何者？人無難於懸斷，難於嘗試；事無難於隨順，難於猝乘。故應猝者貴豫，明試者
translation_en: … the East of Gumie and South of Yuer. Why should those enrolled in the military registers today not be the same kind of men? Yet if we examine that era, the men of Yue, regardless of whether they were old or young, all wished to exhaust their strength to devote their righteous ardor to their ruler. Indeed, only when they had avenged themselves on Wu and preserved their state, assembled with the feudal lords of Qi and Jin above the Si River, and received sacrificial meat from the Heavenly King along with the mandate as Hegemon, did one know that those six thousand men were truly "gentlemen"! How readily they obeyed as soon as they were trained, and how immediately effective they were whenever they were employed! You scholars know only stale words on paper. When you speak of events from a thousand years ago, it is like counting one and two or distinguishing white from black—one might call it exceedingly clear; yet I dare not hastily take it as a standard. Why is this? For men, there is no difficulty in making abstract judgments from afar; the difficulty lies in putting them to the test of action. For affairs, there is no difficulty in going along smoothly; the difficulty lies in seizing sudden emergencies. Therefore, in responding to sudden emergencies one values preparedness, and in clearly testing [men]…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以功吾姑置遠事弗論論其
近者昔劉文成豎儒耳躡屨
擔簦以見
高皇帝一語建萬世之業摧强敵
蕩腥虜儵忽萬變而不窮于
肅愍一綈袍上
殿腋
===
景皇除姦肅紀片言而定遂收
回蹕之勳王新建幅巾講道俄
聞宸濠之變馳入吉安一麾
而逆藩授首夫此三君非當
時所謂龍化虎變之大人觸
斯應應斯效者邪諸士幸生
三君後未嘗身際斯景徒執
punctuated: 以功。吾姑置遠事弗論，論其近者。昔劉文成，豎儒耳，躡屨擔簦以見高皇帝，一語建萬世之業，摧强敵，蕩腥虜，儵忽萬變而不窮；于肅愍，一綈袍上殿，腋景皇，除姦肅紀，片言而定，遂收回蹕之勳；王新建，幅巾講道，俄聞宸濠之變，馳入吉安，一麾而逆藩授首。夫此三君，非當時所謂龍化虎變之大人，觸斯應、應斯效者邪？諸士幸生三君後，未嘗身際斯景，徒執
translation_en: … by results. Let me set aside distant events without discussing them, and discuss those that are recent. In the past, Liu Wencheng 劉文成 (Liu Ji 劉基) was merely a humble scholar; wearing straw sandals and carrying an umbrella on his shoulder, he went to see the Exalted Emperor (Gao Huangdi 高皇帝, i.e., Emperor Taizu), and with a single word founded an enterprise for ten thousand generations—crushing powerful enemies, sweeping away the foul northern nomads, and remaining inexhaustible through sudden and myriad changes. Yu Suming 于肅愍 (Yu Qian 于謙) ascended the palace hall in a single coarse silk robe, supported Emperor Jing (Jinghuang 景皇) by the arm, eliminated traitors and restored discipline, settling matters with a few words and thereby achieving the merit of bringing back the imperial carriage. Wang Xinjian 王新建 (Wang Shouren 王守仁, Earl of Xinjian) was wearing a cloth head-kerchief and lecturing on the Way when he suddenly heard of the rebellion of Chenhao 宸濠 (Zhu Chenhao 朱宸濠); he galloped into Ji'an 吉安, and at a single wave of his banner the rebel prince surrendered his head. Now, were not these three gentlemen what their contemporaries called great men who transformed like dragons and changed like tigers—responding the moment they were touched, and succeeding the moment they responded? You scholars are fortunate to have been born after these three gentlemen and have never personally encountered such circumstances; if you merely cling to…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
臆見騁筆鋒以摧古今之非
是則可若漫自謂能劻勷割
煩劇前無千古後無三君此
大言無當人耳何實之可効
主上圖新化理日警於有位非篤
誠不二心之臣不以登非懇
悃之論不以見於行古之君
===
子居安類不忘危今地誠大
人誠眾物力誠詘謠俗誠澆
具鏡於吾前有象爾諸士處
不諱之
朝宜如何奮夫智者燭萌勇者
薙本豫之弗謀而猝是謀鮮
不躓矣其務竭款款無貳爾
punctuated: 臆見，騁筆鋒以摧古今之非是，則可；若漫自謂能劻勷割煩劇，前無千古，後無三君，此大言無當人耳，何實之可効？主上圖新化理，日警於有位，非篤誠不二心之臣不以登，非懇悃之論不以見於行。古之君子，居安類不忘危。今地誠大，人誠眾，物力誠詘，謠俗誠澆，具鏡於吾前，有象爾。諸士處不諱之朝，宜如何奮？夫智者燭萌，勇者薙本；豫之弗謀，而猝是謀，鮮不躓矣。其務竭款款，無貳爾
translation_en: …their own subjective opinions, giving free rein to the tip of the brush to demolish the rights and wrongs of past and present, that is easy enough. Yet if one casually boasts of being able to assist the state in crises and slice through complex affairs, claiming that there is no match in a thousand years of antiquity before, nor the three worthies after—these are merely grandiloquent speakers of empty words; what practical results can they deliver? Our Sovereign seeks to renew transforming governance and daily admonishes those in office: unless one is a minister of steadfast sincerity and undivided loyalty, he is not advanced; unless it is a discourse of earnest sincerity, it is not put into practice. When the gentlemen of antiquity dwelt in security, they generally did not forget danger. Today, the territory is truly vast, the population is truly numerous, material resources are truly depleted, and popular customs are truly decadent—all this is mirrored before us in clear manifestation. Living in a court that does not taboo frank speech, how ought you scholars to rouse yourselves? Now, the wise illuminate the first sprouts of trouble, and the brave weed out the roots. If one does not plan beforehand, and plans only when things happen suddenly, rarely will one avoid stumbling. Strive to exhaust your utmost sincerity; do not divide your…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心無飾爾言久將
主自明不易哉其治天下乎是在
諸士先是三月屬前所指譁
士者
上命少司馬張佳胤以都御史撫
定之大江以南式底靜謐維
時御史孫旬風猷肅穆佐都
===
御史御史若輔車然於是言
官謂浙事重宜更置大僚乃
簡藩臣舒應龍等臬臣徐元泰等
以往誠重之也若刑部郎中
霍鎮東以省刑至户部主事
韓取善以督漕至工部主事
王謙南京户部主事朱讓以
punctuated:
心，無飾爾言，久將主自明。不易哉其治天下乎！是在諸士。
先是三月，屬前所指譁士者，上命少司馬張佳胤以都御史撫定之，大江以南式底靜謐。維時御史孫旬風猷肅穆，佐都御史，御史若輔車然。於是言官謂浙事重，宜更置大僚，乃簡藩臣舒應龍等、臬臣徐元泰等以往，誠重之也。若刑部郎中霍鎮東以省刑至，户部主事韓取善以督漕至，工部主事王謙、南京户部主事朱讓以
translation_en:
…minds, and do not embellish your words; in time, the Sovereign will naturally see clearly. Is it not no easy matter to govern the Empire! This rests with you gentlemen.

Earlier, in the third month, following the incident of the clamoring soldiers referred to above, His Majesty ordered Vice Minister of War Zhang Jiayin 張佳胤, serving as Censor-in-Chief, to pacify and settle them, and the region south of the Great River was thereby brought to peace and tranquility. At that time, Investigating Censor Sun Xun 孫旬, whose bearing and counsel were solemn and dignified, assisted the Censor-in-Chief, the Censor-in-Chief and Investigating Censor working together as closely as cheek and jawbone. Thereupon, the speaking officials stated that affairs in Zhejiang were of great importance and that the senior provincial officials ought to be replaced; thus, Administration Commissioner Shu Yinglong 舒應龍 and others, and Surveillance Commissioner Xu Yuantai 徐元泰 and others, were selected to go there, truly because of the importance attached to the region. As for Director in the Ministry of Justice Huo Zhendong 霍鎮東, who arrived to review penal cases; Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue Han Qushan 韓取善, who arrived to superintend grain transport; and Secretary in the Ministry of Works Wang Qian 王謙 and Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue Zhu Rang 朱讓, who [arrived] to…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
權關王均樂觀厥盛而左參
政劉世賞副使陳澗張子仁
署都指揮僉事常錞王接武
錢經濟亦胥有職於棘院者
焉若副使徐汝陽參議唐本
堯署都指揮僉事馬繼武先
期入
===
賀前左布政使游季勳劉漢儒
右布政使郝杰按察使王湘
僉事許一德李宗魯皆始事
有勞得附書
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教
諭周溥謹序
punctuated:
權關王，均樂觀厥盛。而左參政劉世賞、副使陳澗、張子仁、署都指揮僉事常錞、王接武、錢經濟，亦胥有職於棘院者焉。若副使徐汝陽、參議唐本堯、署都指揮僉事馬繼武先期入賀，前左布政使游季勳、劉漢儒、右布政使郝杰、按察使王湘、僉事許一德、李宗魯皆始事有勞，得附書。
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教諭周溥謹序。
translation_en:
…arrived to collect customs duties [reading 王 as 至], all took pleasure in witnessing this grand occasion. Moreover, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Liu Shishang 劉世賞, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Jian 陳澗 and Zhang Ziren 張子仁, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Chang Chun 常錞, Wang Jiewu 王接武, and Qian Jingji 錢經濟 also all held duties in the examination compound. As for Surveillance Vice Commissioner Xu Ruyang 徐汝陽, Administration Assistant Commissioner Tang Benyao 唐本堯, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Ma Jiwu 馬繼武, who departed ahead of time to enter the capital for audience congratulations, and the former Left Administration Commissioners You Jixun 游季勳 and Liu Hanru 劉漢儒, Right Administration Commissioner Hao Jie 郝杰, Surveillance Commissioner Wang Xiang 王湘, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Xu Yide 許一德 and Li Zonglu 李宗魯, all contributed their efforts at the beginning of the undertaking and thus merit being recorded alongside the others.

Respectfully prefaced by Zhou Pu 周溥, Instructor of the Confucian School of Kunshan County 崑山縣, Suzhou Prefecture 蘇州府, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸).

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
萬曆拾年浙江鄉試
監臨官
巡按浙江監察御史張文煕〔質卿廣西臨桂縣人丁丑進士〕
提調官
浙江等處承宣布政使司右參政吳自新〔伯恒應天府江寧縣籍直隸祁門縣人戊辰進士〕
浙江等處承宣布政使司右參議顧養謙〔益卿直隸通州人乙丑進士〕
監試官
浙江等處提刑按察司副使馮時雨〔化之直隸長洲縣籍崑山縣人戊辰進士〕
浙江等處提刑按察司副使楊標〔廷瞻江西清江縣人丙辰進士〕
===
考試官
直隸蘇州府崑山縣儒學教諭周溥〔德元廣東瓊山縣人丁卯貢士〕
江西吉安府廬陵縣儒學教諭程端容〔孟禮直隸婺源縣人庚午貢士〕
同考試官
江西贛州府會昌縣儒學教諭陳文銓〔子衡福建福清縣人丁卯貢士〕
直隸徽州府黟縣儒學教諭陳承芳〔萬春福建莆田縣人庚午貢士〕

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
康誥曰如保赤子心誠求之雖不中不遠
矣未有學養子而后嫁者也
子曰不得中行而與之必也狂狷乎狂者
進取狷者有所不爲也
徐子曰仲尼亟稱於水曰水哉水哉何取
於水也孟子曰原泉混混不舍晝夜盈
科而後進放乎四海有本者如是是之
===
取爾苟爲無本七八月之間雨集溝澮
皆盈其涸也可立而待也故聲聞過情
君子恥之
易
初九拔茅茹以其彙征吉象曰拔茅征吉
志在外也九二包荒用馮河不遐遺朋
亡得尚于中行象曰包荒得尚于中行
以光大也九三无平不陂无往不復艱
貞无咎勿恤其孚于食有福象曰无往
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

《康誥》曰：「如保赤子。」心誠求之，雖不中，不遠矣。未有學養子而后嫁者也。

子曰：「不得中行而與之，必也狂狷乎！狂者進取，狷者有所不爲也。」

徐子曰：「仲尼亟稱於水，曰：『水哉，水哉！』何取於水也？」孟子曰：「原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。苟爲無本，七八月之間雨集，溝澮皆盈；其涸也，可立而待也。故聲聞過情，君子恥之。」

易

初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。《象》曰：「拔茅征吉」，志在外也。九二，包荒，用馮河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。《象》曰：「包荒，得尚于中行」，以光大也。九三，无平不陂，无往不復，艱貞无咎，勿恤其孚，于食有福。《象》曰：「无往…
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

The Announcement to Kang (Kang gao) says, "Act as if you were watching over an infant." If a mother is sincerely trying, even if she does not guess its desires right, she will not be far from doing so. There has never been a girl who learned to bring up a child before she married.

The Master said, "Having failed to find moderate men to impart my teachings to, I must turn to the ardent and the cautiously independent! The ardent will advance and lay hold of truth; the cautiously independent will keep themselves from doing what is wrong."

Master Xu (Xuzi) said, "Confucius (Zhongni) often praised water, saying, 'O water! O water!' What did he find in water to approve of?" Mencius (Mengzi) replied, "Waters from a source come gushing out, never ceasing day or night. Waiting until they have filled the hollows, they then go on, reaching even to the Four Seas. Such is the nature of things that have a source, and it was just this that he approved of. Suppose a thing has no source: in the seventh and eighth months when the rain falls abundantly, the ditches and channels are all filled, but we may stand and wait to see them dry up again. Thus a superior man is ashamed of a reputation beyond his true merits."

Book of Changes (Yi)

Nine in the first place: Pulling up thatch grass, its roots come with its kind. Setting forth brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'Pulling up thatch grass, setting forth brings good fortune'—his will is set on what is outside." Nine in the second place: Embracing the uncultivated, crossing the river without a boat, not neglecting what is distant, parting from one's clique; thus one manages to match the way of the mean. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Embracing the uncultivated, managing to match the way of the mean'—because his light is great." Nine in the third place: There is no plain not followed by a slope; there is no going forth not followed by a return. In hardship, perseverance brings no blame. Do not grieve over its truth; in eating and drinking there will be blessing. The Commentary on the Images says: "'There is no going forth…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不復天地際也
象曰玉鉉在上剛柔節也
見乃謂之象
師者眾也眾必有所比故受之以比
書
曰后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民
敏德帝曰俞允若茲嘉言罔攸伏野無
遺賢萬邦咸寧稽于眾舍己從人不虐
無告不廢困窮惟帝時克
===
若農服田力穡乃亦有秋
惟御事厥棐有恭
旌别淑慝表厥宅里彰善癉惡樹之風聲
弗率訓典殊厥井疆俾克畏慕申畫郊
圻慎固封守以康四海
詩
淑人君子其儀一兮其儀一兮心如結兮
我孔熯矣式禮莫愆工祝致告徂賚孝孫
苾芬孝祀神嗜飲食卜爾百福如幾如
punctuated:
不復，天地際也。」
「《象》曰：玉鉉在上，剛柔節也。」
「見乃謂之象。」
「師者，眾也；眾必有所比，故受之以《比》。」

《書》：
「曰：『后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。』帝曰：『俞！允若茲，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于眾，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。』」
「若農服田力穡，乃亦有秋。」
「惟御事，厥棐有恭。」
「旌别淑慝，表厥宅里，彰善癉惡，樹之風聲。弗率訓典，殊厥井疆，俾克畏慕。申畫郊圻，慎固封守，以康四海。」

《詩》：
「淑人君子，其儀一兮；其儀一兮，心如結兮。」
「我孔熯矣，式禮莫愆。工祝致告，徂賚孝孫：『苾芬孝祀，神嗜飲食，卜爾百福，如幾如
translation_en:
…without return”: this is where Heaven and Earth meet.”
“The Commentary on the Images says: “Choosing to use rings of jade at the top” shows how the firm and the yielding are kept in due proportion.”
“When manifested in visible phenomena, it is called an image.”
““Multitude” means the masses; the masses must have something to which they cleave in close union, and therefore it is followed by the hexagram “Union” (Bi).”

Book of Documents (Shu):
“[Yu] said: ‘If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of his sovereignty, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of his ministry, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will sedulously seek virtue.’ The Emperor said: ‘Yes! Really let it be thus, and good words will nowhere lie hidden, no worthy men will be left neglected in the wilds, and the myriad states will all enjoy repose. To consult the multitude, setting aside one’s own views to follow others, not oppressing the helpless, nor neglecting the straitened and poor—only the Emperor [Yao] was able to do this.’”
“Like a husbandman who works his fields and labors at his reaping, there is then also an autumn harvest.”
“As for those who manage affairs, their assisting was marked by reverence.”
“Distinguish the good and the evil, mark the gates of their hamlet dwellings, make manifest the good and make loathsome the evil, establishing the influence and reputation of their deeds. As for those who do not follow the instructive canons, set apart their well-field boundaries, so that they may learn both to fear and to emulate. Clearly define the suburban borders and carefully strengthen the frontier defenses, so as to bring peace to all within the four seas.”

Book of Odes (Shi):
“The good man, the princely lord, / His deportment is invariable; / His deportment is invariable, / And his heart is as if tied fast.”
“We are very exhausted, / And have performed every ceremony without error. / The skillful invocators convey the message, / Going to present it to the filial descendant: / ‘Fragrant has been your filial sacrifice, / And the spirits have enjoyed the drink and food. / They foretell for you a hundred blessings, / According to the due season, according to…’”

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
式旣齊旣稷旣匡旣敕永錫爾極時萬

大任有身生此文王
敬之敬之天惟顯思命不易哉

遂及齊侯宋公盟莊公十有九年
楚人侵鄭僖公二年齊人執陳轅濤塗僖

===
夏齊侯衞侯胥命于蒲桓公三年秋八月
諸侯盟于首止僖公五年九月戊辰諸
侯盟于葵丘僖公九年公會晉侯宋公

式，旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕，永錫爾極，時萬時億。

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陰陽和而萬物得
是故樂之隆非極音也食饗之禮非致味
也清廟之瑟朱絃而疏越壹倡而三歎
有遺音者矣大饗之禮尚玄酒而俎腥
魚大羹不和有遺味者矣
備者百順之名也
子云善則稱君過則稱己則民作忠君陳
曰爾有嘉謀嘉猷入告爾君于內女乃
順之于外曰此謀此猷惟我君之德於
===
乎是惟良顯哉
第貳場
論
天下國家之大務
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石修職詔〔景帝後二年〕
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬
punctuated:
陰陽和而萬物得。
是故樂之隆，非極音也；食饗之禮，非致味也。清廟之瑟，朱絃而疏越，壹倡而三歎，有遺音者矣；大饗之禮，尚玄酒而俎腥魚，大羹不和，有遺味者矣。
備者，百順之名也。
子云：「善則稱君，過則稱己，則民作忠。《君陳》曰：『爾有嘉謀嘉猷，入告爾君于內，女乃順之于外，曰：「此謀此猷，惟我君之德。」於乎！是惟良顯哉！』」

第貳場
論
天下國家之大務。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石修職詔〔景帝後二年〕
擬唐以房玄齡、杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬
translation_en:
"When yin and yang are in harmony, all things obtain their due."

"Therefore, the culmination of music does not lie in the utmost indulgence of sound, nor do the rites of food and banquets lie in the perfection of flavor. The zither of the 'Clear Temple' (Qingmiao) has vermilion strings and widely spaced sound-holes; when one person leads the singing and three join in with sighs, there is a lingering sound left unsaid. In the ceremony of the great banquet, dark water (xuanjiu) is esteemed above all, raw fish is placed on the sacrificial stands, and the great broth is unseasoned; there is a lingering flavor left unexhausted."

"Completeness (bei) is the name given to the hundred顺 [harmonies/compliances]."

"The Master said: 'When attributing what is good to the ruler and taking faults upon oneself, the people are moved to loyalty. The "Jun Chen" says: "When you have fine plans and fine counsels, go in and announce them to your ruler within; then comply with them outside, saying: 'These plans and these counsels are all due to the virtue of our ruler.' Oh! How excellent and illustrious this is!"'"

Second Session

Discourse (lun)
"The great affairs of the realm and the state."

Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials (zhao, gao, biao) [examined on one topic from among these]:
Imitation of a Han-dynasty edict ordering officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank to attend diligently to their duties [2nd year of the Latter Era of Emperor Jing (142 BCE)].

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
御製輔臣賛和詩集序
示大學士楊一清等謝表〔嘉靖七年〕
判語〔五條〕
收藏禁書及私習天文
投匿名文書告言人罪
在官求索借貸人財物
虛費工力採取不堪用
織造違禁龍鳳文段疋
第叄場
===
第五道
問自古聖帝明王雖履泰寧之世猶然兢
業抑畏延納忠謨唐虞邈矣逮商周時
如伊傅姬公之告其君動稱先王以爲
儆戒廼其君不憚委己從之迄爲一代
令主登上理而鞏鴻圖治固莫尚於法
祖與三代而下有書貞觀政要於屏風
每正容斂手而讀之者有進講三朝寶
訓注目傾耳隨事咨詢不倦者視商周
punctuated:
御製《輔臣賛和詩集序》示大學士楊一清等謝表〔嘉靖七年〕。

判語〔五條〕：
收藏禁書及私習天文；
投匿名文書告言人罪；
在官求索借貸人財物；
虛費工力採取不堪用；
織造違禁龍鳳文段疋。

第叄場

第五道：
問：自古聖帝明王，雖履泰寧之世，猶然兢業抑畏，延納忠謨。唐、虞邈矣，逮商、周時，如伊、傅、姬公之告其君，動稱先王以爲儆戒；廼其君不憚委己從之，迄爲一代令主，登上理而鞏鴻圖。治固莫尚於法祖與？三代而下，有書《貞觀政要》於屏風，每正容斂手而讀之者；有進講《三朝寶訓》，注目傾耳，隨事咨詢不倦者。視商、周

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
令主奚殊夷考其實政乃不逮遠甚意
者其詒謀不足法耶亡其誦法者以文
不以實耶何治效之闊疎也洪惟我
祖
宗創造於前
列聖紹庥於後至我
皇上益繼序而闡揚之
聖德睿猷卓邁千古矣頃歲
俞輔臣之請輯
===
累朝
訓錄分類編摩稍倣貞觀政要釐爲條目者以
四十計
便殿進
講
特賜延納凜然陟降紹庭之思矣顧孫卿有言
主術約而易操也主好要則百事詳卽
此四十事者一一而畫之日亦不遑給
耳玆欲掇要探本稽
punctuated: 令主奚殊？夷考其實政，乃不逮遠甚。意者其詒謀不足法耶？亡其誦法者以文不以實耶？何治效之闊疎也！洪惟我祖宗創造於前，列聖紹庥於後，至我皇上，益繼序而闡揚之，聖德睿猷，卓邁千古矣。頃歲俞輔臣之請，輯累朝訓錄，分類編摩，稍倣《貞觀政要》，釐爲條目者以四十計。便殿進講，特賜延納，凜然陟降紹庭之思矣。顧孫卿有言：「主術約而易操也，主好要則百事詳。」卽此四十事者，一一而畫之，日亦不遑給耳。玆欲掇要探本，稽
translation_en:
…admirable rulers [of the Shang and Zhou], how did they differ? Yet when we calmly examine their actual governance, it fell far short. Could it be that the counsels bequeathed to them were unworthy of emulation? Or was it rather that those who recited and emulated them did so in mere form rather than in substance? Why were the effects of their governance so remote and slight!

We humbly reflect how Our Imperial Ancestors founded the dynasty in the past, and the Successive Sacred Emperors continued their blessings thereafter; down to His Majesty the Emperor, who has further succeeded to the line and gloriously expounded their legacy, so that His sacred virtue and wise plans far surpass all antiquity. In recent years, granting the request of the Grand Secretaries, He had the Precious Injunctions and Veritable Records (Xunlu) of the successive reigns compiled, classified and edited in rough imitation of the Essentials of Government of the Zhenguan Reign (Zhenguan zhengyao), and arranged into some forty topical categories. When these were presented and expounded in the side halls of the palace, He specially granted them a receptive hearing, filled with reverent thoughts of His ancestors ascending and descending in the court.

Yet Xun Qing (Xunzi) had a saying: "The art of the ruler is concise and easy to grasp; when the ruler loves the essential, the hundred affairs are attended to in detail." If one were to plan out these forty matters one by one, the days would not be long enough to suffice. Now, if we wish to gather the essentials and probe the fundamentals, examining…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖
宗故實爲我
皇上保治之助爾多士其各攄所見焉
問人主需材以易天下奚啻饑渴顧材品
不同真似靡辨脫眩於名實則似材者
類得以倖進而真材隱矣我思古人有
名實之相副者有有其實而無其名者
有有其名而無其實者有蚤蒙不美之
名而晚令者有始被貪濁之名而終著
===
高操者有初陷兇惡之名而後更改行
者有陽附君子之名而陰實爲小人者
有外近小人之名而中實爲君子者蓋
不可以一端盡也人主亦安從而辨之
俾不爲名實所眩歟夫徇名而失實有
國者之大患也玆欲俾登進者皆真材
而各獲其用似材者罔所售而倖進之
竇塞果何道而可諸士抱材而待用久
矣幸相與盡言之以驗知人之鑒
punctuated:
祖宗故實，爲我皇上保治之助。爾多士其各攄所見焉。

問：人主需材以易天下，奚啻饑渴？顧材品不同，真似靡辨。脫眩於名實，則似材者類得以倖進，而真材隱矣。我思古人，有名實之相副者，有有其實而無其名者，有有其名而無其實者，有蚤蒙不美之名而晚令者，有始被貪濁之名而終著高操者，有初陷兇惡之名而後更改行者，有陽附君子之名而陰實爲小人者，有外近小人之名而中實爲君子者，蓋不可以一端盡也。人主亦安從而辨之，俾不爲名實所眩歟？夫徇名而失實，有國者之大患也。玆欲俾登進者皆真材，而各獲其用；似材者罔所售，而倖進之竇塞，果何道而可？諸士抱材而待用久矣，幸相與盡言之，以驗知人之鑒。
translation_en:
… the historical precedents of the imperial ancestors, as an aid to His Majesty in preserving good governance. May all you gentlemen each set forth your views.

Question: A ruler needs talent to transform the empire—how is that desire any less urgent than hunger and thirst? Yet the qualities of talent differ, and the genuine is hard to distinguish from the specious. If one is dazzled by reputation versus reality, then those with specious talent are generally able to advance by luck, while genuine talent remains hidden. When I reflect upon the ancients, there were those whose reputation and reality matched each other; those who possessed the reality without the reputation; those who possessed the reputation without the reality; those who early on bore an unsavory reputation yet became admirable in their later years; those who initially suffered a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately displayed lofty integrity; those who at first fell into a reputation for fierceness and wickedness yet later reformed their conduct; those who outwardly attached themselves to the reputation of a gentleman while secretly acting as petty men; and those who externally came close to the reputation of a petty man while inwardly being true gentlemen—indeed, they cannot be exhausted by any single category. How, then, is a ruler to distinguish among them so as not to be dazzled by reputation and reality? Now, pursuing reputation while losing sight of reality is a great peril for those who hold a state. If we now wish to ensure that all who are promoted and advanced are genuine talents and that each obtains his proper use, while those of specious talent have no way to peddle themselves and the channels of opportunistic advancement are blocked, by what way indeed can this be achieved? You gentlemen have cherished your talents and awaited employment for a long time; please speak your minds fully on this, so as to test your discernment in knowing men.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
問樂以象成其來尚矣古六代皆有樂非
徒作也至韶武而盛傳何與韶武傳于
何時絶于何時亦可得而言與樂起于
聲成于音束于律呂一也乃聲有倍半
音有和謬律有三始七始之别調有六
十八十四之殊果何說與或謂徑象有
同于易納音有符于曆然與否與五音
備而成樂周禮大祭獨無商音律止十
二以象月也乃議者至取增十六者以
===
===
爲當土圭之法所以辨方正位也乃布
律候氣者必稍偏而後應抑又何與宋
儒謂元聲難測欲多截管以候黃鐘亦
有據焉否與黃鐘之實歷十二辰而後
備是矣乃約十爲九而法至不可行陽
律下生陰律上生固也而說者又謂蕤
賓以後陽反上生陰反下生果何當與
黃鐘之長積分至八十一所從來久矣
乃說者又謂三寸九分以爲清聲抑可
punctuated: 問：樂以象成，其來尚矣。古六代皆有樂，非徒作也，至《韶》、《武》而盛傳，何與？《韶》、《武》傳于何時？絶于何時？亦可得而言與？樂起于聲，成于音，束于律呂，一也；乃聲有倍半，音有和謬，律有三始、七始之别，調有六十、八十四之殊，果何說與？或謂徑象有同于《易》，納音有符于曆，然與否與？五音備而成樂，《周禮》大祭獨無商音；律止十二以象月也，乃議者至取增十六者以爲當；土圭之法，所以辨方正位也，乃布律候氣者必稍偏而後應，抑又何與？宋儒謂元聲難測，欲多截管以候黃鐘，亦有據焉否與？黃鐘之實，歷十二辰而後備，是矣；乃約十爲九，而法至不可行。陽律下生，陰律上生，固也；而說者又謂蕤賓以後，陽反上生，陰反下生，果何當與？黃鐘之長，積分至八十一，所從來久矣；乃說者又謂三寸九分以爲清聲，抑可
translation_en: Question: Music serves to symbolize completed achievement; its origins reach back to antiquity. All six dynasties of antiquity had their music, which was not created in vain—yet why is it that when we come to the Shao and the Wu, they were so widely transmitted? At what time were the Shao and the Wu transmitted, and at what time did they die out? Can this also be spoken of? Music arises from sound (sheng), is formed in tone (yin), and is regulated by the yang and yin pitch-standards (lülü)—all this is one. Yet sounds have doubled and halved lengths, tones have harmony and discord (hemiu), pitch-standards have the distinction between the Three Beginnings and the Seven Beginnings, and modes have the difference between sixty and eighty-four—what is the explanation for all this? Some say that the diameter-figures correspond to the Book of Changes (Yi), and that the nayin (induced tones) tally with the calendar—is this so or not? Only when the five tones are complete is music formed, yet in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) great sacrifices alone omit the shang tone; the pitch-standards stop at twelve to symbolize the months, yet some discussants go so far as to take the addition to sixteen as proper; the method of the jade sundial-template (tugui) is the means of distinguishing directions and rectifying positions, yet those who set out pitch-pipes to watch for the seasonal ethers (houqi) must angle them slightly askew before they respond—why is all this so? Song-dynasty scholars held that the primordial sound (yuansheng) is difficult to measure, and wished to cut many pipes in order to watch for the Yellow Bell (Huangzhong) pitch—was there any basis for this or not? That the numerical substance of the Yellow Bell becomes complete only after passing through the twelve earthly branches is indeed right; yet if one reduces ten to nine, the method becomes unworkable. That yang pitch-standards generate downward (xiasheng) and yin pitch-standards generate upward (shangsheng) is established; yet commentators also say that from Ruibin onward, yang conversely generates upward and yin conversely generates downward—what is right in this? That the length of the Yellow Bell accumulates fractions to eighty-one is of long standing; yet commentators also speak of three cun and nine fen as the clear sound (qingsheng)—can this also be…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
解與
聖朝積德久矣大樂宜興願相與講明之以爲
考古者地
問士人習尚上翼王教下表民風所繋非
眇小也揚子稱周士貴秦士賤以爲士
之貴賤惟時所遷其果然與成周之制
自三物教民而賓興之至於論定而官
之後又有以詔廢置而致誅賞相見之
際非擯紹持贄則不得通何詳也一時
===
髦士斂容戢武於法制教令之中視秦
時縱横捭闔之徒桀驁横恣其氣焰傾
於人主此何貴何賤與豈其貴賤固有
所在與兩漢之興士靡不以功業節義
爭相策勵洎其末路浸淫敗壞莫可挽
回或以諂佞成風或以抗激取錮說者
謂皆剏業二君所由作也何前後之相
盭與豈鄒軻氏所稱豪傑之興不待文
王非與方今
punctuated:
解與？聖朝積德久矣，大樂宜興，願相與講明之，以爲考古者地。

問：士人習尚，上翼王教，下表民風，所繋非眇小也。揚子稱周士貴、秦士賤，以爲士之貴賤惟時所遷，其果然與？成周之制，自三物教民而賓興之，至於論定而官之後，又有以詔廢置而致誅賞；相見之際，非擯紹持贄則不得通，何詳也！一時髦士，斂容戢武於法制教令之中，視秦時縱横捭闔之徒，桀驁横恣，其氣焰傾於人主，此何貴何賤與？豈其貴賤固有所所在與？兩漢之興，士靡不以功業節義爭相策勵；洎其末路，浸淫敗壞，莫可挽回，或以諂佞成風，或以抗激取錮。說者謂皆剏業二君所由作也，何前後之相盭與？豈鄒軻氏所稱「豪傑之興，不待文王」非與？方今
translation_en:
…be explained? Our Sacred Dynasty has accumulated virtue for a long time, and great music ought to flourish. I wish to discuss and clarify these matters together with you, so as to lay a foundation for those who investigate antiquity.

Question: The habits and ethos of literati above support royal instruction and below exemplify popular customs; what depends on them is by no means trivial. Master Yang [Yang Xiong 楊雄] stated that the scholars of Zhou were noble whereas the scholars of Qin were base, holding that the nobility or baseness of scholars merely shifts with the times. Is this truly so? In the institutions of Complete Zhou, from teaching the people with the "three things" and recommending them as honored guests, up to appointing them to office after evaluation had been settled, there were furthermore measures to proclaim dismissal or retention and to mete out punishment or reward. On occasions of audience and meeting, without ceremonial assistants, introducers, and the presentation of gifts, communication could not take place—how detailed this was! Theoutstanding scholars of the age composed their countenance and restrained their steps within the bounds of laws, institutions, instructions, and ordinances. Compared with the practitioners of vertical and horizontal alliances and rhetorical manipulation in the Qin era—who were unruly, arrogant, and unrestrained, their bluster overshadowing even the ruler of men—which of these was noble and which was base? Or did their nobility and baseness indeed lie in something else? With the rise of the Two Han dynasties, there were no scholars who did not vie to spur themselves on through meritorious achievement and righteous integrity. Yet by the end of their courses, they became gradually corrupted and ruined beyond recovery: some formed a prevailing custom of flattery and sycophancy, while others courted proscription through defiant extremism. Commentators say that both resulted from what the two founding monarchs initiated. Why were the earlier and later phases so contradictory to one another? Could it be that what Meng Ke of Zou [Mencius 孟子] called "outstanding heroes rising up even without a King Wen" is untrue? At present…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
主聖時清澤流化布而爲之士者尚未知其爲
周爲秦爲兩漢也玆欲一道德同風俗
周人之制儻可行於今否抑别有道與
故蘄與諸士考衷焉
問天下不可一日而無法捐法而求治猶
涉江河而亡維楫鮮有濟矣迺入關而
約法三章克長安而約法十二條至簡
略也而卒爲二代基治之主何歟懸告
姦之格定減爵之令法至詳矣而竟兆
===
危亡之禍抑又何歟世儒拘於法而不
獲自適至舉聖人之法而力詆之有謂
焚符破璽而民朴鄙剖斗折衡而民不
爭殫殘天下之聖法而後可與論議者
有謂民知書而德衰知數而厚衰知券
契而信衰知機械而實衰者語至拂經
也豈亦有激而言之歟
明自
二祖開基
punctuated:
主聖時清，澤流化布，而爲之士者，尚未知其爲周、爲秦、爲兩漢也。玆欲一道德，同風俗，周人之制儻可行於今否？抑别有道與？故蘄與諸士考衷焉。
問：天下不可一日而無法。捐法而求治，猶涉江河而亡維楫，鮮有濟矣。迺入關而約法三章，克長安而約法十二條，至簡略也，而卒爲二代基治之主，何歟？懸告姦之格，定減爵之令，法至詳矣，而竟兆危亡之禍，抑又何歟？世儒拘於法而不獲自適，至舉聖人之法而力詆之。有謂「焚符破璽而民朴鄙，剖斗折衡而民不爭，殫殘天下之聖法而後可與論議」者；有謂「民知書而德衰，知數而厚衰，知券契而信衰，知機械而實衰」者，語至拂經也，豈亦有激而言之歟？明自二祖開基，
translation_en:
… the sovereign is sage and the era is pure, beneficence flows and transforming influence spreads, yet as for those who serve as its scholars, we still do not know whether they are like those of the Zhou, the Qin, or the Two Han dynasties. Now, if we wish to unify morality and make customs uniform, could the institutions of the men of Zhou perhaps be put into practice today? Or is there another way? Therefore I seek to examine the inner truth of this with you gentlemen.

Question: The realm cannot go a single day without laws. To cast aside laws and seek good governance is like crossing rivers and streams without ropes and oars—seldom will one succeed! Yet upon entering the Pass, a covenant of laws in three articles was made, and upon capturing Chang'an, a covenant of laws in twelve articles was made. These were rudimentary in the extreme, and yet their makers ultimately became the rulers who laid the foundations of governance for two dynasties—why is this? Posting regulations for denouncing villainy and establishing ordinances for reducing ranks of nobility—such laws were detailed in the extreme, and yet they ultimately presaged the disaster of peril and ruin—why is this, moreover? Mundane scholars feel fettered by laws and cannot find ease for themselves, to the point of taking up the laws of the sages and forcefully slandering them. There is one who says, "Burn the tallies and shatter the seals, and the people will be simple and unadorned; split the peck-measures and snap the steelyards, and the people will not contend; only when the sage laws of the realm have been utterly destroyed can one begin to discuss and deliberate with them." And there is one who says, "When the people know writing, virtue declines; when they know calculation, generosity declines; when they know deeds and contracts, trustworthiness declines; when they know mechanical contrivances, sincerity declines." Such words are contrary to the constant norms in the extreme—could it be that they too were spoken out of provocation?

Since the Ming’s Two Ancestors founded the dynastic enterprise, …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
列聖繼統二百年來
德澤深厚法立而不用至我
皇上端拱而朝萬國垂十禩矣而
威日旁暢論者謂宜養以寬大俾
國家之元氣益實亦自有見歟諸生行持文
墨議論幸熟計之務以質對
punctuated: 列聖繼統，二百年來，德澤深厚，法立而不用。至我皇上端拱而朝萬國，垂十禩矣，而威日旁暢。論者謂宜養以寬大，俾國家之元氣益實，亦自有見歟？諸生行持文墨議論，幸熟計之，務以質對。
translation_en: …and the successive sage emperors have carried on the imperial line; for two hundred years, their virtuous beneficence has been deep and generous, and laws have been established without having to be invoked. Coming down to our present Sovereign, he has sat upright with folded hands while receiving the homage of the myriad states for nearly ten years now, and his august authority spreads ever more widely day by day. Commentators suggest that it would be fitting to nurture the realm through leniency and magnanimity, so that the vital energy of the state may become ever more substantial—do they too have a valid insight of their own? You students will soon take up brush and ink to engage in policy discussions; please consider these matters thoroughly, and be sure to reply with substance.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人九十名
第一名姜鏡紹興府學生書
第二名李繼韶縉雲縣學生禮記
第三名祝以忠海寧縣學生易
第四名葉秉敬西安縣學增廣生詩
第五名方學龍淳安縣學生春秋
第六名陳治則紹興府學生禮記
第七名陳典學平陽縣學增廣生易
===
第八名施夢麟黃巖縣學生春秋
第九名祝以豳海寧縣學生易
第十名陶志高紹興府學附學生詩
第十一名孫懋昭湖州府學生書

第十五名張應宿平湖縣學生書
第十六名錢士鰲錢塘縣學附學生易
punctuated:
中式舉人九十名：

第一名，姜鏡，紹興府學生，《書》。

第八名，施夢麟，黃巖縣學生，《春秋》。
第九名，祝以豳，海寧縣學生，《易》。
第十名，陶志高，紹興府學附學生，《詩》。
第十一名，孫懋昭，湖州府學生，《書》。
第十二名，劉佳，山陰縣學附學生，《易》。
第十三名，陳于王，嘉善縣學附學生，《詩》。
第十四名，吳道光，紹興府學附學生，《易》。

第十六名，錢士鰲，錢塘縣學附學生，《易》。
translation_en:
Ninety Successful Provincial Graduates (juren):

First place: Jiang Jing 姜鏡, a student of the Shaoxing Prefectural School, specializing in the Book of Documents (Shu).
Second place: Li Jishao 李繼韶, a student of the Jinyun County School, specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji).
Third place: Zhu Yizhong 祝以忠, a student of the Haining County School, specializing in the Book of Changes (Yi).
Fourth place: Ye Bingjing 葉秉敬, anadded-quota student (zengguang sheng) of the Xi'an County School, specializing in the Book of Odes (Shi).
Fifth place: Fang Xuelong 方學龍, a student of the Chun'an County School, specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu).
Sixth place: Chen Zhize 陳治則, a student of the Shaoxing Prefectural School, specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji).
Seventh place: Chen Dianxue 陳典學, an added-quota student (zengguang sheng) of the Pingyang County School, specializing in the Book of Changes (Yi).

text:
第壹場
四書
康誥曰如保赤子心誠求之雖不中不遠
矣未有學養子而后嫁者也
祝以忠
同考試官訓導張批詞理燦然情境俱見保
民者不當如是耶
同考試官教諭區批精深瑩徹無纎毫麤𡝤
錄以式
===
考試官教諭程批聘雅不浮
考試官教諭周批說題意懇切
傳者引言慈出于性立教之本可識矣蓋保赤
子之心天性也觀於書而以慈立教者其亦求
端于性乎傳者釋齊治意謂家國異勢矣而教
之所以相通者固以其理之一然其機亦自有
所不容强者試以慈觀之康誥曰如保赤子夫
保赤子母道也曰如保赤子君道也保赤子者
如何蓋赤子有欲無言者也惟有欲則遂其欲
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

《康誥》曰：「如保赤子。」心誠求之，雖不中，不遠矣。未有學養子而后嫁者也。

祝以忠

傳者引言慈出于性，立教之本可識矣。蓋保赤子之心，天性也；觀於《書》而以慈立教者，其亦求端于性乎！傳者釋齊治，意謂：家、國異勢矣，而教之所以相通者，固以其理之一；然其機亦自有所不容强者，試以慈觀之。《康誥》曰：「如保赤子。」夫保赤子，母道也；曰「如保赤子」，君道也。保赤子者如何？蓋赤子，有欲無言者也。惟有欲，則遂其欲…
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Announcement to Kang (Kang gao) says: "Act as if you were protecting an infant." If the heart sincerely seeks its needs, even if it does not hit the mark exactly, it will not be far off. There has never been a girl who learned to raise a child and only afterward married.

Zhu Yizhong 祝以忠
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang 張: The diction and reasoning are brilliant, and both sentiment and circumstance are vividly revealed. Should not one who protects the people act just like this?
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Ou 區: Profound and pellucid, without the slightest crudeness or vulgarity. Selected to serve as a model.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng 程: Galloping elegance [? 聘雅, likely for 典雅 or 博雅] without superficiality.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhou 周: Expounds the meaning of the topic with earnest sincerity.

The commentator quotes words showing that parental kindness springs from human nature, whereby the foundation of establishing instruction may be known. Indeed, the heart that protects an infant is heavenly nature; looking at the Book of Documents (Shu), should not one who establishes instruction through kindness also seek its beginning in human nature? In explaining the regulation of the family and the governance of the state, the commentator meant to say: Family and state differ in their circumstances, and the reason instruction communicates between them is assuredly because their principle is one; yet its inner mechanism also naturally has that which cannot be forced—let us examine this through parental kindness. The Announcement to Kang says: "Act as if you were protecting an infant." Now, protecting an infant is the way of a mother; saying "as if you were protecting an infant" is the way of a ruler. How does one who protects an infant act? Indeed, an infant has desires but lacks speech. Because it has desires, fulfilling its desires…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者必待于求惟無言則求其欲者未易以中故
爲之母者體其方萌之欲而乂察其必至之情
以心求之者此誠也而意念相孚有不求求斯
中矣探其欲之不獲遂而只通其意於不能言
以誠求之者此心也而氣機相感雖不中亦不
遠矣此其鞠育之愛根於性之所自來而天不
容僞顧復之恩本於情之所自致而機不容強
其求也母何心焉以天通之不期誠而自誠其
中也子何心焉以天合之不期中而自中是誠
===
保之于母而若有不得以自與者豈有學養子
而后嫁者哉吁母非子也心誠求之可保其子
則君非民也心誠求之可保其民此康誥意也
觀於慈而孝弟可類推矣吾獨怪世之爲慈母
者衆而保民之主不多見焉豈母之求子以已
求之而君民尚有一體之間與保民者能以慈
母爲心則聯天下爲一身而民又何有不得其
情者故古先聖王曰恫瘝曰如傷誠以一體視
之也而民咸愛之如父母有以哉欲保民者可
punctuated: 者必待于求；惟無言，則求其欲者未易以中。故爲之母者，體其方萌之欲，而乂察其必至之情。以心求之者，此誠也；而意念相孚，有不求，求斯中矣。探其欲之不獲遂，而只通其意於不能言。以誠求之者，此心也；而氣機相感，雖不中，亦不遠矣。此其鞠育之愛，根於性之所自來，而天不容僞；顧復之恩，本於情之所自致，而機不容強。其求也，母何心焉？以天通之，不期誠而自誠；其中也，子何心焉？以天合之，不期中而自中。是誠保之于母，而若有不得以自與者，豈有學養子而后嫁者哉！吁！母非子也，心誠求之，可保其子；則君非民也，心誠求之，可保其民，此《康誥》意也。觀於慈，而孝弟可類推矣。吾獨怪世之爲慈母者衆，而保民之主不多見焉。豈母之求子以已求之，而君民尚有一體之間與？保民者能以慈母爲心，則聯天下爲一身，而民又何有不得其情者？故古先聖王曰「恫瘝」，曰「如傷」，誠以一體視之也，而民咸愛之如父母，有以哉！欲保民者，可
translation_en:
… [satisfying those desires] must depend on seeking to understand them; yet only because the infant cannot speak is it not easy for one who seeks to understand its desires to hit the mark. Therefore, one who is its mother sympathetically understands its newly sprouting desires and also examines its inevitable feelings. Seeking them with the mind—this is sincerity; and when thoughts and intentions are in mutual accord, if one seeks at all, the seeking hits the mark. She probes the desires that have not yet been satisfied, and simply communicates with its intentions where it cannot speak. Seeking them with sincerity—this is the mind; and when vital impulses mutually respond, even if she does not hit the mark, she will not be far off.

This love of nurturing and rearing is rooted in what arises naturally from human nature, where Heaven admits no falsity; the kindness of looking after and protecting is based on what comes naturally from feelings, where the vital mechanism admits no forcing. In her seeking, what deliberate mind does the mother have? Communicating through Heaven, she does not expect to be sincere and yet is naturally sincere. In her hitting the mark, what deliberate mind does the child have? Joined through Heaven, it does not expect the mark to be hit and yet it is naturally hit. Thus, protecting the child truly lies with the mother, yet it is as if she herself has no deliberate part in it—how could there ever be anyone who learns to raise a child first and only marries afterward!

Ah! The mother is not the child, yet if in her mind she sincerely seeks its desires, she can protect her child; so too, the ruler is not the people, yet if in his mind he sincerely seeks their desires, he can protect his people. This is the meaning of the "Announcement to Kang" (Kang gao). Looking at parental kindness, filial piety and fraternal respect can be inferred by analogy.

I only find it strange that in the world those who are kind mothers are many, while rulers who protect the people are rarely seen. Could it be that a mother seeks her child's desires as though seeking her own, whereas between ruler and people there still remains a barrier to being one body? If one who protects the people can take the mind of a kind mother as his own mind, he will unite the whole world into a single body—and how then could the people ever fail to have their true condition understood? Therefore, when the ancient sage-kings spoke of "sickness and pain in one's own body" and of tending the people "as if tending a wound," they truly regarded them as one body; and that the people all loved them like parents was indeed for good reason! Those who wish to protect the people may…

進取狷者有所不爲也
姜鏡

聖人思中行之次而重志節之士焉夫狂以志
===
勝狷以節勝得若人而可進於中矣聖人能無
思哉夫子蓋曰道之所以傳者人也人之所以
傳道者中也得中行而與之非吾之願哉而今
不可得矣然天下有任道之人而後有傳道之
人中行而下必也其狂狷乎蓋謹厚之士若近
於中而委靡因循無以勝斯道之重狂狷之士
若遠於中而慷慨獨立實具夫進道之資道本
高明而狂者之志常以高明自待卽上古之事
世之所視以爲難能者而彼獨以身當之也覬
punctuated:
以鍳矣。

子曰：「不得中行而與之，必也狂狷乎！狂者進取，狷者有所不爲也。」

姜鏡

考試官教諭程批：命意精切，措詞嚴整。

聖人思中行之次，而重志節之士焉。夫狂以志勝，狷以節勝，得若人而可進於中矣，聖人能無思哉？夫子蓋曰：道之所以傳者，人也；人之所以傳道者，中也。得中行而與之，非吾之願哉？而今不可得矣。然天下有任道之人，而後有傳道之人。中行而下，必也其狂狷乎！蓋謹厚之士，若近於中，而委靡因循，無以勝斯道之重；狂狷之士，若遠於中，而慷慨獨立，實具夫進道之資。道本高明，而狂者之志，常以高明自待。卽上古之事，世之所視以爲難能者，而彼獨以身當之也。覬
translation_en:
… take this as a mirror.

The Master said: "Having failed to find those who walk the middle way with whom to associate, I must turn to the ardently ambitious and the fastidiously cautious! The ardently ambitious press forward to seize what they seek, while the fastidiously cautious have things they refuse to do."

Jiang Jing 姜鏡

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Long 龍: "Stripping away hackneyed expressions and exercising original craftsmanship, it deeply captures the Sage's intent in turning his thoughts to the ardently ambitious and the fastidiously cautious."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng 程: "The conception is precise and incisive; the diction is rigorous and well-ordered."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhou 周: "Pure, orthodox, and refined."

The Sage, pondering those next best to the followers of the middle way, places weight upon men of aspiration and integrity. Now, the ardently ambitious excel in aspiration, and the fastidiously cautious excel in integrity; if one obtains such men, they can be guided to advance toward the middle way—how could the Sage not turn his thoughts to them?

What the Master meant was to say: That by which the Way is transmitted is men; that by which men transmit the Way is the middle way. To find those who walk the middle way and associate with them—is this not my wish? Yet today they cannot be found. Still, in the world there must first be men who take up the burden of the Way before there can be men who transmit the Way. Below those who walk the middle way, it must surely be the ardently ambitious and the fastidiously cautious!

For men who are merely cautious and agreeable seem close to the middle way, yet being dispirited and bound by routine, they lack the wherewithal to bear the weight of this Way; whereas men who are ardently ambitious or fastidiously cautious seem far from the middle way, yet being high-spirited and independent, they truly possess the endowments to advance in the Way.

The Way is inherently lofty and brilliant, and the aspiration of the ardently ambitious always holds itself to a lofty and brilliant standard. Even regarding the deeds of high antiquity, which the world regards as difficult to achieve, he alone takes them upon himself in person. Observing [?] …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其志而知若人之可以任道巳道本正大而狷
者之節常以正大自持即流俗之行世之溺焉
而不自知者而彼獨不以身徇之也觀其節而
知若人之可以任道巳蓋自今日之所就而言
則立志太高持守太激固不可以列於中行也
自他日之所養而言則行可副志才可達節亦
未始不可進於中行也然則吾之與狂狷也豈
與其終於狂狷哉噫觀聖人之所思而知其所
重者有在矣大抵狂狷之人常足濟天下事狂
===
者切直不諱故有所必爲而非喜事狷者獨立
不隨故有所不爲而非畏事彼其不眩利害不
動榮辱者其中先定也故聖學不可無狂狷之
士而世道不可不任狂狷之人
徐子曰仲尼亟稱於水曰水哉水哉何取
於水也孟子曰原泉混混不舍晝夜盈
科而後進放乎四海有本者如是是之
取爾苟爲無本七八月之間雨集溝澮
皆盈其涸也可立而待也故聲聞過情
punctuated:
其志，而知若人之可以任道巳。道本正大，而狷者之節常以正大自持，即流俗之行，世之溺焉而不自知者，而彼獨不以身徇之也。觀其節，而知若人之可以任道巳。蓋自今日之所就而言，則立志太高、持守太激，固不可以列於中行也；自他日之所養而言，則行可副志、才可達節，亦未始不可進於中行也。然則吾之與狂狷也，豈與其終於狂狷哉？噫！觀聖人之所思，而知其所重者有在矣。大抵狂狷之人，常足濟天下事。狂者切直不諱，故有所必爲，而非喜事；狷者獨立不隨，故有所不爲，而非畏事。彼其不眩利害、不動榮辱者，其中先定也。故聖學不可無狂狷之士，而世道不可不任狂狷之人。
徐子曰：「仲尼亟稱於水，曰：『水哉，水哉！』何取於水也？」孟子曰：「原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。苟爲無本，七八月之間雨集，溝澮皆盈；其涸也，可立而待也。故聲聞過情，
translation_en:
… observing [?] their aspirations, one knows that such men are indeed capable of shouldering the Way. The Way is fundamentally upright and great, and the integrity of the scrupulous (juan) constantly upholds itself with uprightness and greatness; even when it comes to the practices of vulgar custom, in which the world drowns without realizing it, they alone refuse to sacrifice themselves to follow them. Observing their integrity, one knows that such men are indeed capable of shouldering the Way. Speaking from what they have achieved today, their aspirations are set too high and their self-restraint is too extreme, so of course they cannot be ranked among those of the Mean in action; yet speaking from what they will cultivate in the future, their conduct can match their aspirations and their talent can fulfill their integrity, so it is by no means impossible for them to advance to the Mean in action. This being so, when I associate with the ardently ambitious and the scrupulous, am I approving of their remaining merely ambitious and scrupulous to the end? Alas! Observing what the Sage longed for, we know where his emphasis lay. Generally speaking, ambitious and scrupulous men are always sufficient to accomplish the affairs of the world. The ambitious are forthright and outspoken without evasion, so there are things they are determined to do, yet not out of a fondness for meddling; the scrupulous stand alone without following the crowd, so there are things they refuse to do, yet not out of a fear of trouble. That they are not dazzled by advantage and harm, nor moved by honor and disgrace, is because their inner resolve is settled beforehand. Therefore, Sacred Learning cannot be without ambitious and scrupulous scholars, and the way of the world cannot fail to employ ambitious and scrupulous men.

Master Xu said, "Confucius frequently praised water, saying, 'Water, O water!' What did he find to approve of in water?" Mencius replied, "Water from a spring gushes forth, never ceasing day or night; it fills up every hollow before advancing, and goes on until it reaches the four seas. What has a source is like this, and it was simply this that he approved of. Suppose it has no source: in the seventh and eighth months when the rains gather, the ditches and channels are all filled; yet their drying up may be expected as one stands and waits. Therefore, having a reputation that exceeds the reality…

Ye Bingjing 葉秉敬

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Chen 陳: With well-forged phrasing, he expresses deeply reflective thoughts. How earnestly has he articulated the sage's intent in approving of water! Those who read this essay will perceive its depth.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen 陳: The exposition is concise and clean, the train of thought refined and harmonious—truly one skilled in the contemporary examination essay (shiyi).

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng 程: Concise in wording and comprehensive in principle.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhou 周: Balanced, proper, and fluent.

The great worthy [Mencius] elucidates how the sage [Confucius] valued the fundamental source, and deeply warns people against chasing after reputation. Now in learning, what is prized is having a fundamental source, not seeking nearness to fame. By observing the fundamental source in what the sage approved of in water, one knows that lacking a fundamental source is truly worthy of shame. Moreover, the Way of the sage reveres the fundamental source and rejects hollow reputation, whereas the learning of a degenerate age pursues empty fame and is sparse in substantive conduct. Thus the sigh of “O water!” was how the Master lodged his thought of revering the fundamental source, yet Master Xu (Xuzi 徐子) did not recognize it. Mencius told him: Do you know the reason why Zhongni 仲尼 [Confucius] approved of water? The water that Zhongni approved of was the water of a gushing spring with a source. It moves day and night, advances after filling every hollow, and reaches to the Four Seas—so far-reaching is its flow! And the reason why it does not cease, why it fills every hollow, and why it reaches the seas is because its source is deep. title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
易盈易涸而其終不繼仲尼奚取焉吾以是知
君子之學其敦本尚行而與聲名相孚者此原
泉之水也固君子之所重也其釣名干譽而與
本原相違者此易涸之水也尤君子之所恥也
是故君子寧效混混之泉無爲暴集之雨寧效
放海之流無爲溝澮之盈何者實德可久而虛
名鮮終也通乎此者庶無負仲尼取水之意乎

以光大也九三无平不陂无往不復艱
punctuated:
易盈易涸，而其終不繼，仲尼奚取焉？吾以是知君子之學，其敦本尚行而與聲名相孚者，此原泉之水也，固君子之所重也；其釣名干譽而與本原相違者，此易涸之水也，尤君子之所恥也。是故君子寧效混混之泉，無爲暴集之雨；寧效放海之流，無爲溝澮之盈。何者？實德可久，而虛名鮮終也。通乎此者，庶無負仲尼取水之意乎！大抵務本之學，莫先漸進。是故宇宙內事，卽放海之流也；身心本原，卽盈科之始也。古之君子，潛伏屋漏，不蘄近名，遠邇卑高，不蘄速效，凡以頓悟之功，不如循序之爲得耳。孟子稱仲尼之道，至於觀海難水，而歸於不盈科不行，其深知聖人哉！

「初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。《象》曰：拔茅征吉，志在外也。九二，包荒，用馮河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。《象》曰：包荒，得尚于中行，以光大也。九三，无平不陂，无往不復，艱
translation_en:
… easily fills and easily dries up, so that in the end it cannot continue—what would Zhongni [Confucius] find to approve in that? From this I know that in the learning of the superior man, that which cultivates the root, prizes practice, and corresponds truly with reputation and fame is the water of a spring with a source, and is certainly what the superior man values; whereas that which fishes for a name, seeks after praise, and goes against the fundamental source is water that easily dries up, and is especially what the superior man is ashamed of. Therefore, the superior man would rather emulate the gushing spring than be the suddenly gathered rain; he would rather emulate the current that reaches the sea than be the overflowing of ditches and drains. Why is this? Because genuine virtue can endure, whereas empty fame rarely lasts to the end. One who thoroughly understands this will perhaps not fail to live up to the meaning of Zhongni's approval of water! In general, in learning that attends to the fundamental, nothing comes before gradual advancement. Therefore, the affairs within the universe are like the current that reaches the sea, while the fundamental source in body and mind is like the beginning of filling up the hollows. When the superior men of antiquity cultivated themselves in the seclusion of their private chambers, they did not seek immediate fame; in proceeding from near to far and from low to high, they did not seek quick results—all because the effort of sudden enlightenment is not as sound as following the proper sequence. When Mencius praised the Way of Zhongni, speaking of how having seen the sea makes it difficult to think much of other waters, and concluding with how water does not proceed without filling up the hollows, how deeply he understood the Sage!

Book of Changes (Yijing)

"Nine at the beginning: Pulling up thatch grass with its entangled roots, each according to its kind. Going forward brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: 'Pulling up thatch grass, going forward brings good fortune'—his ambition lies outside. Nine in the second place: Embracing the uncultivated, crossing the river without a boat, not neglecting what is distant, casting off factional friends, one succeeds in matching the central course. The Commentary on the Images says: 'Embracing the uncultivated, one succeeds in matching the central course'—because his illumination and greatness are vast. title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
貞无咎勿恤其孚于食有福象曰无往
不復天地際也
陳典學
同考試官訓導張批清灑脫塵冲和合度論
斯文也宛然有泰寧氣象
同考試官教諭區批發揮輔泰保泰之意纍
纍若貫珠此蓋有志於鳴世者
考試官教諭程批布格修整而意更躍如
考試官教諭周批莊嚴塗架
===
觀泰之三爻而知君子之關於世道也夫治世
不可無君子也三陽協心以保泰而世道終賴
之矣且古之賢人每思效于盛世而古之盛世
亦有賴於賢人二者常相待也茲泰之時三陽
並進是則豪傑之士濟濟然共奮於明時而先
憂之思師師焉同心於王室故曰拔茅征吉幸
其進也曰志在外原其心也然君子進矣而維
世道者將何如哉吾知時至於泰則人情之玩
愒易生而所以合人情而劑量之者以中行之
punctuated:
貞，无咎；勿恤其孚，于食有福。象曰：无往不復，天地際也。
陳典學
同考試官訓導張批：清灑脫塵，冲和合度。論斯文也，宛然有泰寧氣象。
同考試官教諭區批：發揮輔泰、保泰之意，纍纍若貫珠，此蓋有志於鳴世者。
考試官教諭程批：布格修整，而意更躍如。
考試官教諭周批：莊嚴塗架。
觀泰之三爻，而知君子之關於世道也。夫治世不可無君子也，三陽協心以保泰，而世道終賴之矣。且古之賢人，每思效于盛世，而古之盛世，亦有賴於賢人，二者常相待也。茲泰之時，三陽並進，是則豪傑之士，濟濟然共奮於明時；而先憂之思，師師焉同心於王室。故曰「拔茅征吉」，幸其進也；曰「志在外」，原其心也。然君子進矣，而維世道者將何如哉？吾知時至於泰，則人情之玩愒易生，而所以合人情而劑量之者，以中行之…
translation_en:
… [arduous] and constant, there will be no blame; do not worry about its trustworthiness, for in one's sustenance there will be blessing." The Commentary on the Images says: "'No going without a return'—this is the juncture of Heaven and Earth."

Chen Dianxue 陳典學

Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang 張 comments: Pure, brisk, and free of worldly dust; harmonious, moderate, and fitting in measure. To judge this essay, it truly possesses an aura of great peace and tranquility.
Associate Examiner Instructor Ou 區 comments: It elaborates the meaning of assisting and preserving Great Peace (Tai 泰) like a string of pearls; this is surely someone who aspires to make his mark in the world.
Examiner Instructor Cheng 程 comments: The structural layout is neat and well-ordered, and the meaning is even more vivid and alive.
Examiner Instructor Zhou 周 comments: Stately and dignified in its framework [?].

When we observe the three yang lines of the hexagram Tai (Peace), we understand how vital the noble man is to the Way of the world. Indeed, a well-governed age cannot be without noble men; when the three yang lines unite their hearts to preserve peace, the Way of the world ultimately depends on them. Moreover, the worthies of antiquity always thought of rendering service in a flourishing age, and the flourishing ages of antiquity likewise depended on worthies—the two always awaited each other. Now, at the time of Tai, the three yang lines advance together. This means that men of outstanding talent, in stately numbers, rouse themselves together in an enlightened age, and their thoughts of being the first to worry [about the world's troubles] are harmoniously united in devotion to the royal house. Therefore, the text says, "Pulling up the茅 [thatch] grass, advancing brings good fortune," rejoicing in their advancement; and it says, "The will is directed outward," tracing their intention to its source. Yet once the noble men have advanced, how will they uphold the Way of the world? I know that when the times reach a state of peace (Tai), human sentiments easily give rise to negligence and complacency, and that by which one brings human sentiments into harmony and tempers them is through the [Way of] central action…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道得也誠寬弘其量而濟以斷精詳其慮而運
以公自是而人情宜之矣何也有光大之心而
後有行中之事是九二保泰之志所以孚於初
也然時至於泰則天運之盛衰相仍而所以舉
天運而力回之者以豫防之道勝也誠主之以
艱而靡有逸志行之以貞而靡有過動自是而
天運佑之矣何也有方盛之戒而後無盛極之
衰是九三保泰之志所以孚於初也噫不有拔
茅之初誰其倡之不有中行之二艱貞之三誰
===
其維之信乎泰之係於君子矣雖然三陽者亦
特行願之君耳君心偏則柔而疑其阿剛而疑
其激君心弛則以長駕爲略以桑土爲迂何以
彙征而共濟哉故曰上下交而其志同斯志也
固所以行在外之志也已
師者衆也衆必有所比故受之以比
祝以豳
同考試官訓導張 批 運筆雄奇構思縝密而
結意不超出經生口吻
punctuated:
道得也。誠寬弘其量而濟以斷，精詳其慮而運以公，自是而人情宜之矣。何也？有光大之心，而後有行中之事，是九二保泰之志，所以孚於初也。然時至於泰，則天運之盛衰相仍，而所以舉天運而力回之者，以豫防之道勝也。誠主之以艱而靡有逸志，行之以貞而靡有過動，自是而天運佑之矣。何也？有方盛之戒，而後無盛極之衰，是九三保泰之志，所以孚於初也。噫！不有拔茅之初，誰其倡之？不有中行之二、艱貞之三，誰其維之？信乎泰之係於君子矣！雖然，三陽者，亦特行願之君耳。君心偏，則柔而疑其阿，剛而疑其激；君心弛，則以長駕爲略，以桑土爲迂，何以彙征而共濟哉？故曰：「上下交而其志同。」斯志也，固所以行「在外」之志也已。

師者，衆也；衆必有所比，故受之以比。
祝以豳
同考試官訓導張批：運筆雄奇，構思縝密，而結意不超出經生口吻……
translation_en:
… way of the mean is attained. If one is truly broad and magnanimous in capacity yet complements it with decisiveness, and is minute and thorough in deliberation yet exercises it with impartiality, then from this point on human sentiments will find it fitting. Why is this? Only when there is an illustrious and great mind can there be deeds that walk the mean; this is whereby the aspiration of the Nine in the Second place to preserve Peace (Tai) is in accord with the First place. Yet when the times reach Peace, the flourishing and decline of Heaven's course follow upon one another, and that whereby one takes up Heaven's course and strenuously turns it back is by prevailing through the way of precautionary prevention. If one truly governs it with a sense of difficulty and has no indolent intentions, and practices it with constancy and has no excessive actions, then from this point on Heaven's course will assist it. Why is this? Only when there is caution right at the height of flourishing will there be no decline from flourishing reaching its extreme; this is whereby the aspiration of the Nine in the Third place to preserve Peace is in accord with the First place. Ah! Without the First place pulling up the thatch-grass, who would initiate it? Without the Second place walking the mean and the Third place remaining constant in difficulty, who would maintain it? Truly, Peace depends upon the noble man! Even so, the three yang lines merely await a ruler who acts upon their wishes [reading 待 for 特]. If the ruler's mind is partial, then when they are gentle he will suspect them of flattery, and when they are firm he will suspect them of extremity; if the ruler's mind is lax, he will regard far-reaching mastery as mere scheming and precautions for the mulberry-soil as迂腐 (impractical pedantry)—how then could they advance together in a category and jointly bring about success? Therefore it is said: "Above and below commune and their aspirations are the same." This aspiration is indeed the means to carry out the aspiration that lies "outside."

"The Army (Shi) means the multitude; the multitude must have that to which they cleave, hence it is followed by Union (Bi)."
By Zhu Yibin 祝以豳.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭區批詞雄調逸而一統規模
盡洩於穎端矣錄之
考試官教諭程批宏博有奇氣
考試官教諭周批明練俊偉
觀師比相承而得大一統之義焉夫天下之衆
非得人以統之不可也此師之後所以有比與
且所貴乎統一宇内而總理人羣者何也懼天
下相聚而至於相賊也嘗於聖人之序師比得
其故焉師之爲言衆也蓋生人之初其勢均焉
===
耳天下之專猶可聽其自爲而不至於亂物聚
之後其情渙焉已天下之治豈可一无所統而
自底於安饑者欲食寒者欲衣貧者欲給必以
其欲求遂於王者王者起而有以遂其欲將不
召而衆歸往矣智者紿愚勇者脅弱衆者暴寡
必以其情求平於王者王者起而有以平其情
將不集而衆憑依矣蓋惟德可以服人而天生
王者與之以神聖顯懿之資即賢人能士皆在
其範圍而况此衆乎惟位可以率人而天生王
punctuated:
同考試官教諭區批：詞雄調逸，而一統規模盡洩於穎端矣，錄之。
考試官教諭程批：宏博有奇氣。
考試官教諭周批：明練俊偉。

觀《師》、《比》相承，而得大一統之義焉。夫天下之衆，非得人以統之不可也，此《師》之後所以有《比》與？且所貴乎統一宇内而總理人羣者，何也？懼天下相聚而至於相賊也。嘗於聖人之序《師》、《比》得其故焉。師之爲言衆也。蓋生人之初，其勢均焉耳，天下之專，猶可聽其自爲而不至於亂；物聚之後，其情渙焉已，天下之治，豈可一无所統而自底於安？饑者欲食，寒者欲衣，貧者欲給，必以其欲求遂於王者；王者起而有以遂其欲，將不召而衆歸往矣。智者紿愚，勇者脅弱，衆者暴寡，必以其情求平於王者；王者起而有以平其情，將不集而衆憑依矣。蓋惟德可以服人，而天生王者，與之以神聖顯懿之資，即賢人能士皆在其範圍，而况此衆乎？惟位可以率人，而天生王
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Ou 區 comments: The diction is vigorous and the tone transcendent, while the grand framework of unified rule pours forth completely from the tip of his brush. Record it for publication.
Examiner Instructor Cheng 程 comments: Broad and learned, with an extraordinary spirit.
Examiner Instructor Zhou 周 comments: Lucid, practiced, and magnificent.

By observing how the hexagrams Shi [The Army / Multitude] and Bi [Holding Together] succeed one another, one grasps the meaning of grand unification. Now, as for the multitude of the world, it simply will not do unless a person is found to unify them; is this not why Shi is followed by Bi? Moreover, why is it that unifying the realm and overseeing human society is held in such esteem? It is out of fear that when the people of the world gather together, they will end up harming one another. I have found the reason for this in the Sage's sequencing of Shi and Bi. The word "shi" means "multitude." In the beginning of human life, people's power was merely equal; the affairs [?] of the world could still be left to take their own course without descending into disorder. Once things gathered together, however, their inclinations became dispersed; how could the governance of the world have nothing at all to unify it and yet attain peace on its own? The hungry desire food, the cold desire clothing, and the poor desire sufficiency—they must seek the fulfillment of their desires from a true king. When a true king arises and has the means to fulfill their desires, the multitude will turn to him without being summoned. The clever deceive the foolish, the brave intimidate the weak, and the many tyrannize the few—they must seek the redressing of their grievances from a true king. When a true king arises and has the means to redress their grievances, the multitude will rely upon him without being assembled. Indeed, only virtue can win people's submission, and when Heaven gives birth to a true king, endowing him with divinely sagely and manifestly admirable qualities, even worthy men and capable scholars fall within his encompassment—how much more so this multitude! Only position can lead people, and when Heaven gives birth to a true king…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者畀之以崇高富貴之權卽公卿大夫皆惟其
驅使而况此衆乎故聖人於師之後受之以比
者是一人撫萬邦之義也是四海仰一人之義
也是天王大一統者也雖然天下之勢不有所
一則離而不有所分則紊蓋昔者周先王割天
下土地封建諸侯而歷年八百至秦時雖廢封
建哉然猶置郡邑長吏說者謂公天下之大端
大本也誠分之也比之為卦也有內比者有外
比者其意固若斯焉巳
===
書
曰后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民
敏德帝曰俞允若茲嘉言罔攸伏野無
遺賢萬邦咸寧稽于衆舍己從人不虐
無告不廢困窮惟帝時克
姜鏡
同考試官訓導龍批虞庭君臣克艱之心發
揮融透是深於書義者
考試官敎諭程批簡潔精密
punctuated:
者，畀之以崇高富貴之權，卽公卿大夫皆惟其驅使，而况此衆乎？故聖人於《師》之後受之以《比》者，是一人撫萬邦之義也，是四海仰一人之義也，是天王大一統者也。雖然，天下之勢不有所一則離，而不有所分則紊。蓋昔者周先王割天下土地，封建諸侯，而歷年八百；至秦時雖廢封建哉，然猶置郡邑長吏，說者謂公天下之大端大本也，誠分之也。《比》之為卦也，有內比者，有外比者，其意固若斯焉巳。

《書》：
「曰：『后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。』帝曰：『俞！允若茲，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。』」
姜鏡
同考試官訓導龍批：虞庭君臣克艱之心，發揮融透，是深於《書》義者。
考試官敎諭程批：簡潔精密。
translation_en:
… [when Heaven gives birth to a true king,] it endows him with the authority of exalted status, wealth, and honor; even the dukes, ministers, and grandees are all entirely at his command, how much more so this multitude! Therefore, that the sages followed the hexagram Shi (The Army) with Bi (Holding Together) signifies the principle of one man soothing the myriad states, the principle of the four seas looking up to one man, and the grand unity under the Heavenly King. Even so, in the dynamics of the realm, if there is no unification, things will fragment; yet if there is no division of responsibilities, things will fall into disorder. In antiquity, the former kings of Zhou parceled out the lands of the realm to enfeoff the feudal lords, and their dynasty endured for eight hundred years. When it came to the Qin dynasty, although feudal enfeoffment was abolished, they still established commanderies and counties with chief officials; commentators have called this the grand beginning and fundamental basis of treating the realm as public—truly because power was divided and delegated. In the hexagram Bi, there is "holding together within" and "holding together without"; its meaning is indeed just like this.

Book of Documents (Shu):
"[Yu] said: 'If the sovereign can realize the difficulty of his sovereignty, and the minister can realize the difficulty of his ministry, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will sedulously seek virtue.' The Emperor said: 'Yes! If it truly be so, good words will nowhere lie hidden, no worthy men will be left neglected in the wilds, and the myriad states will all enjoy repose. But to consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the distressed and impoverished—only the Emperor [Yao] was able to do this!'"

Jiang Jing 姜鏡.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Long comments: The mind of realizing difficulties shared by sovereign and minister in the court of Yu [Shun] is expounded with thoroughness and lucidity; this is someone deeply versed in the meaning of the Book of Documents.
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Cheng comments: Concise and precise.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭周批朗鬯之作
大臣陳克艱之謨而聖君極言其難能焉夫克
艱致治之本也禹陳謨于舜而舜歸美于堯其
皆克艱之心哉且明主不以世治弛儆哲臣不
以主聖忘規有虞之世舜紹堯而禹佐舜天下
既已治矣乃禹之心未已也故矢諸謨曰君臣
者庶政之紀而萬民之表也是必君致艱於上
而常廑保治之思臣致艱於下而勿忘輔治之
慮則以此理政百度其惟貞矣以此率民羣黎
===
其丕變矣爲我君若臣者奚可不克艱哉帝舜
聞其言而契於心也遂從而俞之曰誠哉汝禹
克艱之言乎果能此道矣豈特政乂民安已哉
由是嘉言則罔伏矣羣賢則無遺矣萬邦則咸
寧矣效如此乎大也而非可倖致也必其從善
則忘已焉無告則不虐焉困窮則不廢焉事如
此乎艱也而何可易能耶蓋惟帝堯無私順理
人已兩忘好士愛民而智仁兼盡是乃可謂
克艱云爾予承帝之統汝熙帝之載尚相與共
punctuated:
考試官教諭周批：朗鬯之作。
大臣陳克艱之謨，而聖君極言其難能焉。夫克艱，致治之本也。禹陳謨于舜，而舜歸美于堯，其皆克艱之心哉！且明主不以世治弛儆，哲臣不以主聖忘規。有虞之世，舜紹堯而禹佐舜，天下既已治矣，乃禹之心未已也。故矢諸謨曰：「君臣者，庶政之紀，而萬民之表也。是必君致艱於上，而常廑保治之思；臣致艱於下，而勿忘輔治之慮。則以此理政，百度其惟貞矣；以此率民，羣黎其丕變矣。爲我君若臣者，奚可不克艱哉！」帝舜聞其言而契於心也，遂從而俞之曰：「誠哉，汝禹克艱之言乎！果能此道矣，豈特政乂民安已哉？由是嘉言則罔伏矣，羣賢則無遺矣，萬邦則咸寧矣，效如此乎大也，而非可倖致也。必其從善則忘已焉，無告則不虐焉，困窮則不廢焉，事如此乎艱也，而何可易能耶？蓋惟帝堯無私順理，人已兩忘，好士愛民，而智仁兼盡，是乃可謂克艱云爾。予承帝之統，汝熙帝之載，尚相與共
translation_en:
Examiner Instructor Zhou comments: A lucid and fluent composition.

The great minister sets forth his counsel on recognizing the difficulty of one's office, and the sage ruler speaks to the utmost of how hard it is to achieve. Now, recognizing the difficulty of one's office is the foundation of bringing about good governance. When Yu set forth his counsel to Shun, and Shun attributed the glory to Yao, did both not stem from a mind that recognized the difficulty of their offices!

Moreover, an enlightened ruler does not relax his vigilance because the world is well-governed, and a wise minister does not forget his admonitions because his ruler is a sage. In the age of Yu [Shun], when Shun succeeded Yao and Yu assisted Shun, the world was already well-governed; yet Yu's mind was still not at rest. Therefore, he declared in his counsel: "Ruler and minister are the regulators of the myriad affairs of governance and the exemplars for the ten thousand people. Thus, the ruler above must attend to the difficulty of his task and constantly cherish thoughts of preserving good order; the minister below must attend to the difficulty of his task and never forget his concerns for assisting in governance. If we manage governance by this principle, then all measures will be upright; if we lead the people by this principle, then the multitudes will be greatly transformed. For us who are ruler and minister, how can we fail to recognize the difficulty of our offices!"

Emperor Shun heard his words and found that they tallied with his own mind. Thereupon he assented to them, saying: "True indeed are your words, O Yu, about recognizing the difficulty of one's office! If one can truly carry out this Way, will the result merely be that governance is ordered and the people are at peace? Through this, admirable words will never be concealed, the host of worthies will none of them be left neglected, and the myriad states will all enjoy tranquility. So great is the efficacy of this! Yet it cannot be attained by mere fortune. One must forget oneself when following the good, never oppress the helpless, and never abandon the distressed and impoverished. So difficult is the practice of this! How could it be easily achieved? Only Emperor Yao, who was selfless and compliant with principle, forgetting the distinction between others and himself, loving scholars and cherishing the people, and exhausting both wisdom and benevolence, can truly be said to have recognized the difficulty of his office. I have succeeded to the Emperor's line, and you make bright the Emperor's undertakings; let us together…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
圖之哉夫禹不有其治責之於舜舜不居其美
歸之於堯有虞君臣同一思艱如此其治所以
弗可及歟抑舜聖君也禹聖臣也當時之治亦
稱極盛矣猶然矢口儆戒常若不及焉此聖人
望治無已之心也乃若後世君臣治未底于小
康而遽陳豫大豐亨之說無惑治未幾而亂隨
之矣視舜禹用心何如
旌別淑慝表厥宅里彰善癉惡樹之風聲
弗率訓典殊厥井疆俾克畏慕申畫郊
===
圻慎固封守以康四海
孫懋昭
同考試官訓導龍 批 體裁整飭詞氣疏暢其
呼應過接處悉中肯綮非學識俱到者不能
考試官教諭程 批 典雅嚴重
考試官教諭周 批 醇正
賢王示大臣化民之政而復嚴其防焉夫化民
之政旌善別惡而已使防之不嚴亦何以安天
下哉康王命畢公者若曰我公之治東郊不惟
punctuated:
圖之哉！」夫禹不有其治，責之於舜；舜不居其美，歸之於堯。有虞君臣同一思艱如此，其治所以弗可及歟！抑舜，聖君也；禹，聖臣也。當時之治，亦稱極盛矣，猶然矢口儆戒，常若不及焉，此聖人望治無已之心也。乃若後世君臣，治未底于小康，而遽陳豫大豐亨之說，無惑治未幾而亂隨之矣。視舜、禹用心何如？

旌別淑慝，表厥宅里，彰善癉惡，樹之風聲。弗率訓典，殊厥井疆，俾克畏慕。申畫郊圻，慎固封守，以康四海。
孫懋昭

賢王示大臣化民之政，而復嚴其防焉。夫化民之政，旌善別惡而已；使防之不嚴，亦何以安天下哉？康王命畢公者若曰：我公之治東郊，不惟
translation_en:
…plan for it together!” Now, Yu did not claim credit for his governance, but placed the responsibility upon Shun; Shun did not dwell in his own excellence, but attributed it to Yao. That the sovereign and minister of the Youyu era shared the same mindfulness of difficulties in this manner—is this not why their governance could never be equaled? Moreover, Shun was a sage sovereign, and Yu was a sage minister. The governance of that time was already acclaimed as the height of flourishing, yet in their utterances they still admonished and cautioned one another, always as if falling short. This was the sages’ ceaseless heart in hoping for good governance. As for the sovereigns and ministers of later ages, before their governance has even reached modest prosperity, they hastily set forth doctrines of grand ease and abundant fortune; it is no wonder that before governance has lasted long, disorder follows upon it! How does that compare with the mindfulness of Shun and Yu?

“Distinguish the good and the evil, mark out their dwellings and neighborhoods, manifest the good and make the evil suffer, and establish the influence of their reputation. For those who do not follow the instructive canons, segregate their well-fields and boundaries, so that they may learn both fear and admiration. Clearly delineate the suburban borders, and carefully secure the frontier defenses, in order to give peace to all within the Four Seas.”
Sun Maozhao 孫懋昭
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Long 龍 comments: The structural form is neat and orderly, and the diction and vital flow are smooth and fluent. Its echoes and transitions all hit the crucial points; none without both learning and insight could achieve this.
Examiner, Instructor Cheng 程 comments: Classically elegant and grave.
Examiner, Instructor Zhou 周 comments: Pure and upright.

A worthy king shows his grand minister the governance for transforming the people, and furthermore tightens its defenses. Now, the governance for transforming the people consists simply of honoring the good and distinguishing the evil; yet if its defenses are not made strict, how can peace be brought to all under Heaven? What King Kang commanded the Duke of Bi was as if to say: In our Duke’s governance of the eastern suburbs, not only…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
商民視以勸懲而亦四海賴以安危者也則所
以為保釐之政者當何如哉蓋東都之民淑慝
不能無辨故今日之政旌別在所宜先其率訓
典而淑也則宅與里其表焉彰其善亦以癉其
惡也而風聲所樹有餘勸矣其不率訓典而慝
也則井與疆其殊焉使之畏亦以使之慕也而
鑒戒所昭有餘懲矣然勸懲之典固所以鼓人
心于不倦而防範之法又所以折姦萌於未形
郊圻嘗規畫矣能無歲久而湮乎則申明其制
===
===
而疆界之必正如封守嘗建置矣能無世平而
玩乎則戒嚴其守而備禦之益周也斯則體統
嚴而强梗默化非獨商民之見旌者有所恃而
四海熙然其乂安矣紀綱肅而窺伺潜消非獨
商民之見別者有所憚而四海帖然其寧謐矣
夫旌別之政行於東郊而保釐之效及於四海
則殷民所係誠大矣公其加之意哉抑論蕞爾
殷民化訓三紀宜無足為慮者而康王乃拳拳
于宅里井疆之辨郊圻封守之制以是見古帝
punctuated: 商民視以勸懲，而亦四海賴以安危者也，則所以為保釐之政者當何如哉？蓋東都之民，淑慝不能無辨，故今日之政，旌別在所宜先。其率訓典而淑也，則宅與里其表焉，彰其善亦以癉其惡也，而風聲所樹，有餘勸矣；其不率訓典而慝也，則井與疆其殊焉，使之畏亦以使之慕也，而鑒戒所昭，有餘懲矣。然勸懲之典，固所以鼓人心于不倦，而防範之法，又所以折姦萌於未形。郊圻嘗規畫矣，能無歲久而湮乎？則申明其制，而疆界之必正；如封守嘗建置矣，能無世平而玩乎？則戒嚴其守，而備禦之益周也。斯則體統嚴而强梗默化，非獨商民之見旌者有所恃，而四海熙然其乂安矣；紀綱肅而窺伺潜消，非獨商民之見別者有所憚，而四海帖然其寧謐矣。夫旌別之政行於東郊，而保釐之效及於四海，則殷民所係誠大矣，公其加之意哉！抑論蕞爾殷民，化訓三紀，宜無足為慮者，而康王乃拳拳于宅里、井疆之辨，郊圻、封守之制，以是見古帝
translation_en: … the people of Shang look to for encouragement and admonition, and upon which the Four Seas also depend for their security or peril—what, then, should the governance of securing and regulating be like? Indeed, among the people of the Eastern Capital, the good and the wicked cannot go without distinction; therefore, in today's governance, honoring the good and segregating the bad must take precedence. For those who follow the instructive canons and are good, their dwellings and neighborhoods are marked with emblems; manifesting their goodness also serves to make the wicked suffer, and the moral influence thus established provides more than enough encouragement. For those who do not follow the instructive canons and are wicked, their well-fields and boundaries are segregated; making them fearful also serves to make them yearn for virtue, and the warning thus displayed provides more than enough admonition. Yet while canons of encouragement and admonition are indeed the means to rouse people's hearts without tiring, laws of precaution and defense are further the means to nip the sprouts of villainy in the bud before they take form. The suburban borders were once planned out—could they not become obliterated with the passage of years? Then reaffirm their regulations, so that the boundaries are sure to be rectified. Likewise, the frontier defenses were once established—could they not be neglected in times of peace? Then maintain strict vigilance over their defense, so that the preparations and protections become ever more thorough. Thus, when the institutional order is strict, the stubborn and obstructive are silently transformed; not only will the people of Shang who are honored have something to rely upon, but the Four Seas will also be harmoniously at peace and well-governed. When discipline and law are solemn, opportunistic designs silently vanish; not only will the people of Shang who are segregated have something to fear, but the Four Seas will also be tranquilly settled and calm. Now, when the governance of honoring and segregating is practiced in the eastern suburbs, and the efficacy of securing and regulating extends to the Four Seas, that upon which the people of Yin bear is truly great—may Your Grace give special heed to it! Moreover, if we consider that the tiny remnant of Yin people had been transformed and instructed for three twelve-year cycles (thirty-six years), they ought to have been no cause for concern; yet King Kang was earnestly attentive to the distinctions of dwellings, neighborhoods, well-fields, and boundaries, and to the regulations of suburban borders and frontier defenses. From this we see how deeply the ancient sovereigns…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王愛民之深而慮事之遠也雖然導民者不專
以言守國者匪徒在險康王命畢公保釐而繼
之曰惟德惟義有以也夫
詩
我孔熯矣式禮莫愆工祝致告徂賚孝孫
苾芬孝祀神嗜飲食卜爾百福如幾如
式旣齊旣稷旣匡旣敕永錫爾極時萬
時億
葉秉敬
===

敬字得詩人旨

也盡其敬矣而神之福之也亦各從其類也巳
歌楚茨者意謂宗廟之祭非以求福也而祭不
punctuated:
王愛民之深，而慮事之遠也。雖然，導民者不專以言，守國者匪徒在險。康王命畢公保釐，而繼之曰「惟德惟義」，有以也夫！

《詩》
「我孔熯矣，式禮莫愆。工祝致告，徂賚孝孫：『苾芬孝祀，神嗜飲食。卜爾百福，如幾如式。旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕。永錫爾極，時萬時億。』」
