兢業允迪乎臯謨遜志時來啓沃猶塵于
說命箴銘在
punctuated: 以言志，本治世之麻音；頌不忘規，惟藎臣之懿榘。道先交儆，事匪彌文。故虞室賡歌，播喜起明良之盛；曁周岡嗣響，宣優游泮渙之和。酬唱同聲，分靡睽於簾陛；贊襄協德，化丕式於寰區。自《大雅》旣湮，而末流斯競。興思猛士，徒遺馬上之風；侈豔祥麟，祗習房中之曲。第詩章於三等，角技雕蟲；直供奉者五人，溺情遊燕。屬和薇槐之賦，義奚補於格心；賜序蘭菊之篇，意豈存于納誨？惟作者之謂聖，斯美焉而可傳。玆蓋恭遇皇帝陛下：仁孝性成，欽明神授。觀人文以成化，運乾旋坤轉之功；建皇極而敷言，踵帝驟王馳之躅。愼脩思永，兢業允迪乎《臯謨》；遜志時來，啓沃猶塵于《說命》。箴銘在
translation_en: … serves to express intent, rooted in the auspicious tones of a well-ordered age; praising without forgetting admonition is the admirable standard of loyal ministers. The Way puts mutual warning first, and the matter is no mere ornamental flourish. Thus in the house of Yu, responsive songs spread the flourishing of joyful arousal between enlightened ruler and worthy ministers; and when the ridges of Zhou echoed in succession, they proclaimed the harmony of leisurely and unconstrained peace. Exchanging verses with a single voice, distinctions created no estrangement between the throne curtain and the palace steps; assisting in governance with united virtue, transformative influence served as a grand model throughout the realm. Since the Greater Odes (Daya) faded away, lesser currents have competed. Stirred by thoughts of fierce warriors, one merely left behind the ethos of ruling from horseback; extravagantly admiring the auspicious unicorn, one only practiced the tunes of the inner chambers. Grading poetic compositions into three ranks was a contest in the petty craft of carving insects; having five men on duty as imperial attendants indulged passions in pleasure and banqueting. Composing matching rhapsodies on roses and pagoda trees—how could their meaning help to rectify the ruler's heart? Bestowing a preface on poems of orchids and chrysanthemums—how could the intention lie in accepting instruction? Only he who creates is called a sage, and thus his work is admirable and worthy of transmission. Now we reverently encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, whose benevolence and filial piety are formed by nature, and whose reverent intelligence is bestowed by the divine. Observing human culture to bring about transformation, You wield the achievement of turning heaven and revolving earth; establishing the august ultimate and spreading forth teachings, You follow in the footsteps of the galloping Five Emperors and Three Kings. Carefully cultivating the self with thoughts of perpetuity, in cautious diligence You truly walk in the Counsels of Gao Yao (Gao mo); with a humble mind as the seasons come round, for enlightening counsel You still humble Yourself before the Charge to Yue (Yue ming). Admonitions and inscriptions are at …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
御彜訓罔愆屬當改歲之期適應迎陽之候攄
淵衷而掞藻儼
寶翰之寵頒謂除舊布新象方懸於月令而塞
違昭德念彌切於時幾
睿語春敷特褒耆碩
虛懷夕惕俯望交脩近體聊取夫五言
旨超邃古
殊貺遥傳于一札重侈兼函敦厚溫柔括魯
頌無邪之義丁寧反覆邁衛武抑戒之詞
===
臣等幸際
昌辰叨司台鼎
彤廷曳珮未聞燮理之猷
黃閣演綸久乏論思之益曩自
平臺
召見揮翰分華逮于
講幄周旋賡詩翊學
楓宸垂眷勉報稱而弗前
藻錫頻蕃詎對揚之敢後恭依
punctuated: 御，彜訓罔愆。屬當改歲之期，適應迎陽之候。攄淵衷而掞藻，儼寶翰之寵頒。謂除舊布新，象方懸於《月令》；而塞違昭德，念彌切於時幾。睿語春敷，特褒耆碩；虛懷夕惕，俯望交脩。近體聊取夫五言，旨超邃古；殊貺遥傳于一札，重侈兼函。敦厚溫柔，括《魯頌》無邪之義；丁寧反覆，邁衛武《抑》戒之詞。臣等幸際昌辰，叨司台鼎。彤廷曳珮，未聞燮理之猷；黃閣演綸，久乏論思之益。曩自平臺召見，揮翰分華；逮于講幄周旋，賡詩翊學。楓宸垂眷，勉報稱而弗前；藻錫頻蕃，詎對揚之敢後？恭依
translation_en:
… imperial presence, and Your constant instructions are without fault. Just at the time of the new year, coinciding with the season of welcoming the returning yang, You poured forth Your profound thoughts and displayed literary brilliance, majestically bestowing the favor of Your precious calligraphy. You declared that in sweeping away the old and spreading the new, the emblems are just now suspended in the Monthly Ordinances (Yueling), while in stopping transgressions and making virtue manifest, Your thoughts grow ever more earnest at every timely juncture. Your imperial words spread like spring, specially praising the aged and eminent ministers; with a humble mind vigilant until evening, You look down in hope of mutual cultivation. Though the regulated verse casually adopts the five-syllable form, its purport surpasses remote antiquity; this extraordinary gift was transmitted from afar in a single note, doubly lavished across twin cases. Sincere and gentle, it encompasses the meaning of "having no depraved thoughts" in the Odes of Lu (Lu song); repeated and earnest, it surpasses the admonitory words of the ode "Yi" by Duke Wu of Wei.

Your servants have been fortunate to encounter this prosperous era and unworthily hold charge of the Grand Secretariat. Trailing our girdle pendants in the vermilion court, we have yet to be heard offering plans for harmonizing governance; drafting imperial decrees in the yellow-doored cabinet, we have long lacked beneficial counsel and deliberation. Earlier, since being summoned to audience at the Pingtai (Platform Terrace), where You wielded the brush and shared its splendor, down to attending upon You in the lecture tent, where we composed matching poems to assist Your learning—as the Maple Palace looks down with favor, we strive to repay and match it yet fail to advance; now that Your resplendent gifts are so frequent and abundant, how could we dare fall behind in extolling Your grace in response? Respectfully following …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
洪韻輒獻蕪言雖
大造帡幪一辭莫賛顧
仁風嘘拂萬籟齊鳴亦步亦趨瞠乎絶塵之逸
遠斯陶斯咏𢣷然下里之懷慙豈謂
兼聽芻蕘遂爾聯編
簡袠仍裁首序
標著嘉名
讓虞周於不居氷淵是凜
奬忠良之同道華袞爭輝
===
親灑御題奚止借世南之筆
榮頒近輔無勞登常侍之牀繽紛焉鳯翥龍翔
光騰
黼扆髣髴乎金聲玉振調協宮商匪繡乎鞶帨
之工蓋責以鹽梅之助不圖迂朽有此遭
逢拭目聳瞻彩絢若迷於五色齋心誦法
典刑媲美於六經敢不矢竭寸衷率先百
職都兪吁咈永輸弼直之忱明聰翼爲恪
效寅恭之誼
punctuated: 洪韻，輒獻蕪言。雖大造帡幪，一辭莫賛；顧仁風嘘拂，萬籟齊鳴。亦步亦趨，瞠乎絶塵之逸遠；斯陶斯咏，𢣷然下里之懷慙。豈謂兼聽芻蕘，遂爾聯編簡袠；仍裁首序，標著嘉名。讓虞周於不居，氷淵是凜；奬忠良之同道，華袞爭輝。親灑御題，奚止借世南之筆；榮頒近輔，無勞登常侍之牀。繽紛焉鳯翥龍翔，光騰黼扆；髣髴乎金聲玉振，調協宮商。匪繡乎鞶帨之工，蓋責以鹽梅之助。不圖迂朽，有此遭逢！拭目聳瞻，彩絢若迷於五色；齋心誦法，典刑媲美於六經。敢不矢竭寸衷，率先百職；都兪吁咈，永輸弼直之忱；明聰翼爲，恪效寅恭之誼。
translation_en: … Your Majesty's grand rhymes, I rashly offered my crude words. Even though beneath the sheltering canopy of Your Great Creation not a single word can add to its praise, yet when the benevolent wind breathes forth and brushes across the world, the myriad pipes all sound in unison. Matching You step for step and stride for stride, I stare helplessly behind as You speed far beyond the dust; rejoicing and singing in this way, I am abashed and ashamed of my rustic tunes. How could I have expected that You would deign to listen even to grass-cutters and firewood-gatherers, and thereupon bind our verses together into a compiled volume; and that You would further compose a preface at its head and bestow upon it an auspicious title! Declining comparison with the eras of Yu and Zhou without claiming their credit, You tremble as if on thin ice or at the brink of an abyss; praising loyal and worthy ministers for sharing the same Way, Your words vie in splendor with ceremonial robes of honor. Personally dashing off the imperial inscription, how does this merely surpass borrowing the brush of Yu Shinan? Gloriously bestowing it upon Your close grand counselors, there is no need to climb onto the couch of the Regular Attendant. In dazzling profusion, like phoenixes soaring and dragons wheeling, its radiance rises from the imperial screen; as if ringing with the sound of bronze and vibrating with the resonance of jade, its melody harmonizes the gong and shang notes. This is not mere ornamental embroidery upon abelt-pouch or kerchief, for it charges us with the duty of assisting You like salt and plum in seasoning the state. Never did this pedantic and decaying servant expect to meet with such an encounter! Wiping my eyes to gaze up in awe, I am nearly dazzled by the brilliant splendor of its five colors; purifying my heart to recite and model myself upon it, I find its canonical standard rivals the beauty of the Six Classics. How dare I not vow to exhaust my humble heart and take the lead before all the hundred officials; in affirming and admonishing at court, forever offer up the sincerity of corrective assistance; and in serving as Your eyes, ears, and wings, reverently fulfill the duty of respectful collegiality…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上以疇答乎
知遇下求不負其平生伏願
左右惟人
始終典學
法天行健憂勤恒徹於夙宵
與物皆春惠保咸周於遐邇則頌聲交作萬
邦底
嘉靖之隆而儆戒無虞
五位衍靈長之慶臣等無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
方學龍
punctuated:
上以疇答乎知遇，下求不負其平生。伏願左右惟人，始終典學；法天行健，憂勤恒徹於夙宵；與物皆春，惠保咸周於遐邇。則頌聲交作，萬邦底嘉靖之隆；而儆戒無虞，五位衍靈長之慶。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至。謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
方學龍
translation_en:
… above, so as to repay Your Majesty's gracious recognition, and below, to seek not to betray the aspirations of our entire lives. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will surround yourself only with worthy men and devote yourself to learning from beginning to end; that you will model yourself on Heaven's unceasing vigor, your anxious diligence persisting from morning through night; and that you will share the vitality of spring with all things, extending yourbenevolent protection universally to those far and near. Then songs of praise will arise together, and the myriad states will attain the flourishing prosperity of admirable tranquility; admonishing yourself to be without complacency, the imperial throne will prolong its enduring blessings. Your servants are overcome with the utmost emotion and reverent trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look upon Your Sacred Majesty. We reverently present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's information.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Fang Xuelong 方學龍

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導趙批我
皇上端好尚勤學敦節儉至矣乃復稱引
家法為勸篇末歸重慎獨忠愛藹然
考試官教諭程批敷對詳明允為讜論
考試官教諭周批頌不忘規足覘其日立
朝之槩
國家之興也必有開泰於先者焉以裕燕
詒之緒必有保泰於後者焉以光纘述之
猷先後同心創守一道用能衍洪庥於不
===
替昌國祚於無疆此豈徒委瑣法制之詳
粉飾文為之具已哉古人有言設誠於內
而致行之此聖帝明王興治之本也
今天下泰運方隆已執事遠舉商周故事近
述
祖
宗弘謨下詢承學冀為我
皇上保治之助甚盛心也愚也敢以臆對今夫
人君之有天下也孰貽之輿圖在御貢賦
punctuated:
同考試官訓導趙批：我皇上端好尚、勤學、敦節儉至矣，乃復稱引家法為勸，篇末歸重慎獨，忠愛藹然。
考試官教諭程批：敷對詳明，允為讜論。
考試官教諭周批：頌不忘規，足覘其日立朝之槩。
國家之興也，必有開泰於先者焉，以裕燕詒之緒；必有保泰於後者焉，以光纘述之猷。先後同心，創守一道，用能衍洪庥於不替，昌國祚於無疆。此豈徒委瑣法制之詳、粉飾文為之具已哉？古人有言：「設誠於內而致行之。」此聖帝明王興治之本也。今天下泰運方隆已，執事遠舉商、周故事，近述祖宗弘謨，下詢承學，冀為我皇上保治之助，甚盛心也。愚也敢以臆對。今夫人君之有天下也，孰貽之？輿圖在御，貢賦
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao: "Our August Emperor has already brought upright preferences, diligent learning, and earnest frugality to the utmost, yet the candidate further cites dynastic family precepts as exhortation, and at the end of the essay places primary emphasis on vigilance in solitude (shen du). His loyalty and affection shine forth."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng: "The exposition and response are detailed and clear; it is truly an upright discourse."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhou: "Praising without forgetting to admonish—this suffices to glimpse the character he will one day show when standing at court."
In the rise of a state, there must first be one who opens an era of great peace beforehand, so as to enrich the legacy bequeathed to posterity; and there must be one who preserves that great peace afterward, so as to glorify the plans of succession and continuation. When predecessors and successors are of one mind, and founding and preserving follow a single Way, thereby are they able to extend vast blessings without cease and make the dynasty's fortune prosper without bound. How could this merely be a matter of the minutiae of petty regulations or the instruments of cosmetic literary display? The ancients had a saying: "Establish sincerity within and carry it out in practice." This is the fundamental basis by which sage emperors and enlightened kings bring about good governance. Today, thegreat fortune of the realm is flourishing at its height. Your Excellency has cited the ancient precedents of the Shang and Zhou dynasties from afar and recounted the grand counsels of our imperial ancestors from recent times, inquiring down to us students in the hope of providing aid to Our August Emperor in preserving good governance—this is a most magnificent intention. Ignorant as I am, I venture to reply with my humble thoughts. Now, when a ruler possesses the realm, who bequeathed it to him? The territory under his rule and the tribute and taxes…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
輸將是祖宗櫛風沐雨而經營者也億兆
臣妾遐邇率賓是祖宗旰食宵衣而耆定
者也百職分官羣材布列是祖宗敬敎勸
學而培養者也顧創業之君備嘗艱阻則
兢惕之心勝而垂裕常周守成之君坐享
太平則宴逸之念萌而瑕纇潛伏明主察
相相與蒿目怵心交儆匪懈是卽易戒平
陂危復隍之旨也譬則世家鉅室席先世
餘貲其箱藏囊橐非不盎然充溢然且謹
===
守家法折節儉勤兢兢焉惟恐失墜故其
先業靡耗而世澤常延保天下者何以異
此昔伊尹之告太甲也曰顧諟明命曰昧
爽丕顯動必稱先王以警之而傅說之告
高宗曰王忱不艱允協于先王成德周公
之告成王亦曰覲文王之耿光揚武王之
大烈彼三君者憬然深思克自抑畏迄爲
商周令主職此之由也三代而下則有書
貞觀政要於屏風如唐之宣宗者焉有進
punctuated: 輸將，是祖宗櫛風沐雨而經營者也；億兆臣妾，遐邇率賓，是祖宗旰食宵衣而耆定者也；百職分官，羣材布列，是祖宗敬敎勸學而培養者也。顧創業之君，備嘗艱阻，則兢惕之心勝，而垂裕常周；守成之君，坐享太平，則宴逸之念萌，而瑕纇潛伏。明主察相，相與蒿目怵心，交儆匪懈，是卽《易》戒平陂、危復隍之旨也。譬則世家鉅室，席先世餘貲，其箱藏囊橐非不盎然充溢，然且謹守家法，折節儉勤，兢兢焉惟恐失墜，故其先業靡耗，而世澤常延。保天下者，何以異此？昔伊尹之告太甲也，曰「顧諟明命」，曰「昧爽丕顯」，動必稱先王以警之；而傅說之告高宗，曰「王忱不艱，允協于先王成德」；周公之告成王，亦曰「覲文王之耿光，揚武王之大烈」。彼三君者，憬然深思，克自抑畏，迄爲商、周令主，職此之由也。三代而下，則有書《貞觀政要》於屏風如唐之宣宗者焉，有進
translation_en: … tribute and taxes brought forward—this is what the Imperial Ancestors painstakingly built up while combed by the wind and bathed by the rain; the millions of subjects and concubines, near and far all submitting in allegiance—this is what the Imperial Ancestors pacified and settled while eating late and dressing before dawn; the hundred offices distributed among posts and the multitude of talents arrayed in rank—this is what the Imperial Ancestors nurtured and cultivated by revering instruction and encouraging learning. Yet rulers who found a dynasty fully experience hardship and obstruction, so their minds of cautious vigilance prevail and the abundance they bequeath is ever comprehensive; whereas rulers who maintain an established order sit and enjoy great peace, so thoughts of ease and indulgence sprout and flaws and blemishes secretly lurk. When an enlightened ruler and discerning ministers gaze anxiously upon the world with trepidation in their hearts, mutually admonishing one another without slackening, this is precisely the purport of the Book of Changes (Yi) in warning that level ground becomes a slope and in dreading that the city wall will crumble back into the moat. Take, for example, a hereditary house or great family resting upon the surplus wealth of former generations: its chests, storehouses, sacks, and bags are not without brimming abundance, yet its members still carefully observe the family regulations, humble themselves in frugality and diligence, and remain cautiously fearful only lest anything be lost or ruined; therefore, their ancestral estate suffers no depletion and their generational blessings are long extended. How is preserving the empire any different from this? In antiquity, when Yi Yin 伊尹 counselled Tai Jia 太甲, he said, "Keep your eye upon this bright mandate," and he said, "At dawn he was greatly illustrious," at every turn citing the former kings to admonish him. When Fu Yue 傅說 counselled Gaozong 高宗, he said, "If the king's sincerity is not daunted by difficulty, it will truly accord with the perfected virtue of the former king." And when the Duke of Zhou 周公 counselled King Cheng 成王, he likewise said, "Behold the bright glory of King Wen 文王, and extol the great achievements of King Wu 武王." That those three rulers awakened to deep reflection, were able to restrain themselves in reverent awe, and ultimately became exemplary sovereigns of the Shang and Zhou dynasties was entirely for this reason. From the Three Dynasties downward, there was one such as Emperor Xuanzong 宣宗 of the Tang, who inscribed the Essentials of Government of the Zhenguan Period (Zhenguan zhengyao) upon his folding screen; and there was one who had presented…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讀三朝寶訓如宋之孝宗者焉夫貞觀政
要神龍中吳兢所撰也謂唐之極治貞觀
爲最采時政可紀者上之於朝其爲篇目
以四十計蓋箴勸之義備焉傳至宣宗毎
拱手斂容而讀之豈不念締造之艱哉顧
勵精未幾旋已怠荒魏謩以直言罷相孰
與獎魏徵之直王宰縁貴倖求用孰與燭
宇文士及之姦迎軒轅集於羅浮孰與斥
蕭瑀崇釋之謬以故河湟雖復內地騷亭
===
大中之政衰巳三朝寶訓天聖中李淑所
撰也始於建隆迄於乾興凡綸音政典悉
著于篇裒而爲事者以百計蓋經緯之謨
具焉傳至孝宗毎値進講輒咨詢弗倦豈
非儼羹墻之見哉顧徒飾口耳靡措躬行
外戚家毋得除兩府矣而張說用戚屬檦
樞內侍省毋得預政事矣而甘昇與曾覿
相表裏王昭素嘗以儒術召對便殿矣而
朱熹用道學見疎以故正邪雜進事權旁
punctuated: 讀《三朝寶訓》如宋之孝宗者焉。夫《貞觀政要》，神龍中吳兢所撰也。謂唐之極治，貞觀爲最，采時政可紀者上之於朝，其爲篇目以四十計，蓋箴勸之義備焉。傳至宣宗，毎拱手斂容而讀之，豈不念締造之艱哉？顧勵精未幾，旋已怠荒。魏謩以直言罷相，孰與獎魏徵之直？王宰縁貴倖求用，孰與燭宇文士及之姦？迎軒轅集於羅浮，孰與斥蕭瑀崇釋之謬？以故河湟雖復，內地騷亭，大中之政衰巳。《三朝寶訓》，天聖中李淑所撰也。始於建隆，迄於乾興，凡綸音政典，悉著于篇，裒而爲事者以百計，蓋經緯之謨具焉。傳至孝宗，毎値進講，輒咨詢弗倦，豈非儼羹墻之見哉？顧徒飾口耳，靡措躬行。外戚家毋得除兩府矣，而張說用戚屬檦樞；內侍省毋得預政事矣，而甘昇與曾覿相表裏；王昭素嘗以儒術召對便殿矣，而朱熹用道學見疎。以故正邪雜進，事權旁
translation_en: …and one who had the Precious Instructions of the Three Reigns (Sanchao baoxun) read to him at court lectures, such as Emperor Xiaozong of the Song. Now, the Essentials of Government of the Zhenguan Era (Zhenguan zhengyao) was compiled by Wu Jing吳兢 during the Shenlong era (705–707). Holding that the pinnacle of Tang governance was the Zhenguan era (627–649), he gathered memorable administrative affairs of that time and presented them to the court; its chapters number forty, and the principles of admonition and encouragement are complete therein. Passed down to Emperor Xuanzong, whenever he folded his hands and composed his countenance to read it, how could he not have been mindful of the hardships of founding the dynasty? Yet after striving for vigor only briefly, he soon grew lax and neglectful. Wei Mo魏謩 was dismissed as Grand Councilor for his forthright speech—how does that compare with praising the rectitude of Wei Zheng魏徵? Wang Zai王宰 sought appointment through influential favorites—how does that compare with seeing through the treachery of Yuwen Shiji宇文士及? Welcoming the adept Xuanyuan Ji軒轅集 from Mount Luofu—how does that compare with rebuking Xiao Yu蕭瑀 for the folly of venerating Buddhism? Consequently, although the He and Huang regions were recovered, the interior was thrown into turmoil [? 騷亭, likely a misprint for 騷動], and the governance of the Dazhong era (847–860) fell into decline. The Precious Instructions of the Three Reigns was compiled by Li Shu李淑 during the Tiansheng era (1023–1032). Beginning with the Jianlong era (960–963) and ending with the Qianxing era (1022), all imperial pronouncements and administrative statutes were recorded in its pages; the matters collected therein number in the hundreds, and the grand plans for ordering the state are fully present. Passed down to Emperor Xiaozong, whenever a court lecture took place, he would inquire tirelessly—was this not like seeing the ancestral exemplars vividly in his soup and on his walls? Yet he merely adorned his ears and mouth without putting those lessons into personal practice. Imperial affines were forbidden from being appointed to the Two Administrations, yet Zhang Yue張說 held the pivot of the Bureau of Military Affairs [? 檦樞, likely for 筦樞] by virtue of being an imperial relative; the Palace Domestic Service was forbidden from interfering in affairs of state, yet Gan Sheng甘昇 and Zeng Di曾覿 colluded from within and without; Wang Zhaosu王昭素 had once been summoned to an informal palace hall to respond on Confucian learning, yet Zhu Xi朱熹 was alienated on account of the Learning of the Way (Daoxue). Consequently, the upright and the wicked advanced together, administrative authority slipped away…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
落乾道之業替已大都人情始於銳常卒
於怠采其華常遺其實唐宋二君非真有
恭默思道陟降在庭之心也陽浮慕之耳
宜其假之而遽歸舉之而旋廢矣矧唐以
雜霸為治而本原弗端宋以忠厚立國而
紀綱弗振卽所以詒謀者不逮商周遠甚
其後嗣又何以觀也洪惟我
祖
宗啓祚
===
列聖紹庥
駿德豐功奠安寓內若乾元之覆幬焉
神謨聖範昭示
後昆若日月之照臨焉
深仁厚澤永庇蒸黔若雨露之滋潤焉
瑤編玉冊之紀
金匱石室之藏非遐逖所能悉窺也而文獻
足徵儀刑如在巍然煥然真克邁三五之
登閎陋唐宋於下風者可歷舉而數矣我
punctuated:
落，乾道之業替已。大都人情始於銳，常卒於怠；采其華，常遺其實。唐、宋二君，非真有恭默思道、陟降在庭之心也，陽浮慕之耳。宜其假之而遽歸，舉之而旋廢矣。矧唐以雜霸為治而本原弗端，宋以忠厚立國而紀綱弗振，卽所以詒謀者，不逮商、周遠甚，其後嗣又何以觀也？

洪惟我祖宗啓祚，列聖紹庥。駿德豐功，奠安寓內，若乾元之覆幬焉；神謨聖範，昭示後昆，若日月之照臨焉；深仁厚澤，永庇蒸黔，若雨露之滋潤焉。瑤編玉冊之紀、金匱石室之藏，非遐逖所能悉窺也；而文獻足徵，儀刑如在，巍然煥然，真克邁三、五之登閎，陋唐、宋於下風者，可歷舉而數矣。我
translation_en:
…slipped away, and the enterprise of the Qiandao reign fell into decline. In general, it is human nature to begin with keenness yet commonly end in laxity, and to gather the outward blossoms while commonly leaving behind the substance. These two monarchs of the Tang and Song did not truly possess a heart that reverently and silently pondered the Way, or felt the spirits of their ancestors ascending and descending in the court; they merely admired such ideals superficially and for show. No wonder, then, that they borrowed those virtues only to quickly abandon them, and initiated reforms only to soon let them lapse! How much more so given that the Tang governed through an admixture of hegemonic force, so its fundamental source was not upright, while the Song founded its state upon generous leniency, so its discipline and institutional order remained uninvigorated. Even the counsels handed down by their founders fell far short of those of the Shang and Zhou—what, then, could their descendants possibly take as a model to behold?

Reverently reflecting upon our own Imperial Ancestors, who opened the dynastic fortune, and the successive Sacred Emperors, who continued their blessings: their lofty virtue and abundant achievements pacified all within the realm, like the overarching canopy of Primal Heaven; their divine counsels and sacred models shone forth as guidance to posterity, like the illumination of the sun and moon; and their deep benevolence and rich grace eternally sheltered the common people, like the nourishing moisture of rain and dew. The records inscribed in jade-like compilations and precious tablets, stored away in golden caskets and stone chambers, are not what someone in a distant and lowly station can fully peer into; yet the documentary evidence is sufficient to corroborate them, and their exemplary standards remain as if present before us—towering and resplendent, truly surpassing the grand heights of the Three Kings and Five Emperors and looking down upon the Tang and Song as inferior. These things can be enumerated one by one. Our…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上嗣曆握乾乃益闡揚而光大之崇奉
兩宮敦隆盛典至孝也
日御講幄
躬裁庶政至明也
軫念民瘼
屢詔蠲恤至仁也一時大小臣工罔不濯磨振
奮求無負於
昌期即山海遐陬亦喁喁歌頌矣頃歲
俞輔臣之請以
===
累朝
訓錄分類編摩
便殿講讀之餘時復
進講曰法祖曰創業艱難其大指也曰敬天
曰保民曰勤學曰勵精圖治其急務也曰
謹祭祀曰愼起居以至於正紀綱御夷狄
絲分縷析其條目也簡袠雖繁而指要則
約事類雖夥而條貫可陳
祖
punctuated: 皇上嗣曆握乾，乃益闡揚而光大之。崇奉兩宮，敦隆盛典，至孝也；日御講幄，躬裁庶政，至明也；軫念民瘼，屢詔蠲恤，至仁也。一時大小臣工，罔不濯磨振奮，求無負於昌期；即山海遐陬，亦喁喁歌頌矣。頃歲俞輔臣之請，以累朝《訓錄》分類編摩，便殿講讀之餘，時復進講：曰法祖，曰創業艱難，其大指也；曰敬天，曰保民，曰勤學，曰勵精圖治，其急務也；曰謹祭祀，曰愼起居，以至於正紀綱、御夷狄，絲分縷析，其條目也。簡袠雖繁，而指要則約；事類雖夥，而條貫可陳。祖
translation_en:
… His Majesty succeeded to the throne and grasped the sovereign power, and he has further expounded and magnified them. He reverently serves the Two Empresses Dowager and richly honors the grand ceremonies: this is supreme filial piety. He daily attends the lecture tent and personally decides the myriad affairs of state: this is supreme perspicacity. He feels deep compassion for the distress of the people and repeatedly issues edicts granting tax remissions and relief: this is supreme benevolence. At this time, officials great and small all without exception polish their conduct and rouse themselves, seeking not to fail this prosperous era; even in distant corners among the mountains and seas, the people look up eagerly and sing his praises.

In recent years, consenting to the request of the Grand Secretaries, he ordered that the Ancestral Injunctions and Veritable Records of successive reigns be classified and compiled. In the intervals from lectures and readings in the side palaces, they are from time to time presented for exposition: "Emulating the Ancestors" and "The Hardships of Founding the Dynasty" are their overarching themes; "Revering Heaven," "Protecting the People," "Diligence in Learning," and "Rousing One's Spirits to Seek Good Governance" are their urgent tasks; "Carefulness in Sacrifices," "Prudence in Daily Conduct," and so on down to "Rectifying the Laws and Discipline" and "Controlling the Four Barbarians," analyzed down to the finest thread, are their detailed headings. Although the volumes are numerous, their essential meaning is concise; although the categories of affairs are multitudinous, their systematic thread can be set forth. The Ancestors'…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宗之彝訓具是矣猗與休哉與治同道罔不□
其斯之謂乎乃執事猶欲掇要探本圖所
為芹曝獻者則何以稱焉仰聞我
太祖諭侍臣曰皇天無親惟德是輔使吾後世
子孫皆如成康輔弼之臣皆如周召則可
以祈天永命國祚愈昌我
成祖之訓曰人常慮危迺不蹈危車行於峻坂
而仆於平地者慎於難而忽於易也保天
下亦如御車何可不慎大哉
===
皇言勒法琬琰
列聖之所以繼序不忘者率是道也愚竊觀輔
臣之所獻規
皇上之所延納如曰審官曰理財曰興教化曰
飭武備諸事則宰臣總其綱六卿分其職
臺諫繩其愆
穆清之上第一加意受成焉即以咸熙庶績
永保丕平易易也顧惟
堂陛森嚴則下情靡達
punctuated: 宗之彝訓具是矣。猗與休哉！「與治同道，罔不□」，其斯之謂乎！乃執事猶欲掇要探本，圖所為芹曝獻者，則何以稱焉？仰聞我太祖諭侍臣曰：「皇天無親，惟德是輔。使吾後世子孫皆如成、康，輔弼之臣皆如周、召，則可以祈天永命，國祚愈昌。」我成祖之訓曰：「人常慮危，迺不蹈危。車行於峻坂而仆於平地者，慎於難而忽於易也。保天下亦如御車，何可不慎！」大哉皇言，勒法琬琰，列聖之所以繼序不忘者，率是道也。愚竊觀輔臣之所獻規，皇上之所延納，如曰審官、曰理財、曰興教化、曰飭武備諸事，則宰臣總其綱，六卿分其職，臺諫繩其愆，穆清之上，第一加意受成焉，即以咸熙庶績，永保丕平，易易也。顧惟堂陛森嚴，則下情靡達；
translation_en:
…the constant instructions of the Imperial Ancestors are all complete here. Oh, how admirable and splendid! "One who follows the same Way as those who brought about order never fails to prosper [□]"—surely this is what is meant! Yet Your Excellency still wishes to gather the essentials and probe the fundamentals, seeking something to offer like the humble gift of wild celery or warming in the sun—how could I be equal to that?

I have reverently heard that our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) instructed his attending officials, saying: "August Heaven has no partiality; it aids only virtue. If my descendants in future generations are all like Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou, and their assisting ministers are all like the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, then we may pray to Heaven for a perpetual mandate, and the dynasty's fortune will grow ever more prosperous." And the instruction of our Accomplished Progenitor (Chengzu) reads: "When a person is constantly mindful of danger, he does not tread into danger. That a carriage travels safely over a steep slope yet overturns on level ground is because one is cautious in difficulty and careless in ease. Preserving the realm is just like driving a carriage—how could one not be cautious!" Great indeed are the Imperial words, engraved as law upon fine jade! That whereby the successive Sacred Emperors have carried on the line without forgetting is by following this very Way.

I have humbly observed that among the admonitions offered by the Grand Secretaries and received by His Majesty—such matters as examining officials, managing finances, promoting moral transformation through education, and putting military defenses in order—the chief ministers oversee their general principles, the Six Ministers divide their specific duties, and the Censorate and Speaking Officials correct their faults. Above in serene profundity, the Emperor need only pay heed and accept the completed results; thus to make all achievements shine brightly and forever preserve great peace is most easy. Yet considering that when the court steps are towering and stern, the conditions of those below cannot reach above; …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宮府懸隔則匡拂末繇是在
密勿之中預圖而默省之耳愚請得正言無
諱可乎夫人主一心攻以衆欲一念之好
尚羣情所共趨也喜珍玩卽淫巧者售喜
異端卽詭誕者售猶設侯張的衆盻咸集
鮮弗中矣故監胡元之覆轍則碎水晶宮
漏懲梁宋之迷途則闢釋老異教是
祖
宗端好尚之家法所當念也自昔高宗之遜志
===
時敏成王之緝煕光明罔非以務學爲急
者學猶植也不以有人而作無人而輟也
一暴十寒其如有萌焉何哉故
御書洪範篇雖
宮中不釋手
命儒臣進講大學衍義雖盛暑不輟業是
祖
宗勤學之家法所當念也天子以天下奉一人
錦衣玉食匪乏供也而曰克儉于家曰慎
punctuated: 宮府懸隔，則匡拂末繇，是在密勿之中，預圖而默省之耳。愚請得正言無諱，可乎？夫人主一心，攻以衆欲，一念之好尚，羣情所共趨也。喜珍玩，卽淫巧者售；喜異端，卽詭誕者售。猶設侯張的，衆盻咸集，鮮弗中矣。故監胡元之覆轍，則碎水晶宮漏；懲梁、宋之迷途，則闢釋、老異教。是祖宗端好尚之家法所當念也。自昔高宗之遜志時敏，成王之緝煕光明，罔非以務學爲急者。學猶植也，不以有人而作，無人而輟也。一暴十寒，其如有萌焉何哉？故御書《洪範篇》，雖宮中不釋手；命儒臣進講《大學衍義》，雖盛暑不輟業。是祖宗勤學之家法所當念也。天子以天下奉一人，錦衣玉食，匪乏供也。而曰「克儉于家」，曰「慎…
translation_en:
… and when the inner palace and the outer court are widely separated, there is no way to offer corrective remonstrance. Thus it rests on anticipating matters and silently examining oneself within the innermost sanctum. May I, in my simplicity, be permitted to speak forthrightly and without taboo?

Now, the sovereign has but a single mind, yet it is besieged by a multitude of desires; the predilection of a single thought is that toward which the sentiments of all converge. If he delights in rare curiosities, then peddlers of extravagant ingenuity find a market; if he delights in heterodox doctrines, then peddlers of deceit and absurdity find a market. It is just like setting up an archery target and stretching its bull's-eye: all eyes gather upon it, and few fail to hit the mark. Therefore, taking warning from the overturned chariot of the Mongol Yuan, [our Imperial Founder] smashed the crystal palace clepsydra; chastened by theastray paths of the Liang and Song, he refuted the heterodox teachings of Buddhism and Daoism. This is the family law of the Ancestors regarding rectifying one's predilections, which ought to be borne in mind.

From of old, King Gaozong's keeping a humble mind and being ever diligent, and King Cheng's continuing the bright illumination, were in every case rooted in making devotion to learning their urgent priority. Learning is like cultivating plants: one does not work at it because others are present and cease when no one is there. If there is one day of warmth followed by ten days of cold, what good will it do even if shoots begin to sprout? Therefore, the "Great Plan" (Hongfan pian) written in the Imperial hand was never put down even inside the palace; and the command to Confucian officials to lecture on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) did not cease even in the height of summer heat. This is the family law of the Ancestors regarding diligence in learning, which ought to be borne in mind.

The Son of Heaven has the entire empire to support his single person; brocade robes and jade-like delicacies are by no means lacking in supply. Yet it was said, "able to be frugal in his household," and it was said, "be mindful of…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乃儉德誠慮夫膏脂易竭意欲難窮作法
於奢將無以維其後矣故惜費效於漢文
則隙地無亭臺之築惡服法於大禹則
後宮有澣濯之衣是
祖
宗敦節儉之家法所當念也伯冏之命曰侍御
僕從罔非正人而無昵憸人之戒尤諄諄
焉彼嬛巧之姿日侍左右憑社則玩紀煬
竈則蔽明自匪剛明果斷之主鮮不昵而
===
蕩矣故私請內庾以充奇富則導諛之詰
責必嚴議省大官議覈營卒則掖廷之浮
言罔奪是
祖
宗馭近習之家法所當念也不特此也思
存省之錄則警戒日勤玩
敬一之箴則起居必慎自
深宮燕閒以及
大廷臨御凜若
punctuated: 乃儉德。誠慮夫膏脂易竭，意欲難窮，作法於奢，將無以維其後矣。故惜費效於漢文，則隙地無亭臺之築；惡服法於大禹，則後宮有澣濯之衣。是祖宗敦節儉之家法，所當念也。《伯冏之命》曰：「侍御僕從，罔非正人。」而無昵憸人之戒，尤諄諄焉。彼嬛巧之姿，日侍左右，憑社則玩紀，煬竈則蔽明，自匪剛明果斷之主，鮮不昵而蕩矣。故私請內庾以充奇富，則導諛之詰責必嚴；議省大官，議覈營卒，則掖廷之浮言罔奪。是祖宗馭近習之家法，所當念也。不特此也，思《存省》之錄，則警戒日勤；玩《敬一》之箴，則起居必慎。自深宮燕閒，以及大廷臨御，凜若
translation_en: … frugal virtue." It is truly out of concern that the people's substance is easily exhausted while personal desires are hard to satisfy; if one sets an example in extravagance, there will be no way to sustain what follows. Therefore, by emulating Emperor Wen of Han (Han Wen) in begrudging expenditures, no pavilions or terraces were built on vacant grounds; by modeling oneself on the Great Yu (Da Yu) in wearing plain clothing, the inner palace wore washed and laundered garments. This is the family law of the Imperial Ancestors in emphasizing frugality, which ought to be borne in mind. "The Charge to Bo Jiong" (Bo Jiong zhi ming) states: "Let none of the attendants, servants, and followers be other than upright men," and its warning against growing familiar with artfully evil men is especially earnest. Those of nimble and cunning disposition attend daily at the sovereign's side; relying on the altar like rats, they trifle with discipline, and standing before the stove to block the light, they obscure his clarity. Unless one is a firm, discerning, and decisive ruler, few avoid growing intimate with them and falling into dissipation. Therefore, when someone privately requested grain from the inner granaries to amass extraordinary wealth, the rebuke for inducing flattery was unfailingly severe; when deliberations were held to curtail the Office of Imperial Entertainments (Daguan) or to verify the garrison troops, the baseless talk of the inner court was not allowed to sway the decision. This is the family law of the Imperial Ancestors in controlling close attendants, which ought to be borne in mind. Not only this: by reflecting on the Record of Preserving the Mind and Self-Examination (Cunxing lu), one's vigilance becomes daily more diligent; by savoring the Admonition on Reverence and Unity (Jingyi zhen), one's daily conduct and movements are unfailingly cautious. From moments of leisure in the deep palace to presiding over audiences in the great court, remain in reverent awe as if…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
列聖之陟降于前焉匪第諷咏遺編聳動觀聽
而已由是則正人日親而奇袤惝滛之徒
遠矣忠言日進而豫大豐亨之說黜矣庶
職競勸方內禔福而明作惇大之業成矣
蓋天下國家之本在
君身而其機在宥密雖拂士無緣畢其議邇臣
不得闚其忠者惟
明主一獨覺耳獨覺則明通明通則公溥夫是
以恭巳南面而宇內太和也故曰王道本
===
于誠意其要只在謹獨執事所謂保泰之
助意在斯乎
第二問
祝以忠
同考試官訓導張批辨析古今人物情態殆盡
而文思縱橫不竭敬服敬服
同考試官教諭區批浩博之學璀璨之詞末歸
重人才樂為吾用尤反覆有情佳士也
考試官教諭程批品藻中有確論非經生語
punctuated:
列聖之陟降于前焉，匪第諷咏遺編、聳動觀聽而已。由是則正人日親，而奇袤惝滛之徒遠矣；忠言日進，而豫大豐亨之說黜矣；庶職競勸，方內禔福，而明作惇大之業成矣。蓋天下國家之本在君身，而其機在宥密。雖拂士無緣畢其議，邇臣不得闚其忠者，惟明主一獨覺耳。獨覺則明通，明通則公溥，夫是以恭巳南面而宇內太和也。故曰：王道本于誠意，其要只在謹獨。執事所謂保泰之助，意在斯乎！

第二問
祝以忠
同考試官訓導張批：辨析古今人物情態殆盡，而文思縱橫不竭，敬服，敬服。
同考試官教諭區批：浩博之學，璀璨之詞，末歸重人才樂為吾用，尤反覆有情，佳士也。
考試官教諭程批：品藻中有確論，非經生語。
translation_en:
… the succession of Imperial Ancestors ascending and descending before him—not merely chanting the bequeathed texts to stir the eyes and ears of observers. From this, upright men will be drawn closer day by day, while deviant, devious, and licentious fellows will be kept at a distance; loyal words will be presented day by day, while talk of extravagant ease and lavish abundance will be dismissed; the hundred officials will vie in diligence, the realm within will enjoy peace and blessing, and the enterprise of enlightened vigor and generous greatness will be accomplished. For the root of the empire and the state lies in the person of the Ruler, and its pivotal mechanism lies in the quiet depth of his mind. Even where remonstrating counselors have no way to exhaust their arguments and close ministers cannot peer in to offer their loyalty, it rests solely on the Enlightened Sovereign's solitary awareness. When there is solitary awareness, there is clear comprehension; when there is clear comprehension, there is impartial breadth. Thus he holds himself in reverent composure facing south, and the whole world enjoys supreme harmony. Therefore it is said: the Kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere, and its essential point lies simply in being watchful over oneself when alone. What Your Excellency refers to as the aid to preserving great peace—does its meaning not lie right here?

Second Question
Zhu Yizhong 祝以忠
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: He analyzes the dispositions and circumstances of figures ancient and modern almost exhaustively, while his literary thought ranges freely and inexhaustibly. Admirable, truly admirable!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Ou: Vast and erudite learning, resplendent phrasing; at the end he places the weight on men of talent rejoicing to be of service to us, which is developed repeatedly and with deep feeling. A fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng: Amidst his appraisals there are definitive judgments; these are not the words of a mere student of the Classics.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭周批〔援古證今說之淵然〕
夫人主所以藻鏡羣材使灼然當于用而
不爽者惟恃吾獨見獨明而不可眩以名
實也何謂名徵諸人而樂道焉與吾之實
而相協者也何謂實施諸用而愜當焉與
吾之名而允稱者也譬之射操弓而立乎
儀的之間聚而指之曰某能射此名也迨
乎一縱一送弓與手相諧手與目相應不
煩矢鏃而收命中之能此實也譬之御列
===
驂而置諸康莊之衢聚而指之曰某能御
此名也迨乎一罄一控車與馬相適馬與
人相調不勞鞭策而收致遠之利此實也
審乎此以藻鏡羣材則徵名而實因以見
考實而名因以符士之任實者將悉為吾
用而飾名者罔所售其欺矣嘗聞嬰兒相
與戲也以塵為飯以塗為羹以木為胾然
至日晩必歸饟者塵飯塗羹可以戲而不
可以飽也鄙生蹲伏蒿萊中抱遺編而呫
punctuated:
考試官教諭周批：〔援古證今，說之淵然。〕

夫人主所以藻鏡羣材，使灼然當于用而不爽者，惟恃吾獨見獨明，而不可眩以名實也。何謂名？徵諸人而樂道焉，與吾之實而相協者也。何謂實？施諸用而愜當焉，與吾之名而允稱者也。譬之射：操弓而立乎儀的之間，聚而指之曰：「某能射。」此名也；迨乎一縱一送，弓與手相諧，手與目相應，不煩矢鏃而收命中之能，此實也。譬之御：列驂而置諸康莊之衢，聚而指之曰：「某能御。」此名也；迨乎一罄一控，車與馬相適，馬與人相調，不勞鞭策而收致遠之利，此實也。審乎此以藻鏡羣材，則徵名而實因以見，考實而名因以符，士之任實者將悉為吾用，而飾名者罔所售其欺矣。嘗聞嬰兒相與戲也，以塵為飯，以塗為羹，以木為胾；然至日晩必歸饟者，塵飯塗羹可以戲而不可以飽也。鄙生蹲伏蒿萊中，抱遺編而呫
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhou, Instructor: 〔Citing the ancient to verify the present, he discourses with profound depth.〕

Now, that by which a ruler of men evaluates and reflects the multitude of talents, ensuring that they clearly suit their practical uses without fail, relies solely on his own independent insight and singular discernment, refusing to be dazzled by reputation and reality. What is meant by reputation? That which is attested by others, who gladly speak of it, and which harmonizes with one's reality. What is meant by reality? That which is applied in practical use and proves thoroughly fitting, and which truly corresponds to one's reputation. Take archery as an analogy: when a man holds a bow and stands amidst the targets, and people gather to point at him, saying, "So-and-so is skilled at archery," this is reputation; when it comes to the actual release and follow-through, where bow and hand are in harmony, hand and eye respond to one another, and without wasting arrows he achieves the feat of hitting the mark, this is reality. Take charioteering as an analogy: when a man arrays a team of horses and places them upon a broad thoroughfare, and people gather to point at him, saying, "So-and-so is skilled at charioteering," this is reputation; when it comes to giving rein and checking the steeds, where chariot and horses are mutually suited, horses and driver are attuned to one another, and without the toil of the whip he reaps the advantage of reaching afar, this is reality. If one examines things in this light to evaluate and reflect the multitude of talents, then by verifying reputation the reality is thereby revealed, and by testing reality the reputation is thereby confirmed. Thus, scholars who shoulder true substance will all be employed for our use, while those who merely adorn their reputation will have nowhere to peddle their deceit. I have heard that when young children play together, they use dust for rice, mud for soup, and wood for sliced meat; yet when evening comes they must return home for a meal, because dust-rice and mud-soup can serve for play, but cannot satisfy hunger. I, a rustic student crouching among the weeds, clasping handed-down texts and murmuring…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嚅烏覩所謂名實之指即使言稡然當明
問亦塵飯塗羹耳執事將無以鄙生爲戲
耶久矣夫名實之難辯也假令名之與實
若左券之相符則一庸人能辯之久矣俟
於英辟顧抱實者鮮矜名者多車輈與月
旦齊呼腊鼠與璞玉竝號荻苗類菉薏苡
似菊虎皮而羊質鳳彩而鵲聲其情貌懸
也且飾名者進則尚實者抑朝有捷巧輕
躁之夫則野有敦朴恬靜之士朝有容悅
===
便佞之黨則野有剛正伉直之人朝有暴
戾貪黷之臣則野有寛大謹廉之輩其負
勝定也皐陶之告舜曰知人則哲能官人
惟帝其難之子產有言人心不同有如其
面蓋自古記之矣請略陳疇昔之槩以復
明問而徐效一得之愚可乎材品不同信
不可以一端盡也何謂名實之相副者伊
尹有莘之農夫也方其秉耒而耕固已希
心堯舜及三聘而出遂建華夏之勳而商
punctuated:
嚅，烏覩所謂名實之指？即使言稡然當明問，亦塵飯塗羹耳。執事將無以鄙生爲戲耶？

久矣夫，名實之難辯也！假令名之與實，若左券之相符，則一庸人能辯之久矣，俟於英辟？顧抱實者鮮，矜名者多。車輈與月旦齊呼，腊鼠與璞玉竝號，荻苗類菉，薏苡似菊，虎皮而羊質，鳳彩而鵲聲，其情貌懸也。且飾名者進，則尚實者抑：朝有捷巧輕躁之夫，則野有敦朴恬靜之士；朝有容悅便佞之黨，則野有剛正伉直之人；朝有暴戾貪黷之臣，則野有寛大謹廉之輩，其負勝定也。皐陶之告舜曰：「知人則哲，能官人，惟帝其難之。」子產有言：「人心不同，有如其面。」蓋自古記之矣。請略陳疇昔之槩以復明問，而徐效一得之愚，可乎？

材品不同，信不可以一端盡也。何謂名實之相副者？伊尹，有莘之農夫也。方其秉耒而耕，固已希心堯、舜；及三聘而出，遂建華夏之勳，而商
translation_en:
…reciting in a whisper, how could I perceive the purport of what are called reputation and reality? Even if my words happen to match your enlightened inquiry, they are nothing more than rice of dust and soup of mud. Would Your Excellency not regard this rustic scholar as merely playing a game?

Long indeed has it been difficult to distinguish between reputation and reality! Suppose reputation and reality matched each other like the left half of a tally; then any ordinary person could have distinguished them long ago—why wait for an heroic sovereign? Yet those who embrace reality are few, while those who boast of reputation are many. A carriage pole and the "monthly critique" (Yuedan) are called by the same name [?]; dried rats and uncarved jade share the same designation; reed shoots resemble green bamboo [?], and job's-tears look like chrysanthemums; there is the skin of a tiger over the substance of a sheep, the plumage of a phoenix with the voice of a magpie—so far apart are their true nature and outward appearance. Moreover, when those who embellish their reputation advance, those who prize reality are suppressed: if at court there are nimble, artful, frivolous, and impetuous fellows, then in the wilderness there will be honest, simple, calm, and quiet scholars; if at court there are cliques of flattering, obsequious sycophants, then in the wilderness there will be upright, incorruptible, and straightforward men; if at court there are violent, perverse, greedy, and corrupt ministers, then in the wilderness there will be magnanimous, prudent, and incorruptible individuals—their defeat or victory is thus predetermined. Gao Yao 皐陶 told Shun 舜: "To know men is wisdom, to be able to nominate men for office—even the sovereign finds this difficult." Zichan 子產 had a saying: "Men's minds are different, just as their faces are." Indeed, this has been recorded since antiquity. May I roughly set forth the general outlines of the past in reply to your enlightened inquiry, and then slowly offer my humble, single insight?

Talents and characters differ, and truly cannot be exhausted from a single aspect. What is meant by reputation and reality corresponding to each other? Yi Yin 伊尹 was a farmer of Youshen 有莘. While he held the plow and tilled the soil, he had already set his heart on Yao 堯 and Shun; when he emerged after being thrice invited, he established merits throughout the civilized realm, and the Shang 商…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道以隆諸葛亮南陽之隱士也方其抱膝
而吟因已托志管樂及三顧而起遂樹鼎
足之烈而炎祚再昌此所謂名實之相副
者也何謂有其實而無其名者毛遂自賛
於平原門下皆笑之脫穎而結强楚之援
邯鄲之圍立解韓信寄食於漂母少年且
侮之登壇而畫蹙項之計垓下之師竟殲
此所謂有其實而無其名者也何謂有其
名而無其實者馬謖之在蜀嘗奏記孔明
===
曰攻城爲下攻心爲上兵戰爲下心戰爲
上論非不偉也街亭一敗而首領不保殷
浩之在晉謝尚諸人相謂曰淵源不起當
如蒼生何以其出處卜江左興亡望非不
隆也壽陽一挫而身名俱損此所謂有其
名而無其實者也何謂蚤負不美之名而
晚令者王湛名爲癡不爲從子王濟所禮
一日濟與論易多出濟意表復就蟻封盤
馬湛回策如縈而濟馬踣濟乃歎曰家有
punctuated:
道以隆；諸葛亮，南陽之隱士也，方其抱膝而吟，因已托志管、樂，及三顧而起，遂樹鼎足之烈，而炎祚再昌。此所謂名實之相副者也。

何謂有其實而無其名者？毛遂自賛於平原，門下皆笑之，脫穎而結强楚之援，邯鄲之圍立解；韓信寄食於漂母，少年且侮之，登壇而畫蹙項之計，垓下之師竟殲。此所謂有其實而無其名者也。

何謂有其名而無其實者？馬謖之在蜀，嘗奏記孔明曰：「攻城爲下，攻心爲上；兵戰爲下，心戰爲上。」論非不偉也，街亭一敗而首領不保；殷浩之在晉，謝尚諸人相謂曰：「淵源不起，當如蒼生何？」以其出處卜江左興亡，望非不隆也，壽陽一挫而身名俱損。此所謂有其名而無其實者也。

何謂蚤負不美之名而晚令者？王湛名爲癡，不爲從子王濟所禮，一日濟與論《易》，多出濟意表，復就蟻封盤馬，湛回策如縈，而濟馬踣，濟乃歎曰：「家有
translation_en:
… the Way of Shang flourished. Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮 was a recluse of Nanyang 南陽; just when he hugged his knees and chanted, he had already set his ambitions on Guan Zhong 管仲 and Yue Yi 樂毅, and when he rose after three visits, he subsequently established the merit of the tripartite division, and the fiery mandate of Han prospered once again. These are what are called those whose reputation and reality correspond to each other.

What is meant by those who possess the reality without the reputation? When Mao Sui 毛遂 recommended himself to the Lord of Pingyuan 平原, all the retainers laughed at him; yet when he showed his mettle and forged an alliance for aid from powerful Chu 楚, the siege of Handan 邯鄲 was immediately relieved. When Han Xin 韓信 depended on a washerwoman for food, even the youths insulted him; yet when he ascended the altar and mapped out the strategy to corner Xiang Yu 項羽, the army at Gaixia 垓下 was ultimately annihilated. These are what are called those who possess the reality without the reputation.

What is meant by those who possess the reputation without the reality? When Ma Su 馬謖 was in Shu 蜀, he once submitted a memorandum to Kongming 孔明 [Zhuge Liang] saying: "Attacking cities is inferior, attacking hearts is superior; fighting with weapons is inferior, fighting with hearts is superior." The argument was not unmagnificent, yet with a single defeat at Jieting 街亭, he could not preserve his own head. When Yin Hao 殷浩 was in Jin 晉, Xie Shang 謝尚 and others said to one another: "If Yuanyuan 淵源 [Yin Hao] does not rise to office, what will become of the common people?" divining the rise and fall of the region east of the Yangtze by his taking or declining office. His prestige was not unexalted, yet with a single setback at Shouyang 壽陽, both his person and his reputation were ruined. These are what are called those who possess the reputation without the reality.

What is meant by those who early on bore an unfavorable reputation yet proved admirable later in life? Wang Zhan 王湛 had a reputation for idiocy and was not treated with courtesy by his nephew Wang Ji 王濟. One day Ji discussed the Classic of Changes (Yi 易) with him, and much of what Zhan said went beyond Ji's expectations. When they further wheeled their horses around an ant mound, Zhan turned his whip as smoothly as coiling thread while Ji's horse stumbled, whereupon Ji sighed and said: "My family has had a …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
名士三十年而不知魏舒名爲鈍不爲其
叔魏衡所知後爲鍾毓長史毓毎集僚佐
射舒爲點籌偶朋人不足以舒滿數舒發
無不中毓乃謝曰吾之不足以盡卿有如
此射此所謂蚤負不美之名而晚令者也
何謂始被貪濁之名而終著高操者王廙
爲宛陵令頗營家具王導以書戒之後乃
改厲所至以清德聞蕭憺爲雍州刺史頗
有賄聲梁武以人間歌謠示之後乃折節
===
所歷以善政稱此所謂始被貪濁之名而
終著高操者也何謂初陷兇惡之名而後
復改行者周處委身盜賊納父老之諫而
自新迄成名士賈淑侵暴邑里感郭泰之
言而自改竟爲善人此所謂初陷兇惡之
名而後復改行者也何謂陽附君子之名
而陰實爲小人者豎刁之事桓公也附於
忠豎牛之蠱叔孫也附於孝郅都寧成之
治郡也附於守職張湯王溫舒之鞫獄也
punctuated:
名士三十年而不知！」魏舒名爲鈍，不爲其叔魏衡所知。後爲鍾毓長史，毓毎集僚佐射，舒爲點籌。偶朋人不足，以舒滿數，舒發無不中。毓乃謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿，有如此射！」此所謂蚤負不美之名而晚令者也。
何謂始被貪濁之名而終著高操者？王廙爲宛陵令，頗營家具，王導以書戒之，後乃改厲，所至以清德聞。蕭憺爲雍州刺史，頗有賄聲，梁武以人間歌謠示之，後乃折節，所歷以善政稱。此所謂始被貪濁之名而終著高操者也。
何謂初陷兇惡之名而後復改行者？周處委身盜賊，納父老之諫而自新，迄成名士；賈淑侵暴邑里，感郭泰之言而自改，竟爲善人。此所謂初陷兇惡之名而後復改行者也。
何謂陽附君子之名而陰實爲小人者？豎刁之事桓公也，附於忠；豎牛之蠱叔孫也，附於孝；郅都、寧成之治郡也，附於守職；張湯、王溫舒之鞫獄也，
translation_en:
…a famous gentleman for thirty years, and I did not know it!” Wei Shu 魏舒 had a reputation for being dull-witted and was not appreciated by his uncle Wei Heng 魏衡. Later, he served as Chief Administrator (zhangshi) to Zhong Yu 鍾毓. Whenever Yu gathered his staff and subordinates for archery, Shu kept the tally. On one occasion, when there were not enough companions to form the pairings, Shu was used to fill out the number, and every arrow Shu shot hit the mark. Yu then apologized, saying, “My failure to fully gauge your talents is just like this archery match!” This is what is meant by bearing an unfavorable reputation early on yet achieving a fine name later in life.

What is meant by first suffering a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately demonstrating lofty integrity? When Wang Yi 王廙 served as Magistrate (ling) of Wanling 宛陵, he busied himself considerably with acquiring household furnishings. After Wang Dao 王導 admonished him in a letter, he reformed and exerted himself, becoming known for pure virtue wherever he went. When Xiao Dan 蕭憺 served as Regional Inspector (cishi) of Yongzhou 雍州, he had a considerable reputation for taking bribes. After Emperor Wu of Liang 梁武帝 showed him the folk songs circulating among the people, he curbed his behavior, and throughout the posts he subsequently held he was praised for good governance. This is what is meant by first suffering a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately demonstrating lofty integrity.

What is meant by initially falling into a reputation for fierceness and villainy yet later reforming one’s conduct? Zhou Chu 周處 gave himself over to banditry, but upon accepting the remonstrances of the local elders he renewed himself and eventually became a famous gentleman. Jia Shu 賈淑 tyrannized his hometown and neighborhood, but moved by the words of Guo Tai 郭泰 he reformed himself and ultimately became a good man. This is what is meant by initially falling into a reputation for fierceness and villainy yet later reforming one’s conduct.

What is meant by outwardly attaching oneself to the reputation of a gentleman while secretly being a petty man in reality? Attendant Diao’s 豎刁 service to Duke Huan 桓公 borrowed the guise of loyalty; Attendant Niu’s 豎牛 bewitching of Shusun 叔孫 borrowed the guise of filial piety; Zhi Du’s 郅都 and Ning Cheng’s 寧成 governance of their commanderies borrowed the guise of fulfilling one’s official duties; Zhang Tang’s 張湯 and Wang Wenshu’s 王溫舒trying of legal cases…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
附於執法鄧通之柔媚公孫弘之反覆也
附於恭順此所謂陽附君子之名而陰實
爲小人者也何謂外近小人之名而中實
爲君子者子貢之存魯也近於詐弦高之
却秦也近於誕子囊之全楚也近於畏敵
李牧之防邊也近於縱寇蕭何之請苑也
近於賈譽田叔之焚獄書也近於鬻法狄
仁傑之徘徊女后也近於貪位此所謂外
近小人之名而中實爲君子者也夫名實
===
之相副者人主每憚其名而不樂近之有
其實而無其名者人主每略其實而遺之
有其名而無其實者人主每慕其名而悅
之有蚤蒙不美之名而晚令者人主每因
其蚤而棄之有始被貪濁之名而終著高
操者人主每追其始而斥之有初陷兇惡
之名而後更改行者人主每計其初而絶
之有陽附君子之名者人主不察其陰而
日親之有外近小人之名者人主不探其
punctuated: 附於執法；鄧通之柔媚、公孫弘之反覆也，附於恭順。此所謂陽附君子之名，而陰實爲小人者也。何謂外近小人之名，而中實爲君子者？子貢之存魯也，近於詐；弦高之却秦也，近於誕；子囊之全楚也，近於畏敵；李牧之防邊也，近於縱寇；蕭何之請苑也，近於賈譽；田叔之焚獄書也，近於鬻法；狄仁傑之徘徊女后也，近於貪位。此所謂外近小人之名，而中實爲君子者也。夫名實之相副者，人主每憚其名而不樂近之；有其實而無其名者，人主每略其實而遺之；有其名而無其實者，人主每慕其名而悅之；有蚤蒙不美之名而晚令者，人主每因其蚤而棄之；有始被貪濁之名而終著高操者，人主每追其始而斥之；有初陷兇惡之名而後更改行者，人主每計其初而絶之；有陽附君子之名者，人主不察其陰而日親之；有外近小人之名者，人主不探其
translation_en:
…attached itself to strict enforcement of the law; the compliant flattery of Deng Tong 鄧通 and the duplicity of Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 attached themselves to respectful obedience. These are what are called outwardly attaching oneself to the reputation of a gentleman while secretly being a petty man in reality. What is meant by those who outwardly come close to the reputation of a petty man while inwardly being a gentleman in reality? Zigong's 子貢 preservation of Lu came close to deceit; Xian Gao's 弦高 repelling of Qin came close to fabrication; Zinang's 子囊 safeguarding of Chu came close to fearing the enemy; Li Mu's 李牧 defense of the frontier came close to indulging raiders; Xiao He's 蕭何 petitioning for the imperial parklands came close to buying popular praise; Tian Shu's 田叔 burning of the trial records came close to subverting the law; Di Renjie's 狄仁傑 lingering at the court of a female ruler came close to coveting office. These are what are called outwardly coming close to the reputation of a petty man while inwardly being a gentleman in reality.

Now, as for those whose reputation and reality correspond to one another, the ruler often dreads their reputation and does not take pleasure in drawing near to them; as for those who possess the reality without the reputation, the ruler often overlooks their reality and passes them over; as for those who possess the reputation without the reality, the ruler often admires their reputation and delights in them; as for those who early on suffered an unsavory reputation yet proved admirable in later life, the ruler often casts them aside on account of their early years; as for those who initially bore a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately displayed lofty integrity, the ruler often harks back to their beginnings and rejects them; as for those who at first fell into a reputation for fierceness and wickedness yet later reformed their conduct, the ruler often reckons their initial faults and cuts them off; as for those who outwardly attach themselves to the reputation of a gentleman, the ruler fails to examine what they do in secret and grows closer to them by the day; as for those who outwardly come close to the reputation of a petty man, the ruler fails to probe their…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中而日疎之如此則所用非所材所材非
所用賢否倒置而真似淆亂矣自非人主
神識中涵獨見獨明幾何不徇名而失實
耶何謂獨見見在外者也日月之光也而
浮雲翳之則雲之外有遺燭矣燈火之燄
也而薄帷鄣之則帷之外有遺照矣何謂
獨明明在中者也鑑至空也而形不可欺
以妍媸焉衡至平也而物不可欺以輕重
焉屏嗜慾慎起居則內境清而人主之獨
===
明著矣遠佞倖納諫諍則外蔽撤而人主
之獨見昭矣由是出其獨見獨明以辨天
下之材則名實之相副者必庸而鼎鉉之
佐皆伊葛矣有其實而無其名者必採而
專對仗鉞之臣皆毛韓矣有其名而無其
實者必遠而虛談如馬謖殷浩者不至僨
事矣蚤蒙不美而晚令者必收而隱德如
王湛魏舒者不以蚤而棄矣始被貪濁而
終著高操者必錄而遷善如王述蕭恪者
punctuated: 中而日疎之。如此，則所用非所材，所材非所用，賢否倒置而真似淆亂矣。自非人主神識中涵，獨見獨明，幾何不徇名而失實耶？何謂獨見？見在外者也。日月之光也，而浮雲翳之，則雲之外有遺燭矣；燈火之燄也，而薄帷鄣之，則帷之外有遺照矣。何謂獨明？明在中者也。鑑至空也，而形不可欺以妍媸焉；衡至平也，而物不可欺以輕重焉。屏嗜慾、慎起居，則內境清而人主之獨明著矣；遠佞倖、納諫諍，則外蔽撤而人主之獨見昭矣。由是出其獨見、獨明以辨天下之材，則名實之相副者必庸，而鼎鉉之佐皆伊、葛矣；有其實而無其名者必採，而專對仗鉞之臣皆毛、韓矣；有其名而無其實者必遠，而虛談如馬謖、殷浩者不至僨事矣；蚤蒙不美而晚令者必收，而隱德如王湛、魏舒者不以蚤而棄矣；始被貪濁而終著高操者必錄，而遷善如王述、蕭恪者
translation_en: … what is within and distances himself from them day by day. When this is the case, those who are employed are not those who have talent, and those who have talent are not those who are employed; the worthy and the unworthy are inverted, and the genuine and the specious are confounded. Unless the ruler harbors spiritual insight within himself, possessing independent vision and independent clarity, how close he comes to pursuing reputation and losing sight of reality! What is meant by independent vision? Vision pertains to what is external. Take the light of the sun and moon: when floating clouds obscure it, beyond the clouds there are places left unlit. Take the flame of a lamp: when a thin curtain screens it, beyond the curtain there are places left unilluminated. What is meant by independent clarity? Clarity pertains to what is internal. A mirror is utterly void of preconception, and thus forms cannot deceive it as to beauty or ugliness; a balance is utterly level, and thus objects cannot deceive it as to weight. When he puts aside desires and is cautious in his daily conduct, his inner realm becomes pure, and the ruler's independent clarity becomes manifest. When he keeps flatterers and favorites at a distance and accepts remonstrance, external obstructions are removed, and the ruler's independent vision becomes bright. When from this basis he brings forth his independent vision and independent clarity to distinguish the talents of the realm, then those whose reputation and reality correspond will surely be employed, and the chief ministers of state will all be like Yi Yin 伊尹 and Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮; those who possess the reality without the reputation will surely be selected, and envoys who can respond on their own initiative and generals who wield the battle-axe of command will all be like Mao Sui 毛遂 and Han Xin 韓信; those who possess the reputation without the reality will surely be kept at a distance, and empty talkers like Ma Su 馬謖 and Yin Hao 殷浩 will not end up ruining affairs; those who early on suffered anunfavorable reputation but proved admirable later in life will surely be taken in, and men of hidden virtue like Wang Zhan 王湛 and Wei Shu 魏舒 will not be discarded on account of their early years; those who were at first tarnished by a reputation for greed and corruption but in the end displayed lofty integrity will surely be enrolled, and men who reformed themselves toward goodness like Wang Shu 王述 and Xiao Ke 蕭恪 …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不以始而斥矣初陷兇惡而後更改行者
必察而自新如周處賈淑者不以初而絕
矣陰爲小人者必疎而豎刁之徒不在左
右矣中爲君子者必親而子貢之流並見
任使矣如此則所用皆真材而似材者無
因而倖進名不浮其實實必符其名亦猶
養由基之於射雖百發無弗中矣造父之
於御雖千里無弗至矣抑愚有說焉辨天
下之材非難使天下之材樂爲吾用爲難
===
是故愛養不可不至也信任不可不專也
微眚不可不宥也宏美不可不錄也陳軫
貴於魏惠子曰夫楊横樹之即生倒樹之
即生折而樹之又生然使十人樹之而一
人拔之無生楊矣子雖工自樹而欲去子
者衆子必危矣愚觀任事之臣竭力以奉
社稷之役一罹讒口則人主爲之投杼故
有十人之譽不勝一夫之毀是生楊之說
也是故愛養不可不至也王登薦士於襄
punctuated:
不以始而斥矣；初陷兇惡而後更改行者必察，而自新如周處、賈淑者，不以初而絕矣；陰爲小人者必疎，而豎刁之徒不在左右矣；中爲君子者必親，而子貢之流並見任使矣。如此，則所用皆真材，而似材者無因而倖進；名不浮其實，實必符其名，亦猶養由基之於射，雖百發無弗中矣；造父之於御，雖千里無弗至矣。
抑愚有說焉：辨天下之材非難，使天下之材樂爲吾用爲難。是故愛養不可不至也，信任不可不專也，微眚不可不宥也，宏美不可不錄也。陳軫貴於魏，惠子曰：「夫楊，横樹之即生，倒樹之即生，折而樹之又生。然使十人樹之，而一人拔之，無生楊矣。子雖工自樹，而欲去子者衆，子必危矣。」愚觀任事之臣，竭力以奉社稷之役，一罹讒口，則人主爲之投杼。故有十人之譽，不勝一夫之毀，是生楊之說也。是故愛養不可不至也。王登薦士於襄…
translation_en:
…will not be rejected because of their early days; those who initially fell into wickedness and later reformed their conduct will surely be discerned, and men who renewed themselves like Zhou Chu 周處 and Jia Shu 賈淑 will not be cut off because of their beginnings; those who are secretly petty men will surely be kept at a distance, and the likes of Shu Diao 豎刁 will not be at the ruler's side; those who are gentlemen at heart will surely be held close, and the likes of Zigong 子貢 will all be employed in service. When it is thus, all who are employed will be genuine talents, and those who merely resemble talent will have no means to advance by luck; reputation will not exceed reality, and reality will surely match reputation. It will be just like Yang Youji 養由基 in archery, who, though shooting a hundred times, never fails to hit the mark; or Zaofu 造父 in charioteering, who, though going a thousand li, never fails to arrive.

Yet I, in my simplicity, have a further point to make: to distinguish the talents of the world is not difficult; what is difficult is to make the talents of the world glad to be of use to us. Therefore, cherishing and nurturing them cannot be anything less than utmost; trusting and employing them cannot be anything less than undivided; minor faults cannot go unpardoned; and great merits cannot go unrecorded. When Chen Zhen 陳軫 was honored in Wei 魏, Huizi 惠子 said to him: "Now as for the willow: plant it horizontally and it grows, plant it upside down and it grows, break off a branch and plant it and still it grows. Yet if you have ten men planting it and one man pulling it up, no willow will survive. Though you are skillful at establishing yourself, those who wish to remove you are many, so you will surely be in danger." I observe that when ministers who shoulder responsibilities exhaust their strength in the service of the altars of soil and grain, once they suffer from slanderous mouths, the ruler drops the shuttle in alarm on that account. Thus the praise of ten men cannot overcome the detraction of a single fellow—this is the principle of the growing willow. Therefore, cherishing and nurturing them cannot be anything less than utmost. Wang Deng 王登 recommended scholars to Xiang…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
主襄主以為中大夫相室諫曰中大夫重
列也今無功而授君其耳而未之目耶襄
主曰我取登既耳而目之矣登之所取又
耳而目之是耳目人終無已也愚觀在事
之臣察其未宜於民不逮三年量移之可
也有罪亟譴斥之可也既以為賢而任之
矣即宜推心置腹令展布四體詎宜屬耳
目於道路而陰裭骫之是賢士程行於不
肖智者決策於愚人况媚嫉者忌其垂成
===
闒茸者幸其俱敗使有志之士疾首而事
事是耳目無已之說也是故信任不可不
專也孟孫獵得麑使秦西巴載之持歸其
母隨之啼秦西巴不忍而予之孟孫歸而
求麑弗得怒而逐之居三月復召為其子
傅曰夫不忍麑又安忍吾子乎愚觀言議
之臣一掛當時之網則執筆者輒游意法
之外而緣飾之務快當事者之心或返編
氓或竄士伍即使無罪而議調亦復優游
punctuated:
主，襄主以為中大夫。相室諫曰：「中大夫，重列也。今無功而授，君其耳而未之目耶？」襄主曰：「我取登，既耳而目之矣；登之所取，又耳而目之，是耳目人終無已也。」愚觀在事之臣，察其未宜於民，不逮三年，量移之可也；有罪，亟譴斥之可也。既以為賢而任之矣，即宜推心置腹，令展布四體，詎宜屬耳目於道路而陰裭骫之？是賢士程行於不肖，智者決策於愚人。况媚嫉者忌其垂成，闒茸者幸其俱敗，使有志之士疾首而事事，是耳目無已之說也。是故信任不可不專也。
孟孫獵得麑，使秦西巴載之持歸，其母隨之啼，秦西巴不忍而予之。孟孫歸而求麑弗得，怒而逐之。居三月，復召為其子傅，曰：「夫不忍麑，又安忍吾子乎？」愚觀言議之臣，一掛當時之網，則執筆者輒游意法之外而緣飾之，務快當事者之心，或返編氓，或竄士伍；即使無罪而議調，亦復優游
translation_en:
… [Lord Xiang], and Lord Xiang appointed them as Grand Masters of the Palace. His house steward remonstrated, saying: "Grand Master of the Palace is an important rank. Now you bestow it upon men of no merit—have you merely heard of them with your ears without inspecting them with your own eyes?" Lord Xiang replied: "When I selected [Wang] Deng, I had already heard of him with my ears and inspected him with my eyes. If for those whom Deng selects I must again hear of them with my ears and inspect them with my eyes, then examining men by ear and eye will never end!" Looking at the officials currently serving in office, I observe that if upon inspection someone proves unsuited to the people, it is permissible to transfer him appropriately before three years are up; if he commits an offense, it is permissible to reprimand and dismiss him promptly. Yet once a man has been deemed worthy and entrusted with office, one ought to place complete confidence in him and allow him to stretch out his four limbs and act freely. How could it be proper to attach ears and eyes along the roads and covertly strip or bend him [? 裭骫]? That would mean having worthy men's conduct measured by the unworthy, and wise men's policies decided by fools. Moreover, the jealous resent a work nearing completion, and the mediocre rejoice when everything fails, causing men of aspiration to attend to affairs with aching heads. This is the very lesson of "examining by ear and eye without end." Therefore, trust and delegation cannot but be undivided.

Mengsun caught a fawn while hunting and had Qin Xiba carry it home in his cart. Its mother followed behind crying, and Qin Xiba, unable to bear it, gave the fawn back to her. When Mengsun returned and asked for the fawn without getting it, he was furious and drove Qin Xiba away. After three months, however, he recalled him to serve as tutor to his son, saying: "The man could not bear to hurt a fawn; how then could he bear to hurt my son?" Looking at the officials who offer counsel and criticism, I observe that once they are caught in the net of the times, those who wield the brush routinely let their intentions roam beyond the law and dress up the charges, striving to gratify the hearts of those in power. Some are reduced to commoners on the household registers, while others are banished to the military ranks. Even when they are innocent and recommended for transfer, they are still left to linger idly in …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
散地困抑而不獲伸孟孫之召秦西巴可
想也是故微眚不可不宥也卞和得玉璞
於荆山獻之厲王玉工曰石也以爲誑而
刖其左足武王立又獻之玉工曰石也以
爲誑而刖其右足文王立和乃抱璞而泣
於荆山之下不敢獻王使理其璞而得寶
焉愚觀疎逖之臣寧無懷瑾握瑜處隱約
而靡由自見者乎微左右爲之先容卒按
劒相盻而莫之收矣卞和之泣玉可鑒也
===
是故宏美不可不錄也人主能盡此四者
而天下之材不樂爲吾用者否也此鄙生
一得之愚敢以效之執事執事將無塵飯
塗羹其言乎
第三問
葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳批究極音律沿革之故殆
無遺旨即牙曠復生當爲鼓掌取之
同考試官教諭陳批經生類鮮究心於樂者
punctuated:
散地，困抑而不獲伸。孟孫之召秦西巴，可想也。是故微眚不可不宥也。卞和得玉璞於荆山，獻之厲王。玉工曰：「石也。」以爲誑而刖其左足。武王立，又獻之。玉工曰：「石也。」以爲誑而刖其右足。文王立，和乃抱璞而泣於荆山之下，不敢獻。王使理其璞而得寶焉。愚觀疎逖之臣，寧無懷瑾握瑜、處隱約而靡由自見者乎？微左右爲之先容，卒按劒相盻而莫之收矣。卞和之泣玉，可鑒也。是故宏美不可不錄也。人主能盡此四者，而天下之材不樂爲吾用者，否也。此鄙生一得之愚，敢以效之執事。執事將無塵飯塗羹其言乎？
第三問
葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳批：究極音律沿革之故，殆無遺旨。即牙、曠復生，當爲鼓掌。取之。
同考試官教諭陳批：經生類鮮究心於樂者，
translation_en:
…sinecure posts, frustrated and suppressed without being able to advance. One may well reflect on Mengsun's recalling of Qin Xiba. Therefore, minor faults must not go unpardoned.

Bian He Bian He 卞和 obtained a piece of unpolished jade from Mount Jing and presented it to King Li. The jade carver said, "It is a stone." Taking him for a deceiver, the king had his left foot amputated. When King Wu ascended the throne, he presented it again. The jade carver said, "It is a stone." Taking him for a deceiver, the king had his right foot amputated. When King Wen ascended the throne, He clasped the unpolished jade and wept at the foot of Mount Jing, not daring to present it. The king ordered the unpolished stone to be dressed, and thus obtained the treasure. In my humble view, among distant and estranged officials, how could there not be those who cherish fine jade-like virtues in their bosoms, dwelling in obscurity and poverty with no means to make themselves known? Without close attendants to introduce and recommend them beforehand, in the end people will grasp their swords and glare at them in suspicion, and no one will take them in. Bian He's weeping over the jade serves as a mirror. Therefore, grand excellence must not go unrecorded.

If a ruler of men can fully practice these four principles, would it ever be that the talents of the realm would not gladly serve us? Never! This is the humble insight of a rustic student, which I venture to offer to Your Excellency. Will Your Excellency not treat these words as mere dust-rice and mud-soup?

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而子獨條分縷析動有証據徵博物矣
考試官敎諭程批詞氣優柔治世之音
考試官敎諭周批綜貫古今深於樂者也
昔太史公爲律書其始不言律而言兵不
言兵之用而言兵之偃及言偃兵而於漢
之文帝獨加詳焉以爲天下富庶百姓嬉
遊此和樂之本也嗚呼若太史公者蓋深
達制律之意者哉六代之樂自咸池而下
靡不由此明問謂非徒作誠然乎漢以來
===
文始之舞卽韶樂也五行之舞卽武樂也
二樂終漢世不壞至魏而亂至晉而亡自
是而古樂不復存矣夫樂之用不外乎聲音
律呂通典云以子聲比正聲則正聲爲倍
以正聲比子聲則子聲爲半如仲呂之管
長六寸五分有奇上生黃鐘三分益一不
及正律九寸之數但得八寸七分有奇以

In antiquity, when the Grand Historian composed the "Treatise on Pitch-Pipes" (Lüshu), at the outset he did not speak of pitch-pipes, but spoke of military arms; and he did not speak of the use of arms, but of the laying down of arms. When he came to speak of laying down arms, he dwelt in particular detail upon Emperor Wen of the Han, holding that when the realm is prosperous and populous and the common people disport themselves in peace, this is the foundation of harmonious music. Alas! A man like the Grand Historian truly grasped the deep intent behind the institution of pitch-pipes! The music of the Six Dynasties of antiquity, from the Pool of Totality (Xianchi) downward, without exception stemmed from this. When the brilliant question states that it was not created in vain, is this not truly so? From the Han onward, the Dance of Literary Inception (Wenshi) was none other than the Shao music, and the Dance of the Five Phases (Wuxing) was none other than the Wu music. These two musical dances remained intact throughout the Han era, fell into disorder in the Wei, and perished in the Jin; from that time forth, ancient music no longer survived. Now, the application of music goes no further than tones, notes, and the yang and yin pitch-pipes (lülü). The Comprehensive Canons (Tongdian) states: "When a derivative pitch (zisheng) is compared to a standard pitch (zhengsheng), the standard pitch is double; when a standard pitch is compared to a derivative pitch, the derivative pitch is half." For instance, the pipe of Zhonglü is six inches and five fen plus a fraction in length; when it generates Huangzhong upward by adding one-third, it does not reach the standard pitch-pipe length of nine inches, yielding only eight inches and seven fen plus a fraction, which serves as the altered pitch-pipe (bianlü) of Huangzhong; halving this yields four inches and three fen plus a fraction, which serves as its derivative pitch. title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
生應鐘比于正音故爲和應鐘生蕤賓不
比于正音故爲謬蓋五音相生至于角位
則其數六十有四隔八下生當得宮前一
位以爲變宮又自變宮隔八上生當得徵
前一位其數五十有六以爲變徵變者與
正比則爲和變者與正不比則爲謬此音
有和謬之略也漢書律歷志天地人及四
時爲七始此合而言之也又以黃鐘爲天
始林鐘爲地始太簇爲人始此分而言之
===
也蓋黃鐘居子爲天統林鐘居未衝丑爲
地統太簇居寅爲人統故爲三始姑洗爲
春蕤賓爲夏南呂爲秋應鐘爲冬以三合
四是謂七始此三始七始之略也以七音
因十二律爲八十四調除二變聲不得爲
調以五因十二則爲六十調然二變不調
則冬夏聲闕四時不備蔡子之說非而鄭
譯之議是也此六十調與八十四調之略
也以徑象言之黃鐘長九寸爲乾林鐘長
punctuated: 生應鐘，比于正音，故爲和；應鐘生蕤賓，不比于正音，故爲謬。」蓋五音相生，至于角位，則其數六十有四；隔八下生，當得宮前一位，以爲變宮；又自變宮隔八上生，當得徵前一位，其數五十有六，以爲變徵。變者與正比，則爲和；變者與正不比，則爲謬。此音有和謬之略也。《漢書·律歷志》：「天、地、人及四時爲七始。」此合而言之也。又以黃鐘爲天始，林鐘爲地始，太簇爲人始，此分而言之也。蓋黃鐘居子爲天統，林鐘居未衝丑爲地統，太簇居寅爲人統，故爲三始；姑洗爲春，蕤賓爲夏，南呂爲秋，應鐘爲冬，以三合四，是謂七始。此三始、七始之略也。以七音因十二律，爲八十四調；除二變聲不得爲調，以五因十二，則爲六十調。然二變不調，則冬夏聲闕，四時不備，蔡子之說非，而鄭譯之議是也。此六十調與八十四調之略也。以徑象言之，黃鐘長九寸爲乾，林鐘長

In general, as the five tones mutually generate one another, when reaching the position of Jue, its number is sixty-four. Generating downward across eight positions yields the position one step before Gong, which serves as Altered Gong (biangong); and generating upward across eight positions from Altered Gong yields the position one step before Zhi, whose number is fifty-six, which serves as Altered Zhi (bianzhi). When an altered tone accords with the regular tones, it is harmonious; when an altered tone does not accord with the regular tones, it is discordant. This is an outline of harmonious and discordant tones. The Treatise on Pitch-Pipes and the Calendar in the History of the Han (Hanshu lulizhi) states: "Heaven, Earth, Man, and the four seasons constitute the Seven Beginnings (qishi)." This is speaking of them collectively. It also takes Huangzhong as the Beginning of Heaven, Linzhong as the Beginning of Earth, and Ta簇 (Taicu) as the Beginning of Man; this is speaking of them separately. Specifically, Huangzhong resides in Zi as the Cosmic Governance of Heaven (tiantong), Linzhong resides in Wei—opposing Chou—as the Cosmic Governance of Earth (ditong), and Taicu resides in Yin as the Cosmic Governance of Man (rentong); thus they constitute the Three Beginnings (sanshi). Guxian represents spring, Ruibin represents summer, Nanlü represents autumn, and Yingzhong represents winter; combining the three with the four is called the Seven Beginnings. This is an outline of the Three Beginnings and Seven Beginnings. Multiplying the seven tones by the twelve pitch-pipes produces eighty-four modes (diao); excluding the two altered tones as incapable of serving as modes and multiplying the five tones by the twelve pitch-pipes produces sixty modes. Yet if the two altered tones are not used for modes, the sounds of winter and summer are lacking and the four seasons are incomplete; thus Master Cai's [Cai Yuanding's] theory is mistaken, while Zheng Yi's argument is correct. This is an outline of the sixty modes and eighty-four modes. title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
六寸爲坤乃邵子皇極經世聲起于多乾
之甲也音起于古乾之子也此理之可通
于易者也以娶妻生子言之黃鍾爲陽大
呂爲陰猶甲子之娶乙丑皆同位者也黃
鍾之生林鍾林鍾之生太蔟猶甲子金之
生庚辰金皆隔八者也乃沈重鍾律議用
京房之術求之得三百六十律當一朞之
日隨日建律依次運行當日者以次爲宮
而商徵以次從焉此義之有符于曆者也
===
樂必用五音然周禮三大祭皆無商音說
者謂周德木也故祭鬼神之樂去金宋元
諸臣建言亦謂唐土德王請加商調去角
調是卽周禮之意云耳我
朝以土德王
太祖高皇帝初作洪武正韻聲起于東從角也
後見禮部韻會而遵用之不起于東而起
于公此則從宮矣豈非深達造化者哉律
止于十二是矣然十二者律之本聲而四
punctuated:
六寸爲坤。乃邵子《皇極經世》，聲起于「多」，乾之甲也；音起于「古」，乾之子也。此理之可通于《易》者也。以「娶妻生子」言之：黃鍾爲陽，大呂爲陰，猶甲子之娶乙丑，皆同位者也；黃鍾之生林鍾，林鍾之生太蔟，猶甲子金之生庚辰金，皆隔八者也。乃沈重《鍾律議》用京房之術求之，得三百六十律，當一朞之日，隨日建律，依次運行，當日者以次爲宮，而商、徵以次從焉。此義之有符于曆者也。
樂必用五音，然《周禮》三大祭皆無商音。說者謂周德木也，故祭鬼神之樂去金。宋、元諸臣建言，亦謂唐土德王，請加商調、去角調，是卽《周禮》之意云耳。我朝以土德王，太祖高皇帝初作《洪武正韻》，聲起于「東」，從角也；後見《禮部韻會》而遵用之，不起于「東」而起于「公」，此則從宮矣，豈非深達造化者哉？
律止于十二，是矣。然十二者，律之本聲，而四

Moreover, in Master Shao’s [Shao Yong 邵雍] Book of Supreme World Ordering Principles (Huangji jingshi), the vocalic finals begin with “duo,” corresponding to the Jia stem of Qian, while the consonantal initials begin with “gu,” corresponding to the Zi branch of Qian. This is how the principle communicates with the Book of Changes (Yi). Speaking in terms of “taking a wife and begetting sons”: Yellow Bell (Huangzhong) is Yang and Great Regulator (Dalü) is Yin, just as Jiazi takes Yichou as wife—both occupy the same position. Yellow Bell begets Forest Bell (Linzhong), and Forest Bell begets Great Cluster (Taicu), just as the metal of Jiazi begets the metal of Gengchen—both are separated by eight positions. Furthermore, Shen Zhong’s Discourse on Bell Pitch-Pipes (Zhonglü yi) used the technique of Jing Fang to calculate them, obtaining three hundred and sixty pitch-pipes corresponding to the days of a full year; the pitch-pipes are established day by day and circulate in sequence, with the pipe of the current day serving in turn as the gong note, and shang and zhi following it in order. This is how their meaning tallies with the calendar.

Music must employ all five tones, yet in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) the three great sacrifices all lack the shang tone. Commentators say that the virtue of the Zhou dynasty was Wood, and therefore the music for sacrificing to ghosts and spirits omitted Metal [the element corresponding to shang]. When various officials of the Song and Yuan dynasties submitted proposals, they likewise said that the Tang ruled by the virtue of Earth, and requested adding the shang mode and removing the jue mode [corresponding to Wood]; this was simply following the intent of the Rites of Zhou. Our Dynasty rules by the virtue of Earth. When Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao [the Hongwu Emperor] first compiled the Correct Rhymes of the Hongwu Era (Hongwu zhengyun), the sounds began with “dong,” which followed the jue tone; later, seeing the Collection of Rhymes of the Ministry of Rites (Libu yunhui), he adopted and followed it, starting not with “dong” but with “gong,” thereby following the gong tone [corresponding to Earth]. Was this not a profound grasp of the workings of nature?

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者應聲也本聲重大爲君爲父應聲輕清
爲臣爲子故四聲曰清聲卽夾鐘大呂黃
鐘太簇之應也苟不用四清聲是有本而
無應矣我
朝泠謙建議用四清聲故編鐘編磬皆爲十
六豈非洞達音律者哉詩稱定之方中謂
測日景以辨方也土圭之法祖冲之之論
備矣然候氣者使按日景之子午以布律
則氣必不應何也天氣微偏于左地氣微
===
偏于右所謂不參差則不能生物者也故
土圭測日景常在子午之中此天之正位
也以鍼定南北常在丙午壬子之中此地
之正位也故冬至置黃鐘之律于壬子之
中夏至置林鐘之律于丙午之中然後飛
灰應律今元定乃欲一室之中多截管以
候黃鐘夫差之毫釐氣卽不應而顧欲多
埋律管豈非臆說哉黃鐘起于子之一以
三倍之歷十二辰而終于亥之一十七萬
punctuated: 者，應聲也。本聲重大，爲君、爲父；應聲輕清，爲臣、爲子。故四聲曰「清聲」，卽夾鐘、大呂、黃鐘、太簇之應也。苟不用四清聲，是有本而無應矣。我朝泠謙建議用四清聲，故編鐘、編磬皆爲十六，豈非洞達音律者哉！《詩》稱「定之方中」，謂測日景以辨方也。土圭之法，祖冲之之論備矣。然候氣者使按日景之子午以布律，則氣必不應，何也？天氣微偏于左，地氣微偏于右，所謂不參差則不能生物者也。故土圭測日景，常在子午之中，此天之正位也；以鍼定南北，常在丙午、壬子之中，此地之正位也。故冬至置黃鐘之律于壬子之中，夏至置林鐘之律于丙午之中，然後飛灰應律。今元定乃欲一室之中多截管以候黃鐘，夫差之毫釐，氣卽不應，而顧欲多埋律管，豈非臆說哉！黃鐘起于子之一，以三倍之，歷十二辰而終于亥之一十七萬

… [the four] are the responsive tones (yingsheng). The fundamental tones are heavy and grand, acting as sovereign and father; the responsive tones are light and clear, acting as minister and son. Therefore, the four tones are called the "clear tones" (qingsheng), which are namely the responses to Jiazhong, Dalü, Huangzhong, and Taicu. If the four clear tones are not used, then there are fundamentals without responses. In our dynasty, Ling Qian 泠謙 proposed using the four clear tones, and consequently both the chime bells (bianzhong) and chime stones (bianqing) were set at sixteen in number—was he not someone with a thorough grasp of musical pitches!

The Book of Odes (Shi) speaks of "When Ding was at the zenith" (Ding zhi fang zhong), which refers to measuring the sun's shadow in order to determine the cardinal directions. As for the method of the gnomon (tugui), Zu Chongzhi's 祖冲之 discourse on it is comprehensive. However, if those who watch for the seasonal ethers (houqi) were to arrange the pitch-pipes according to the north-south (zi-wu) axis determined by the sun's shadow, the ethers would certainly fail to respond. Why is this? Theether of Heaven inclines slightly to the left, while the ether of Earth inclines slightly to the right; this is what is meant by the saying that without irregularity, living things cannot be generated. Therefore, when the gnomon measures the sun's shadow, it always falls along the center of zi and wu—this is the true position of Heaven. When a magnetic needle is used to determine south and north, it always falls along the center between bing-wu and ren-zi—this is the true position of Earth. Thus, at the winter solstice, one places the Huangzhong pitch-pipe at the center of ren-zi, and at the summer solstice, one places the Linzhong pitch-pipe at the center of bing-wu; only then will the flying ashes respond to the pitch-pipes. Yet [Cai] Yuanding 蔡元定 wished to cut numerous pipes within a single chamber in order to watch for the Huangzhong ether. Now, if there is a discrepancy of even the slightest fraction, the ether will not respond; yet to wish instead to bury numerous pitch-pipes—is this not mere conjecture!

Huangzhong begins with one at zi; multiplying it by three successively through the twelve earthly branches, it ends at hai with one hundred seventy [thousand]…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
七千一百四十七漢志蓋借十二辰以列
三因之筭位耳故有寸分釐毫絲之法有
寸分釐毫絲之數至章明也蔡子不知其
假借立法而以為真有十二辰之數張皇
鋪衍而去真益遠矣自黃鐘之管陽皆下
生陰皆上生自蕤賓之管陽反上生陰反
下生此非空言也從子至巳陽生陰退故
律生呂言下生呂生律言上生從午至亥
陰生陽退故律生呂言上生呂生律言下
===
生蓋班志隔八相生一下一上則終于仲
呂其長止三寸三分有奇京房之法至蕤
賓重上生凡五下六上終于仲呂其長六
寸六分有奇若仲呂止三寸三分有奇雖
三分益一不能復生黃鐘之律故用六寸
六分則三分益一可以復生黃鐘耳蔡子
乃譏其陰陽錯亂毋亦未之思乎雖然此
猶可也近世儒者乃又倡為之說曰黃鐘
非九寸之管而引外紀呂氏春秋所載舍
punctuated: 七千一百四十七。《漢志》蓋借十二辰以列三因之筭位耳。故有寸、分、釐、毫、絲之法，有寸、分、釐、毫、絲之數，至章明也。蔡子不知其假借立法，而以為真有十二辰之數，張皇鋪衍，而去真益遠矣。自黃鐘之管，陽皆下生，陰皆上生；自蕤賓之管，陽反上生，陰反下生。此非空言也。從子至巳，陽生陰退，故律生呂言下生，呂生律言上生；從午至亥，陰生陽退，故律生呂言上生，呂生律言下生。蓋班《志》隔八相生，一下一上，則終于仲呂，其長止三寸三分有奇。京房之法，至蕤賓重上生，凡五下六上，終于仲呂，其長六寸六分有奇。若仲呂止三寸三分有奇，雖三分益一，不能復生黃鐘之律；故用六寸六分，則三分益一，可以復生黃鐘耳。蔡子乃譏其陰陽錯亂，毋亦未之思乎？雖然，此猶可也。近世儒者乃又倡為之說曰：「黃鐘非九寸之管。」而引《外紀》、《呂氏春秋》所載「舍…
translation_en: …7,147. The "Treatise" in the History of the Han (Hanzhi 漢志) merely borrowed the twelve earthly branches to arrange the calculation places for multiplying by three. Thus, there is the method of cun, fen, li, hao, and si (tenths, hundredths, thousandths, ten-thousandths of an inch), and there are the numerical values in cun, fen, li, hao, and si; this is crystal clear. Master Cai [Cai Yuanding 蔡元定] did not realize that it borrowed these to establish a calculation method, and instead believed that the twelve earthly branches truly possessed these numbers; by magnifying and elaborating on this, he strayed ever further from the truth. Starting from the pitch-pipe of Huangzhong, the yang pipes all generate downward (by subtracting one-third) and the yin pipes all generate upward (by adding one-third); starting from the pitch-pipe of Ruibin, the yang pipes conversely generate upward and the yin pipes conversely generate downward. These are not empty words. From zi to si, yang grows and yin retreats; therefore, when a yang pitch (lü 律) generates a yin pitch (lü 呂), it is called downward generation, and when a yin pitch generates a yang pitch, it is called upward generation. From wu to hai, yin grows and yang retreats; therefore, when a yang pitch generates a yin pitch, it is called upward generation, and when a yin pitch generates a yang pitch, it is called downward generation. In Ban [Gu]'s "Treatise," generating pitches at intervals of eight by alternating one downward and one upward ends at Zhonglü, whose length is only three cun, three fen and a fraction. In Jing Fang's (京房) method, upon reaching Ruibin it repeats upward generation—making five downward and six upward generations in all—and ends at Zhonglü, whose length is six cun, six fen and a fraction. If Zhonglü were only three cun, three fen and a fraction, even if one added a third to it, it could not regenerate the pitch of Huangzhong; therefore, by using six cun and six fen, adding a third makes it possible to regenerate Huangzhong. Master Cai nonetheless criticized this as throwing yin and yang into confusion—did he not fail to think it through? Even so, this much is still tolerable. Scholars of recent times, however, have advanced yet another theory, claiming: "Huangzhong is not a pipe of nine cun," and citing the theory of "she [han]…" recorded in the Outer Annals (Waiji 外紀) and the Spring and Autumn of Master Lü (Lüshi chunqiu 呂氏春秋)…

text:
少之說爲証曰黃鐘音始也象則君也其
律宜短其氣宜微其聲宜清者也是知其
一而不知其二者也夫黃鐘以八十一分
爲管而吹三十九分以爲聲故謂之含少
乃遂以三十九分爲黃鐘之律而執含少
以爲清管焉是其言本非誤而所以信其
言者誤矣此律一差大呂而下十一律者
將無由取正矣何其好爲異論而不師古
哉蓋太史公之言曰細若氣微若聲聖人
===
===
神而明之雖妙必效彼氣之嬴縮聲之清
濁固有不在于器數之末者使誠在于器
數之末也烏用是聖人神明爲哉雖然審
律之道神解爲上得數者次之不求律于
心而求律于器最下矣毋論黍之縱橫尺
之長短愚直謂俗樂與雅樂亦不甚懸絕
者夫金石鐘磬也後世易之爲方響絲竹
琴簫也後世易之爲箏笛此雅樂之變爲
俗樂者也黃鐘用合字大呂太簇用四字
punctuated: 少之說爲証，曰：「黃鐘，音始也，象則君也；其律宜短，其氣宜微，其聲宜清者也。」是知其一而不知其二者也。夫黃鐘以八十一分爲管，而吹三十九分以爲聲，故謂之含少；乃遂以三十九分爲黃鐘之律，而執含少以爲清管焉。是其言本非誤，而所以信其言者誤矣。此律一差，大呂而下十一律者，將無由取正矣。何其好爲異論而不師古哉！蓋太史公之言曰：「細若氣，微若聲，聖人神而明之，雖妙必效。」彼氣之嬴縮、聲之清濁，固有不在于器數之末者。使誠在于器數之末也，烏用是聖人神明爲哉！雖然，審律之道，神解爲上，得數者次之，不求律于心而求律于器，最下矣。毋論黍之縱橫、尺之長短，愚直謂俗樂與雅樂亦不甚懸絕者。夫金石，鐘磬也，後世易之爲方響；絲竹，琴簫也，後世易之爲箏笛：此雅樂之變爲俗樂者也。黃鐘用合字，大呂、太簇用四字，
translation_en: … [citing] the theory of "retaining the lesser" (hanshao 含少) as evidence, saying: "Huangzhong is the beginning of sound, and its image is the ruler; its pitch-pipe should be short, its vital breath subtle, and its sound clear." This is to know one aspect while remaining ignorant of the other. Now, Huangzhong takes eighty-one fen as its pipe length, yet blows thirty-nine fen to produce its sound, which is why it is called "retaining the lesser." To thereupon take thirty-nine fen as the pitch-pipe of Huangzhong and cling to "retaining the lesser" as a clear-toned pipe—this means that the original words themselves were not mistaken, but the way people have believed those words is mistaken! Once this fundamental pitch-pipe is off, the eleven pitch-pipes from Dalü downward will have no means of being rectified. How fond they are of making heterodox arguments instead of modeling themselves on antiquity! Indeed, in the words of the Grand Scribe (Taishigong 太史公, Sima Qian): "Subtle as vital breath, faint as sound—the sages comprehend them through spiritual intelligence; though mysterious, they must be made manifest." The expansion and contraction of that vital breath, and the clarity and turbidity of sound, inherently do not lie in the trivialities of instruments and numbers. If they truly lay in the trivialities of instruments and numbers, what need would there be for the spiritual intelligence of the sages! Nevertheless, in the Way of examining the pitch-pipes, spiritual comprehension is highest; grasping the numerical proportions comes next; and not seeking the pitch-pipes in the mind while seeking them only in physical instruments is the lowest of all. Setting aside whether the millet grains are laid lengthwise or crosswise, or whether the foot-measure is long or short, I would simply say that popular music (suyue) and elegant ritual music (yayue) are not so vastly separated either. Metal and stone are bells and chimes, which later ages replaced with tuned iron slabs (fangxiang); silk and bamboo are zithers (qin) and panpipes (xiao), which later ages replaced with bridged zithers (zheng) and transverse flutes (di)—this is how elegant music transformed into popular music. Huangzhong uses the note-symbol "he" (合), Dalü and Taicu use the note-symbol "si" (四), …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
夾鐘姑洗用一字夷則南呂用工字此俗
樂之可通于雅樂者也微獨此古以爼豆
今以盃盂古以莞席今以案榻雖聖人復
生不能舍盃盂而復爼豆棄案榻而用莞
席也是古今音樂之說也雖然此之謂樂
器爾數爾非所論于器與數之外也夫有
器而無官與無器同知聲而不知音知音
而不知樂與無官同舍其本而圖其末沾
沾焉鐘律是較非樂之完也本立矣末其
===
矣天造未寧而極音以逞非樂之至也蓋
聲如味一氣二體三類四物五聲六律七
音八風九歌以相成也清濁小大短長疾
徐哀樂剛柔遲速高下出入周疏以相濟
也是樂之器也記所謂聽其鏗鏘者也子
野歌而南北之風殊伯牙鼓琴而峩峩洋
洋之音著后夔氏典樂八音諧神人和焉
是樂之官也記所謂審音以知樂者也嗣
是而後荀勗之識牛鐸阮咸之較玉尺張
punctuated: 夾鐘、姑洗用一字，夷則、南呂用工字，此俗樂之可通于雅樂者也。微獨此，古以爼豆，今以盃盂；古以莞席，今以案榻。雖聖人復生，不能舍盃盂而復爼豆，棄案榻而用莞席也。是古今音樂之說也。雖然，此之謂樂器爾、數爾，非所論于器與數之外也。夫有器而無官，與無器同；知聲而不知音，知音而不知樂，與無官同。舍其本而圖其末，沾沾焉鐘律是較，非樂之完也。本立矣，末其矣，天造未寧而極音以逞，非樂之至也。蓋聲如味：一氣、二體、三類、四物、五聲、六律、七音、八風、九歌以相成也；清濁、小大、短長、疾徐、哀樂、剛柔、遲速、高下、出入、周疏以相濟也。是樂之器也，《記》所謂「聽其鏗鏘」者也。子野歌而南北之風殊，伯牙鼓琴而峩峩、洋洋之音著，后夔氏典樂，八音諧，神人和焉。是樂之官也，《記》所謂「審音以知樂」者也。嗣是而後，荀勗之識牛鐸，阮咸之較玉尺，張
translation_en:
…Jiazhong and Guxian correspond to the character yi, and Yize and Nanlü correspond to the character gong—this is how popular music can be correlated with elegant music. Nor is this the only case: antiquity used sacrificial stands and stemmed bowls (zudou), whereas today we use cups and basins; antiquity used rush mats, whereas today we use tables and couches. Even if a sage were to be reborn, he could not abandon cups and basins to restore sacrificial stands and stemmed bowls, nor discard tables and couches to use rush mats. This is the explanation of ancient and modern music.

Even so, this speaks merely of musical instruments and numerical proportions; it does not address what lies beyond instruments and numerical proportions. Now, to have instruments without a discerning ear (guan) is the same as having no instruments at all; to know sounds (sheng) without knowing tones (yin), and to know tones without knowing music (yue), is the same as having no discerning ear at all. To abandon the root and attend to the branches, fussily comparing bells and pitch-pipes, is not the perfection of music. When the root is established, yet the branches [?
