title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
康誥曰如保赤子心誠求之雖不中不遠
矣未有學養子而后嫁者也
子曰不得中行而與之必也狂狷乎狂者
進取狷者有所不爲也
徐子曰仲尼亟稱於水曰水哉水哉何取
於水也孟子曰原泉混混不舍晝夜盈
科而後進放乎四海有本者如是是之
===
取爾苟爲無本七八月之間雨集溝澮
皆盈其涸也可立而待也故聲聞過情
君子恥之
易
初九拔茅茹以其彙征吉象曰拔茅征吉
志在外也九二包荒用馮河不遐遺朋
亡得尚于中行象曰包荒得尚于中行
以光大也九三无平不陂无往不復艱
貞无咎勿恤其孚于食有福象曰无往
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
《康誥》曰：「如保赤子。」心誠求之，雖不中，不遠矣。未有學養子而后嫁者也。
子曰：「不得中行而與之，必也狂狷乎！狂者進取，狷者有所不爲也。」
徐子曰：「仲尼亟稱於水，曰：『水哉，水哉！』何取於水也？」孟子曰：「原泉混混，不舍晝夜，盈科而後進，放乎四海。有本者如是，是之取爾。苟爲無本，七八月之間雨集，溝澮皆盈；其涸也，可立而待也。故聲聞過情，君子恥之。」
易
初九，拔茅茹，以其彙，征吉。《象》曰：「拔茅征吉」，志在外也。九二，包荒，用馮河，不遐遺，朋亡，得尚于中行。《象》曰：「包荒，得尚于中行」，以光大也。九三，无平不陂，无往不復，艱貞无咎，勿恤其孚，于食有福。《象》曰：「无往
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

In the Announcement to Kang (Kang gao), it is said, "Act as if you were watching over an infant." If a mother is sincerely earnest in seeking its wants, though she may not hit them precisely, she will not be far from doing so. There has never been a girl who learned to bring up a child before she was married.

The Master said, "Since I cannot get men who pursue the due medium to associate with, I must certainly take the ardent and the cautiously-decided! The ardent will advance and lay hold of truth; the cautiously-decided will keep themselves from what is wrong."

Disciple Xu (Xu zi) said, "Zhongni [Confucius] often praised water, saying, 'O water! O water!' What did he find to approve in water?" Mencius replied, "There is a spring of water; how it gushes out! It rests not day nor night. It fills up every hollow, and then advances, flowing onto the Four Seas. Such is the nature of that which has a source, and it was just this that he approved of. But suppose that the water has no source. In the seventh and eighth months when the rain falls abundantly, the channels and ditches are all filled; yet their drying up may be expected as one stands and watches. Thus a superior man is ashamed of a reputation beyond his merits."

Book of Changes (Yi)

Nine at the beginning: Pulling up ribbon-grass, its roots come with its kind. Setting forth brings good fortune. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'Pulling up ribbon-grass, setting forth brings good fortune': his will is set on what is outside." Nine in the second place: Embracing the wasteland, using the river-crossing without a boat, not neglecting what is distant, and losing factional friends, one succeeds in matching the path of the mean. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Embracing the wasteland, one succeeds in matching the path of the mean,' because his way is glorious and great." Nine in the third place: No plain is not followed by a slope; no going is not followed by a return. In hardship, perseverance brings no blame. Do not grieve over its truth; in enjoying happiness, there will be blessing. The Commentary on the Images says: "'No going…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不復天地際也
象曰玉鉉在上剛柔節也
見乃謂之象
師者衆也衆必有所比故受之以比
書
曰后克艱厥后臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民
敏德帝曰俞允若茲嘉言罔攸伏野無
遺賢萬邦咸寧稽于衆舍己從人不虐
無告不廢困窮惟帝時克
===
若農服田力穡乃亦有秋
惟御事厥棐有恭
旌別淑慝表厥宅里彰善癉惡樹之風聲
弗率訓典殊厥井疆俾克畏慕申畫郊
圻慎固封守以康四海
詩
淑人君子其儀一兮其儀一兮心如結兮
我孔熯矣式禮莫愆工祝致告徂賚孝孫
苾芬孝祀神嗜飲食卜爾百福如幾如
punctuated:
不復，天地際也。
象曰：玉鉉在上，剛柔節也。
見乃謂之象。
師者，衆也，衆必有所比，故受之以比。
書：
曰：「后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。」帝曰：「俞！允若茲，嘉言罔攸伏，野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。稽于衆，舍己從人，不虐無告，不廢困窮，惟帝時克。」
若農服田力穡，乃亦有秋。
惟御事，厥棐有恭。
旌別淑慝，表厥宅里，彰善癉惡，樹之風聲。弗率訓典，殊厥井疆，俾克畏慕。申畫郊圻，慎固封守，以康四海。
詩：
淑人君子，其儀一兮；其儀一兮，心如結兮。
我孔熯矣，式禮莫愆。工祝致告，徂賚孝孫。苾芬孝祀，神嗜飲食。卜爾百福，如幾如
translation_en:
… return without going forth refers to the juncture of Heaven and Earth.

The Commentary on the Images says: "The jade carrying-rings at the top" means that the hard and the soft are in due proportion.

When it becomes visible, it is called an image.

"The Army" (Shi) means the multitude. The multitude must have that to which it cleaves; therefore it is followed by "Holding Together" (Bi).

Book of Documents (Shu):

[Yu] said: "If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of his sovereignty, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of his ministry, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will sedulously seek after virtue." The Emperor [Shun] said: "Yes! Truly if it be so, admirable words will nowhere lie hidden, no men of worth will be left neglected in the countryside, and the myriad states will all enjoy repose. To consult with the multitude, to set aside one's own views and follow those of others, not to oppress the helpless, and not to neglect the straitened and poor—only the Emperor [Yao] was able to do this."

Just as a husbandman works his fields and labors at his harvesting, then there is also an autumn harvest.

As for the managers of affairs, in assisting they showed reverence.

Distinguish the good from the wicked, set up marks at their dwellings and villages, make manifest the good and make loathsome the evil, and establish the voice of their moral influence. As for those who do not follow the instructive statutes, set apart their well-field boundaries, so that they may learn both to fear and to emulate. Clearly define the suburban borders, and carefully strengthen the frontier defenses, in order to give peace to all within the Four Seas.

Book of Odes (Shi):

The good man, the princely man, his deportment is invariable; his deportment is invariable, and his heart is as if tied fast.

We are very exhausted, and have performed every ceremony without error. The skillful invocators convey the message, and go to present it to the filial descendant: "Fragrant has been your filial sacrifice, and the spirits have enjoyed your drink and food. They confer on you a hundred blessings; according to the due time, according to …"

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
式旣齊旣稷旣匡旣敕永錫爾極時萬
時億
大任有身生此文王
敬之敬之天惟顯思命不易哉
春秋
遂及齊侯宋公盟荘公十有九年
楚人侵鄭僖公二年齊人執陳轅濤塗僖
公四年
春白狄來襄公十有八年
===
夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲桓公三年秋八月
諸侯盟于首止僖公五年九月戊辰諸
侯盟于葵丘僖公九年公會晉侯宋公
衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭魚襄公十
有一年叔孫豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊
國弱宋向戌衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫
歸生鄭罕虎許人曹人于虢昭公元年
禮記
punctuated:
式。旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕，永錫爾極，時萬時億。
大任有身，生此文王。
敬之敬之，天惟顯思，命不易哉！

《春秋》
遂及齊侯、宋公盟。莊公十有九年。
楚人侵鄭。僖公二年。齊人執陳轅濤塗。僖公四年。
春，白狄來。襄公十有八年。
夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。桓公三年。秋八月，諸侯盟于首止。僖公五年。九月戊辰，諸侯盟于葵丘。僖公九年。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。襄公十有一年。叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。昭公元年。

《禮記》
translation_en:
…according to the proper measure. You have been exact and expeditious; you have been upright and cautious; forever will they bestow upon you the utmost blessings, in tens of thousands and in hundreds of millions.”
“Tai Ren became pregnant, and gave birth to this King Wen.”
“Revere it, revere it! Heaven is illustrious in its ways; its Mandate is not easily preserved!”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
“Sui made a covenant with the Marquis of Qi and the Duke of Song.” (Nineteenth year of Duke Zhuang).
“Men of Chu invaded Zheng.” (Second year of Duke Xi). “Men of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen.” (Fourth year of Duke Xi).
“In spring, the White Di came.” (Eighteenth year of Duke Xiang).
“In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu.” (Third year of Duke Huan). “In autumn, in the eighth month, the feudal lords made a covenant at Shouzhi.” (Fifth year of Duke Xi). “In the ninth month, on the wuchen day, the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu.” (Ninth year of Duke Xi). “The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu.” (Eleventh year of Duke Xiang). “Shusun Bao met Zhao Wu of Jin, Gongzi Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Gongzi Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, a man of Xu, and a man of Cao at Guo.” (First year of Duke Zhao).

Record of Rites (Liji)

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
陰陽和而萬物得
是故樂之隆非極音也食饗之禮非致味
也清廟之瑟朱絃而疏越壹倡而三歎
有遺音者矣大饗之禮尚玄酒而俎腥
魚大羹不和有遺味者矣
備者百順之名也
子云善則稱君過則稱已則民作忠君陳
曰爾有嘉謀嘉猷入告爾君于內女乃
順之于外曰此謀此猷惟我君之德於
===
乎是惟良顯哉
第貳場
論
天下國家之大務
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢令二千石修職詔景帝後二年
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦爲僕射誥貞觀三
年
擬
punctuated:
陰陽和而萬物得。
是故樂之隆，非極音也；食饗之禮，非致味也。清廟之瑟，朱絃而疏越，壹倡而三歎，有遺音者矣；大饗之禮，尚玄酒而俎腥魚，大羹不和，有遺味者矣。
備者，百順之名也。
子云：「善則稱君，過則稱已，則民作忠。《君陳》曰：『爾有嘉謀嘉猷，入告爾君于內，女乃順之于外，曰：「此謀此猷，惟我君之德。」於乎！是惟良顯哉！』」

第貳場
論：
天下國家之大務。
詔、誥、表內科一道：
擬漢令二千石修職詔〔景帝後二年〕。
擬唐以房玄齡、杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬
translation_en:
"When yin and yang are in harmony, the myriad things attain their proper state."

"Therefore, the pinnacle of music does not lie in the utmost indulgence of sound, nor do the rites of food and feasting lie in the utmost perfection of flavor. The zithers of the Ancestral Temple have vermilion strings and widely spaced sound-holes; when one leads the singing and three sigh in response, there is a lingering resonance left unexpressed. In the rites of the Great Banquet, plain water is esteemed as the dark liquor, raw fish is placed on the sacrificial stands, and the great broth is unseasoned; there is a lingering flavor left unexpressed."

"Completeness is the name for smoothness in all things."

"The Master said: 'If one attributes what is good to one's ruler and takes fault upon oneself, then the people will be moved to loyalty. The Jun Chen (Book of Documents) says: "When you have fine plans and fine counsels, enter and report them to your ruler within; then comply with them outside, saying: 'These plans, these counsels, are all due to the virtue of our ruler.' Oh! How admirable and illustrious this is!"'"

Second Session

Discourse:
"The great affairs of the empire and the state."

Imperial Edict (zhao), Mandate (gao), or Memorial (biao) (choose one):
Compose an imitation of the Han dynasty edict ordering Two-thousand-bushel Officials (Grand Administrators) to attend diligently to their duties (2nd year of the Later Era of Emperor Jing, 142 BCE).
Compose an imitation of the Tang dynasty mandate appointing Fang Xuanling 房玄齡 and Du Ruhui 杜如晦 as Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs (puye) (3rd year of the Zhenguan era, 629 CE).
Compose an imitation of…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
御製輔臣賛和詩集序
示大學士楊一清等謝表〔嘉靖七年〕
判語〔五條〕
收藏禁書及私習天文
投匿名文書告言人罪
在官求索借貸人財物
虛費工力採取不堪用
織造違禁龍鳳文段疋
第叄場
===
第五道
問自古聖帝明王雖履泰寧之世猶然兢
業抑畏延納忠謨唐虞邈矣逮商周時
如伊傅姬公之告其君動稱先王以爲
儆戒廼其君不憚委己從之迄爲一代
令主登上理而鞏鴻圖治固莫尚於法
祖與三代而下有書貞觀政要於屏風
每正容斂手而讀之者有進講三朝寶
訓注目傾耳隨事咨詢不倦者視商周
punctuated:
《御製輔臣賛和詩集序》示大學士楊一清等謝表〔嘉靖七年〕

判語〔五條〕：
收藏禁書及私習天文；
投匿名文書告言人罪；
在官求索借貸人財物；
虛費工力採取不堪用；
織造違禁龍鳳文段疋。

第叄場

第五道：
問：自古聖帝明王，雖履泰寧之世，猶然兢業抑畏，延納忠謨。唐、虞邈矣，逮商、周時，如伊、傅、姬公之告其君，動稱先王以爲儆戒；廼其君不憚委己從之，迄爲一代令主，登上理而鞏鴻圖。治固莫尚於法祖與？三代而下，有書《貞觀政要》於屏風，每正容斂手而讀之者；有進講《三朝寶訓》，注目傾耳，隨事咨詢不倦者。視商、周

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
令主奚殊夷考其實政乃不逮遠甚意
者其詒謀不足法耶抑其誦法者以文
不以實耶何治效之闊疎也洪惟我
祖
宗創造於前
列聖紹庥於後至我
皇上益繼序而闡揚之
聖德睿猷卓邁千古矣頃歲
俞輔臣之請輯
===
累朝
訓錄分類編摩稍倣貞觀政要釐爲條目者以
四十計
便殿進
講
特賜延納凜然陟降紹庭之思矣顧孫卿有言
主術約而易操也主好要則百事詳卽
此四十事者一一而畫之日亦不遑給
耳茲欲掇要探本稽
punctuated: 令主奚殊？夷考其實政，乃不逮遠甚。意者其詒謀不足法耶？抑其誦法者以文不以實耶？何治效之闊疎也！洪惟我祖宗創造於前，列聖紹庥於後，至我皇上，益繼序而闡揚之，聖德睿猷，卓邁千古矣。頃歲，俞輔臣之請，輯累朝訓錄，分類編摩，稍倣《貞觀政要》，釐爲條目者以四十計，便殿進講，特賜延納，凜然陟降紹庭之思矣。顧孫卿有言：「主術約而易操也，主好要則百事詳。」卽此四十事者，一一而畫之，日亦不遑給耳。茲欲掇要探本，稽
translation_en:
…excellent rulers, how did they differ? Yet when we calmly examine their actual governance, they fell short by a great distance. Could it be that the ancestral counsels bequeathed to them were unworthy of emulation? Or was it that those who recited and emulated them did so in letter rather than in substance? Why was the efficacy of their governance so remote and sparse?

Reflecting upon our Imperial Ancestors, who founded the dynasty before, and the Successive Sage Emperors, who continued the blessings thereafter: down to His Majesty the reigning Emperor, he has further carried on the succession and magnified their legacy; his sagely virtue and wise plans far surpass all antiquity. In recent years, granting the request of the Grand Secretaries, he ordered the compilation of the Precious Instructions and Veritable Records of Successive Reigns (Leichao xunlu), categorized and edited slightly in imitation of the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Period (Zhenguan zhengyao), arranged into headings numbering forty in all. When these are presented and expounded in the side palaces, he specially grants audience and acceptance, filled with a reverent mindfulness of the ancestral spirits ascending and descending in the court.

Yet Master Xun (Xun Qing 孫卿, i.e., Xunzi) had a saying: "The art of the ruler is concise and easy to grasp; when the ruler loves the essential, then the hundred affairs are attended to in detail." If one were to plan out each and every one of these forty matters individually, the days would not be sufficient for the task. Now, if we wish to gather the essentials and probe the fundamental, examining…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
令主奚殊夷考其實政乃不逮遠甚意
者其詒謀不足法耶亡其誦法者以文
不以實耶何治效之闊疎也洪惟我
祖
宗創造於前
列聖紹庥於後至我
皇上益繼序而闡揚之
聖德睿猷卓邁千古矣頃歲
俞輔臣之請輯
===
累朝
訓錄分類編摩稍倣貞觀政要釐爲條目者以
四十計
便殿進
講
特賜延納稟然陟降紹庭之思矣顧孫卿有言
主術約而易操也主好要則百事詳卽
此四十事者一一而畫之日亦不遑給
耳玆欲掇要探本稽
punctuated: 令主奚殊？夷考其實政，乃不逮遠甚。意者其詒謀不足法耶？亡其誦法者以文不以實耶？何治效之闊疎也！洪惟我祖宗創造於前，列聖紹庥於後，至我皇上，益繼序而闡揚之，聖德睿猷，卓邁千古矣。頃歲俞輔臣之請，輯累朝《訓》、《錄》，分類編摩，稍倣《貞觀政要》，釐爲條目者以四十計。便殿進講，特賜延納，稟然陟降紹庭之思矣。顧孫卿有言：「主術約而易操也。」主好要則百事詳，卽此四十事者一一而畫之，日亦不遑給耳。玆欲掇要探本，稽
translation_en:
…wherein did they differ from exemplary rulers? Yet when we calmly examine their actual governance, it fell short by far. Could it be that the counsels bequeathed to them were unworthy of emulation? Or was it rather that those who recited and modeled themselves on them did so merely in letter and not in substance? Why were the results of their governance so remote and meager!

Reverently reflecting upon how our Imperial Ancestors founded the dynasty in the past, and how the Successive Sage Emperors continued their blessings thereafter, down to our Emperor, who has further succeeded to the line and gloriously expounded their legacy—his sagely virtue and farsighted plans surpass a thousand ages! In recent years, assenting to the request of the Grand Secretaries, he ordered the compilation of the Ancestral Injunctions (Xun) and Veritable Records (Lu) of successive reigns, classifying and editing them broadly in imitation of the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Period (Zhenguan zhengyao), and organizing them into some forty headings. When these are presented and expounded in the side halls of the palace, he specially grants audience and receptively accepts them, filled with awe-inspiring thoughts of the ancestral spirits ascending and descending and of continuing their work in the court.

Yet Master Xun (Xunzi) had a saying: "The ruler's art is concise and easy to grasp." If the ruler loves the essential, then the hundred affairs will be attended to in detail; whereas if he were to plan out each of these forty matters one by one, the days would not be sufficient for the task. Now, if one wishes to gather the essentials and probe the fundamentals, examining…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖
宗故實爲我
皇上保治之助爾多士其各攄所見焉
問人主需材以易天下奚啻饑渴顧材品
不同眞似靡辨脫眩於名實則似材者
類得以倖進而眞材隱矣我思古人有
名實之相副者有有其實而無其名者
有有其名而無其實者有蚤蒙不美之
名而晚令者有始被貪濁之名而終著
===
高操者有初陷兇惡之名而後更改行
者有陽附君子之名而陰實爲小人者
有外近小人之名而中實爲君子者蓋
不可以一端盡也人主亦安從而辨之
俾不爲名實所眩歟夫徇名而失實有
國者之大患也茲欲俾登進者皆眞材
而各獲其用似材者罔所售而倖進之
竇塞果何道而可諸士抱材而待用久
矣幸相與盡言之以驗知人之鑒
punctuated:
祖宗故實，爲我皇上保治之助。爾多士其各攄所見焉。
問：人主需材以易天下，奚啻饑渴？顧材品不同，眞似靡辨。脫眩於名實，則似材者類得以倖進，而眞材隱矣。我思古人，有名實之相副者；有有其實而無其名者；有有其名而無其實者；有蚤蒙不美之名而晚令者；有始被貪濁之名而終著高操者；有初陷兇惡之名而後更改行者；有陽附君子之名而陰實爲小人者；有外近小人之名而中實爲君子者。蓋不可以一端盡也，人主亦安從而辨之，俾不爲名實所眩歟？夫徇名而失實，有國者之大患也。茲欲俾登進者皆眞材而各獲其用，似材者罔所售而倖進之竇塞，果何道而可？諸士抱材而待用久矣，幸相與盡言之，以驗知人之鑒。
translation_en:
…the precedents and actual deeds of the Ancestors, to serve as an aid to His Majesty in preserving good governance. May all you gentlemen each set forth your views.

Question: A ruler stands in need of talent to transform the world—how is this any less urgent than hunger and thirst? Yet the qualities of talent differ, and the genuine and the specious are difficult to distinguish. Should one be dazzled by reputation and reality, those who merely resemble men of talent will generally manage to advance by luck, while true talent will remain hidden. When I reflect upon the ancients, there were those whose reputation and reality matched one another; there were those who possessed the reality without the reputation; there were those who possessed the reputation without the reality; there were those who early on suffered an unsavory reputation yet achieved a fine name in their later years; there were those who at first bore a reputation for greed and corruption yet in the end displayed lofty integrity; there were those who initially fell into a reputation for fierceness and evil yet later reformed their conduct; there were those who outwardly attached themselves to the reputation of superior men while secretly acting as petty men in reality; and there were those who externally came close to the reputation of petty men while inwardly being superior men in reality. Indeed, they cannot be exhausted by any single category. How, then, is a ruler to distinguish among them so as not to be dazzled by reputation and reality? Now, pursuing reputation while losing sight of reality is the great affliction of those who possess a state. Today, if we wish to ensure that all who are promoted and advanced are men of true talent and each is put to his proper use, while those who merely resemble men of talent have no way to peddle themselves and the channels of undeserved advancement are blocked up, by what way indeed can this be achieved? You gentlemen have cherished your talents and awaited employment for a long time; please speak your minds fully together, so as to test your discernment in knowing men.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
解與
聖朝積德久矣大樂宜興願相與講明之以爲
考古者地
問士人習尚上翼王敎下表民風所繋非
眇小也揚子稱周士貴秦士賤以爲士
之貴賤惟時所遷其果然與成周之制
自三物敎民而賔興之至於論定而官
之後又有以詔廢置而致誅賞相見之
際非擯紹持贄則不得通何詳也一時
===
髦士斂容戢武於法制敎令之中視秦
時縱横捭闔之徒桀驁横恣其氣焰傾
於人主此何貴何賤與豈其貴賤固有
所在與兩漢之興士靡不以功業節義
爭相策勵洎其末路浸淫敗壞莫可挽
回或以諂佞成風或以抗激取錮說者
謂皆肈業二君所由作也何前後之相
盭與豈鄒軻氏所稱豪傑之興不待文
王非與方今
punctuated:
解與？聖朝積德久矣，大樂宜興，願相與講明之，以爲考古者地。
問：士人習尚，上翼王敎，下表民風，所繋非眇小也。揚子稱：「周士貴，秦士賤。」以爲士之貴賤惟時所遷，其果然與？成周之制，自三物敎民而賔興之，至於論定而官之，後又有以詔廢置而致誅賞；相見之際，非擯紹持贄則不得通，何詳也！一時髦士，斂容戢武於法制敎令之中；視秦時縱横捭闔之徒，桀驁横恣，其氣焰傾於人主，此何貴何賤與？豈其貴賤固有所與？兩漢之興，士靡不以功業節義爭相策勵；洎其末路，浸淫敗壞，莫可挽回：或以諂佞成風，或以抗激取錮。說者謂皆肈業二君所由作也，何前後之相盭與？豈鄒軻氏所稱「豪傑之興，不待文王」，非與？方今
translation_en:
… explained? Our Sacred Dynasty has accumulated virtue for a long time, and great music ought to flourish. I wish to discuss and clarify these matters together with you, so as to lay a foundation for those who investigate antiquity.

Question: The customs and inclinations of scholars above assist the kingly instruction and below exemplify the customs of the common people; what hinges upon them is by no means trivial. Master Yang (Yang Xiong 楊雄) declared that "the scholars of Zhou were noble, whereas the scholars of Qin were base," taking the nobility or baseness of scholars to shift solely with the times. Is this truly so? Under the institutions of the flourishing Zhou, from instructing the people in the "three things" and recommending them as honored guests, to appointing them to office once their merits were assessed and settled, and subsequently issuing decrees on dismissal and placement and meting out punishment and reward; and on occasions of formal audiences, not allowing communication without intermediaries introducing them and the presentation of ceremonial gifts—how detailed it all was! Theeminent scholars of that age composed their countenances and restrained their steps within the bounds of laws, institutions, instructions, and ordinances. Compared with the practitioners of vertical and horizontal alliances and rhetorical maneuvering in the Qin period—who were unruly, arrogant, and unrestrained, their bluster overwhelming even the rulers of men—which of these was noble and which was base? Or did their nobility and baseness indeed rest upon something intrinsic? At the rise of the Two Han dynasties (Western and Eastern Han), there were no scholars who did not vie to spur one another on with meritorious achievements and moral integrity. Yet by their final years, they gradually sank into corruption beyond recovery: in the one case making a custom of flattery and sycophancy, and in the other courting proscription through defiant extremism. Commentators say that both were brought about by the two founding rulers; why were their beginnings and ends so mutually contradictory? Could it be that what Mencius of Zou (Zou Ke 鄒軻) called "outstanding heroes rising up even without waiting for a King Wen" is untrue? At the present time, …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
主聖時清澤流化布而爲之士者尚未知其爲
周爲秦爲兩漢也玆欲一道德同風俗
周人之制儻可行於今否抑别有道與
故蘄與諸士考衷焉
問天下不可一日而無法捐法而求治猶
涉江河而亡維楫鮮有濟矣廼入關而
約法三章克長安而約法十二條至闊
略也而卒爲二代基治之主何歟懸告
姦之格定減爵之令法至詳矣而竟兆
===
危亡之禍抑又何歟世儒拘於法而不
獲自適至舉聖人之法而力詆之有謂
焚符破璽而民朴鄙剖斗折衡而民不
爭殫殘天下之聖法而後可與論議者
有謂民知書而德衰知數而厚衰知券
契而信衰知機械而實衰者語至拂經
也豈亦有激而言之歟
明自
二祖開基
punctuated:
主聖時清，澤流化布，而爲之士者，尚未知其爲周、爲秦、爲兩漢也。玆欲一道德，同風俗，周人之制，儻可行於今否？抑别有道與？故蘄與諸士考衷焉。
問：天下不可一日而無法。捐法而求治，猶涉江河而亡維楫，鮮有濟矣。廼入關而約法三章，克長安而約法十二條，至闊略也，而卒爲二代基治之主，何歟？懸告姦之格，定減爵之令，法至詳矣，而竟兆危亡之禍，抑又何歟？世儒拘於法而不獲自適，至舉聖人之法而力詆之：有謂焚符破璽而民朴鄙，剖斗折衡而民不爭，殫殘天下之聖法而後可與論議者；有謂民知書而德衰，知數而厚衰，知券契而信衰，知機械而實衰者。語至拂經也，豈亦有激而言之歟？明自二祖開基，
translation_en:
…the Sovereign is sage and the times are pure, blessings flow and transformative teaching spreads everywhere, yet as for those who serve as scholars, it is still unknown whether they are like those of the Zhou, the Qin, or the Two Han dynasties. Now, if we wish to unify morality and make customs uniform, could the institutions of the Zhou people perhaps be practiced today, or is there another way? Therefore, I seek to examine the innermost thoughts of you gentlemen on this matter.

Question: The realm cannot go a single day without laws. To cast aside laws and seek good governance is like crossing great rivers without ropes and oars—seldom will one succeed. Yet upon entering the Pass, [Liu Bang 劉邦] agreed upon a code of law in three articles, and upon capturing Chang'an, [Yuwen Tai 宇文泰 / Li Yuan 李淵] agreed upon a code of law in twelve articles. These were extremely broad and simplified, and yet they ultimately became the rulers who laid the foundations of governance for two dynasties—why is this? Posting regulations for denouncing villainy and establishing ordinances for reducing noble ranks—such laws were extremely detailed, and yet they ultimately presaged the disaster of peril and ruin—why, again, is this? Worldly scholars are fettered by laws and cannot find ease for themselves, to the point that they take up the laws of the sages and vigorously malign them. There are those who say: "Burn the tallies and shatter the seals, and the people will be simple and unadorned; split the peck-measures and snap the steelyards, and the people will not contend; only when the sage laws of the world have been utterly destroyed can one begin to discuss and deliberate with them." And there are those who say: "When the people know writing, virtue declines; when they know calculation, generosity declines; when they know deeds and contracts, trustworthiness declines; when they know mechanical contrivances, substance declines." Such words are utterly contrary to canonical principles; could it be that they too were spoken out of provocation? Since the Two Progenitors [Taizu 太祖 and Chengzu 成祖] of the Ming laid the foundations…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
康誥曰如保赤子心誠求之雖不中不遠
矣未有學養子而后嫁者也
祝以忠
同考試官訓導張批詞理燦然情見俱見保
民者不當如是耶
同考試官敎諭區批精深瑩徹無瑕疵處宜
錄以式
===
考試官敎諭程批醇雅不浮
考試官敎諭周批說題意懇切
傳者引言慈出于性立敎之本可識矣蓋保赤
子之心天性也觀於書而以慈立敎者其亦求
端于性乎傳者釋齊治意謂家國異勢矣而敎
之所以相通者固以其理之一然其機亦自有
所不容强者試以慈觀之康誥曰如保赤子夫
保赤子母道也曰如保赤子君道也保赤子者
如何蓋赤子有欲無言者也惟有欲則遂其欲
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「《康誥》曰：『如保赤子。』心誠求之，雖不中，不遠矣。未有學養子而后嫁者也。」

祝以忠

同考試官訓導張批：詞理燦然，情見俱見。保民者不當如是耶？
同考試官敎諭區批：精深瑩徹，無瑕疵處，宜錄以式。
考試官敎諭程批：醇雅不浮。
考試官敎諭周批：說題意懇切。

傳者引言慈出于性，立敎之本可識矣。蓋保赤子之心，天性也；觀於《書》，而以慈立敎者，其亦求端于性乎！傳者釋齊治，意謂：家、國異勢矣，而敎之所以相通者，固以其理之一，然其機亦自有所不容强者，試以慈觀之。《康誥》曰：「如保赤子。」夫保赤子，母道也；曰「如保赤子」，君道也。保赤子者如何？蓋赤子，有欲無言者也。惟有欲，則遂其欲…
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"The Announcement to Kang (Kang gao) says: 'Act as if you were protecting a newborn infant.' If you seek its needs with a sincere heart, even if you do not hit the mark, you will not be far off. There has never been anyone who first learned how to raise a child and only afterward married."

Zhu Yizhong 祝以忠

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang 張: The diction and reasoning are brilliant, and both sentiment and insight [?; 情見俱見] are fully revealed. Should not those who protect the people be like this?
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Ou 區: Profound and pellucid, without a single flaw; it ought to be recorded as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Cheng 程: Pure and refined, without superficiality.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhou 周: Explains the meaning of the topic with earnestness and precision.

The commentator cites a quotation to show that parental kindness issues from human nature, whereby the foundation for establishing instruction can be known. Indeed, the heart that protects a newborn infant is endowed by Heaven's nature; looking at the Book of Documents (Shu), should not he who establishes instruction through kindness also seek its beginnings in human nature! In explaining the regulation of the family and the governance of the state, the commentator meant to say: Family and state differ in their circumstances, yet the reason instruction is mutually continuous between them is assuredly because their principle is one; however, its vital spring also naturally has that which cannot be forced—let us examine this through kindness. The Announcement to Kang says: "Act as if you were protecting a newborn infant." Now, protecting a newborn infant is the way of a mother; to say "as if you were protecting a newborn infant" is the way of a ruler. How does one protect a newborn infant? A newborn infant is one who has desires but lacks speech. Precisely because it has desires, to fulfill its desires…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭區批詞雄調逸而一統規模
盡洩於親端矣錄之
考試官教諭程批宏博有奇氣
考試官教諭周批明練俊偉
觀師比相承而得大一統之義焉夫天下之衆
非得人以統之不可也此師之後所以有比與
且所貴乎統一宇內而總理人羣者何也懼天
下相聚而至於相戮也嘗於聖人之序師比得
其故焉師之爲言衆也蓋生人之初其勢均焉
===
耳天下之事猶可聽其自爲而不至於亂物聚
之後其情渙焉已天下之治豈可一无所統而
自底於安饑者欲食寒者欲衣貧者欲給必以
其欲求遂於王者王者起而有以遂其欲將不
召而衆歸往矣智者紿愚勇者脅弱衆者暴寡
必以其情求平於王者王者起而有以平其情
將不集而衆憑依矣蓋惟德可以服人而天生
王者與之以神聖顯懿之資卽賢人能士皆在
其範圍而况此衆乎惟位可以率人而天生王
punctuated:
同考試官教諭區批：詞雄調逸，而一統規模盡洩於親端矣。錄之。
考試官教諭程批：宏博有奇氣。
考試官教諭周批：明練俊偉。
觀《師》《比》相承，而得大一統之義焉。夫天下之衆，非得人以統之不可也。此《師》之後所以有《比》與？且所貴乎統一宇內而總理人羣者，何也？懼天下相聚而至於相戮也。嘗於聖人之序《師》《比》得其故焉。師之爲言衆也。蓋生人之初，其勢均焉耳，天下之事猶可聽其自爲而不至於亂；物聚之後，其情渙焉已，天下之治豈可一无所統而自底於安？饑者欲食，寒者欲衣，貧者欲給，必以其欲求遂於王者；王者起而有以遂其欲，將不召而衆歸往矣。智者紿愚，勇者脅弱，衆者暴寡，必以其情求平於王者；王者起而有以平其情，將不集而衆憑依矣。蓋惟德可以服人，而天生王者，與之以神聖顯懿之資，卽賢人能士皆在其範圍，而况此衆乎？惟位可以率人，而天生王
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Ou: The diction is vigorous and the tone transcendent, while the grand scale of great unification is fully revealed at the tip of the brush [? 親端, likely a woodblock error for 毫端]. Record it.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng: Vast and erudite, with an extraordinary spirit.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhou: Lucid, practiced, and heroically grand.

By observing how the hexagrams Shi (The Army / The Multitude) and Bi (Holding Together) follow one another, one grasps the meaning of the great unification. Now, as for the multitude of the world, it simply will not do unless a person is found to unify and govern them. Is this not why after Shi there comes Bi? Moreover, why do we value unifying all within the universe and exercising overall governance over the human flock? It is out of fear that the people of the world, in gathering together, will end up slaughtering one another. I have examined the Sage's sequencing of Shi and Bi and found the reason for this. The word "shi" means "multitude." In the beginning of humankind, their power was merely equal, and the affairs of the world could still be left to take their own course without descending into disorder. After things gathered in great numbers, however, their sentiments became dispersed; how could the governance of the world have nothing at all to unify it and yet arrive at peace on its own? The hungry desire food, the cold desire clothing, and the poor desire sufficiency—they must bring their desires and seek their fulfillment from the true king. When a true king arises and has the means to fulfill their desires, the multitude will turn to and follow him without being summoned. The clever deceive the foolish, the brave intimidate the weak, and the many tyrannize the few—they must bring their grievances and seek redress from the true king. When a true king arises and has the means to redress their grievances, the multitude will rely upon him without being assembled. Indeed, only virtue can win people's submission; Heaven gives birth to the true king and endows him with divinely sagely and illustriously admirable qualities, so that even worthy men and capable scholars are all within his compass—how much more so this multitude? Only position can lead people, and Heaven gives birth to the true king…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
王愛民之深而慮事之遠也雖然導民者不專
以言守國者匪徒在險康王命畢公保釐而繼
之曰惟德惟義有以也夫
詩
我孔熯矣式禮莫愆工祝致告徂賚孝孫
苾芬孝祀神嗜飲食卜爾百福如幾如
式旣齊旣稷旣匡旣敕永錫爾極時萬
時億
葉秉敬
===
同考試官教諭陳批刋盡浮詞而始終重一
敬字得詩人旨
同考試官教諭陳批體裁整飭意趣悠長颯
颯乎盛世之音可以雄視諸作
考試官教諭程批格局正大義理精密
考試官教諭周批明健可誦
觀公卿祀盡其敬而神福從之焉夫祭主於敬
也盡其敬矣而神之福之也亦各從其類也已
歌楚茨者意謂宗廟之祭非以求福也而祭不
punctuated:
王愛民之深，而慮事之遠也。雖然，導民者不專以言，守國者匪徒在險。康王命畢公保釐，而繼之曰：「惟德惟義」，有以也夫！

《詩》
「我孔熯矣，式禮莫愆。工祝致告，徂賚孝孫：『苾芬孝祀，神嗜飲食。卜爾百福，如幾如式。旣齊旣稷，旣匡旣敕。永錫爾極，時萬時億。』」
葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳批：刋盡浮詞，而始終重一「敬」字，得詩人旨。
同考試官教諭陳批：體裁整飭，意趣悠長，颯颯乎盛世之音，可以雄視諸作。
考試官教諭程批：格局正大，義理精密。
考試官教諭周批：明健可誦。

觀公卿祀盡其敬，而神福從之焉。夫祭，主於敬也。盡其敬矣，而神之福之也，亦各從其類也已。歌《楚茨》者意謂：宗廟之祭，非以求福也；而祭不
translation_en:
… how deeply the king loved the people and how far-reaching was his foresight in affairs! Even so, guiding the people does not rely solely on words, and defending the state does not depend merely on strategic fastnesses. When King Kang commanded the Duke of Bi to secure and regulate the territory, he followed it by saying, "Only virtue, only righteousness"—there was good reason for this indeed!

Classic of Poetry (Shi)
"We are very exhausted, and have performed every ceremony without error. The skillful invoker conveys the message, and goes to present it to the filial descendant: 'Fragrant has been your filial sacrifice, and the spirits have enjoyed the drink and food. They confer on you a hundred blessings; each as desired, each as sure as law. You have been exact and expeditious; you have been correct and cautious. Forever will they bestow on you the utmost good, in tens of thousands and in hundreds of millions.'"

Ye Bingjing 葉秉敬
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen: It pare away all superficial verbiage and from beginning to end emphasizes the single word "reverence" (jing), grasping the poet's true intent.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen: The form and structure are well-ordered, the meaning and spirit lingering and profound. With the grand resonance of the music of a flourishing age, it stands preeminent among all the compositions.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Cheng: The framework is upright and grand; the moral reasoning is precise and thorough.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zhou: Clear, vigorous, and worthy of recitation.

Observe how the dukes and ministers exhaust their reverence in sacrifice, and the blessings of the spirits follow accordingly. Now, sacrifice takes reverence as its core principle. When one has exhausted one's reverence, the spirits' bestowal of blessings likewise corresponds to each according to its kind. What the singer of the ode "Chu ci" (Thick Star-thistle) meant to say is this: The sacrifice in the ancestral temple is not performed for the purpose of seeking blessings; yet if one sacrifices and does not…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
受福是神弗享而吾之孝誠未孚矣我公卿而
有是哉彼禮行之久則力竭而易愆也今則自
求神以至于獻尸時雖久而致愨之忱益虔力
已竭而不匱之思罔懈蓋備之爲禮物著之爲
禮容舉莫或愆焉誠盡其敬而敬者由是祝傳
神意以賚孝孫也何如哉蓋曰祭有飲食而芳
潔其至也茲而苾苾芬芬既莫非神之所嗜矣
則卜爾百福其取諸飲食焉來如幾也多如式
也庶徵與庶羞其相應也已何也敬昭於物而
===
百福之□□以其敬也非以物也祭有禮容而
莊敬其至也茲而齊稷匡敕既莫非神之所歆
矣則永錫爾極其取諸禮容焉時萬善也時億
善也多福與多儀其相應也已何也敬見於容
而爾極之錫也以其敬也非以容也此其式禮
謹而孝誠備類應速而顯道彰公卿盡祭之義
如此非德盛政脩何以致之抑不求其爲孝子
之祭也而嘏詞以類應賚之何哉蓋不期福者
固奉祭之心而祀典之舉肇于力農則宜稼于
punctuated: 受福，是神弗享，而吾之孝誠未孚矣。我公卿而有是哉？彼禮行之久，則力竭而易愆也。今則自求神以至于獻尸，時雖久而致愨之忱益虔，力已竭而不匱之思罔懈。蓋備之爲禮物，著之爲禮容，舉莫或愆焉，誠盡其敬而敬者。由是祝傳神意以賚孝孫也，何如哉？蓋曰：祭有飲食，而芳潔其至也。茲而苾苾芬芬，既莫非神之所嗜矣，則卜爾百福，其取諸飲食焉，來如幾也，多如式也，庶徵與庶羞其相應也已。何也？敬昭於物，而百福之□□以其敬也，非以物也。祭有禮容，而莊敬其至也。茲而齊稷匡敕，既莫非神之所歆矣，則永錫爾極，其取諸禮容焉，時萬善也，時億善也，多福與多儀其相應也已。何也？敬見於容，而爾極之錫也以其敬也，非以容也。此其式禮謹而孝誠備，類應速而顯道彰。公卿盡祭之義如此，非德盛政脩，何以致之？抑不求其爲孝子之祭也，而嘏詞以類應賚之，何哉？蓋不期福者，固奉祭之心；而祀典之舉，肇于力農，則宜稼于
translation_en: … fails to receive blessings, it means the spirits do not partake of the offerings, and our filial sincerity has not yet inspired trust. Could our dukes and ministers be like this? When ritual ceremonies are carried on for a long time, one's strength is exhausted and it is easy to commit faults. Now, from the invocation of the spirits all the way to the presentation of offerings to the impersonator of the dead, although the time is long, the sincerity of their utmost reverence grows ever more devout; although their strength is exhausted, their unfailing thoughtfulness never slackens. Indeed, whether prepared as ritual offerings or manifested as ritual demeanor, in nothing do they ever err—truly fulfilling their reverence in the most reverent way. Thereupon, when the invocators convey the will of the spirits to bestow blessings upon the filial descendant, what is it like? It may be said: A sacrifice has food and drink, and fragrance and purity are their highest perfection. Now that they are so sweet and fragrant, and there is nothing that the spirits do not relish, the spirits foretell for you a hundred blessings, drawing the analogy from the food and drink: they come at the proper time, and are as abundant as the proper measure; the manifold felicitous signs and the manifold delicacies correspond to one another! Why is this? Because reverence is made manifest in the offerings, and the [bestowal of] a hundred blessings is due to that reverence, not to the offerings themselves. A sacrifice has ritual demeanor, and solemnity and reverence are its highest perfection. Now that the participants are so grave and brisk, upright and cautious, and there is nothing that the spirits do not delight in, the spirits forever bestow upon you the highest standard of perfection, drawing the analogy from the ritual demeanor: a myriad blessings in due season, a hundred million blessings in due season; the abundant blessings and the abundant ceremonies correspond to one another! Why is this? Because reverence is seen in the demeanor, and the bestowal of the highest perfection is due to that reverence, not to the demeanor itself. Thus the performance of the rites is circumspect and filial sincerity is complete; the response in kind is swift and the manifest way is illuminated. That the dukes and ministers fulfill the meaning of sacrifice like this—if not for flourishing virtue and well-cultivated governance, how could they achieve it? Yet not seeking [blessings] is the sacrifice of a filial son; why then do the words of blessing reward him by responding in kind? title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者常存嚴翼之思尚其敬之哉敬之哉而何言
乎其當敬也蓋人君所事者惟天而其所以得
爲天子者惟其受天之命也今以言乎天命則
冲漠無朕之中而監觀爲之有赫其克敬也天
必知之而命之留者恒因之其所以使命之必
我留者不易也太虛無物之表而臨下爲之孔
昭其弗敬也天必知之而命之去者恒因之其
所以使命之不我去者不易也知天之惟顯則
當思所以格天知命之不易則當思所以保命
===
卽日兢業以圖之猶懼天之難忱而命之不常
也尚可以不敬哉吁周臣以此告成王而王且
述之則所以祈天永命者必有道矣抑是道也
固心法也亦周之家法也文之敬止武之敬勝
謨烈昭然在也何他求乎卒之成王能緝熈光
明而夙夜敬止凡以畏天之威而繼序不忘也
其用諸臣之言而以法祖爲事者乎是故思敬
天者惟在於法祖
春秋
punctuated:
者，常存嚴翼之思，尚其敬之哉！「敬之哉」，而何言乎其當敬也？蓋人君所事者惟天，而其所以得爲天子者，惟其受天之命也。今以言乎天命，則冲漠無朕之中，而監觀爲之有赫。其克敬也，天必知之，而命之留者恒因之；其所以使命之必我留者，不易也。太虛無物之表，而臨下爲之孔昭。其弗敬也，天必知之，而命之去者恒因之；其所以使命之不我去者，不易也。知天之惟顯，則當思所以格天；知命之不易，則當思所以保命。即日兢業以圖之，猶懼天之難忱而命之不常也，尚可以不敬哉！吁，周臣以此告成王，而王且述之，則所以祈天永命者必有道矣。抑是道也，固心法也，亦周之家法也。文之敬止，武之敬勝，謨烈昭然在也，何他求乎？卒之成王能緝熈光明，而夙夜敬止，凡以畏天之威，而繼序不忘也。其用諸臣之言，而以法祖爲事者乎！是故思敬天者，惟在於法祖。

《春秋》
translation_en:
… should always maintain thoughts of solemn reverence—may you be reverent, may you be reverent! In saying "Be reverent!", why does one speak of the necessity of being reverent? For what a ruler of men serves is solely Heaven, and the reason he is able to be the Son of Heaven is solely that he has received the Mandate of Heaven. Now, to speak of the Mandate of Heaven: within the vast emptiness where there is no visible sign, its inspection and observation are nonetheless resplendent. When one is able to be reverent, Heaven surely knows it, and the retention of the Mandate invariably follows upon it; yet bringing it about that the Mandate will surely remain with us is not easy. Beyond the great void where there is no physical form, its oversight of the world below is nonetheless abundantly clear. When one is not reverent, Heaven surely knows it, and the departure of the Mandate invariably follows upon it; yet bringing it about that the Mandate will not depart from us is not easy. Knowing that Heaven is so manifest, one ought to ponder how to reach Heaven; knowing that the Mandate is not easy to keep, one ought to ponder how to preserve the Mandate. Even if one strives for it day by day with cautiousness and trembling, one still fears that Heaven is hard to rely upon and that the Mandate is not constant—how, then, could one fail to be reverent! Alas, the ministers of Zhou admonished King Cheng with these words, and the King moreover recounted them; thus there must have been a Way by which he prayed to Heaven for a lasting Mandate. Furthermore, this Way is indeed the method of the mind, and it is also the family tradition of the house of Zhou. The resting in reverence of King Wen and the triumph through reverence of King Wu—their counsels and achievements are brightly preserved; why seek elsewhere? In the end, King Cheng was able to continue the bright glory and be reverent from dawn to night, all because he stood in awe of the majesty of Heaven and did not forget to carry on the succession. Did he not employ the words of his ministers and make emulating his ancestors his task? Therefore, for one who wishes to revere Heaven, it lies solely in emulating one's ancestors.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
春秋
楚人侵鄭〔僖公二年〕齊人執陳轅濤塗〔僖
公四年〕
方學龍
同考試官訓導趙批詞平平爾而曲折開闔
處卓有先輩矩矱豈以格勝者乎取之
考試官教諭程批格嚴語練
考試官教諭周批明整
伯德之勤怠於人心之思斁驗之矣此鄭被兵
而興思陳同好而見斁皆由於桓德之所召也
嘗謂王伯之辨惟德之誠偽爾王者感人惟誠
故人心思之愈久不忘伯者異是有思未幾而
厭即至矣何不引齊桓之事明之夫鄭之見侵
於楚也以即夏也於時聃伯被囚鄭患蓋孔棘
矣使桓無德以聯其志則鋌而走險奚擇焉惟
自會檉以來念深禮謹志切安攘彼鄭亦已諒
之故三揖可擒五廟可震寧以國斃而不肯納
款於南荆也觀孔叔之言曰齊方勤我棄德不
祥吁名其為德且完守以待之思可知也古有
punctuated:
春秋

「楚人侵鄭」〔僖公二年〕，「齊人執陳轅濤塗」〔僖公四年〕。

方學龍

同考試官訓導趙批：詞平平爾，而曲折開闔處卓有先輩矩矱，豈以格勝者乎？取之。
考試官教諭程批：格嚴語練。
考試官教諭周批：明整。

伯德之勤怠，於人心之思斁驗之矣。此鄭被兵而興思，陳同好而見斁，皆由於桓德之所召也。嘗謂王伯之辨，惟德之誠偽爾。王者感人惟誠，故人心思之，愈久不忘；伯者異是，有思未幾，而厭即至矣。何不引齊桓之事明之？夫鄭之見侵於楚也，以即夏也。於時聃伯被囚，鄭患蓋孔棘矣。使桓無德以聯其志，則鋌而走險，奚擇焉？惟自會檉以來，念深禮謹，志切安攘，彼鄭亦已諒之。故三揖可擒，五廟可震，寧以國斃，而不肯納款於南荆也。觀孔叔之言曰：「齊方勤我，棄德不祥。」吁！名其為德，且完守以待之，思可知也。古有
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"The people of Chu invaded Zheng" [Second year of Duke Xi]; "The people of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen" [Fourth year of Duke Xi].

Fang Xuelong 方學龍

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhao comments: The diction is quite plain, yet in its twists and turns, openings and closings, it outstandingly possesses the standards and rules of our predecessors. Is it not one that prevails through structure? Selected.
Examiner and Instructor Cheng comments: Strict in structure and polished in phrasing.
Examiner and Instructor Zhou comments: Clear and well-ordered.

The diligence or laxity of a hegemon's virtue is verified by whether people's hearts long for him or grow weary of him. Thus, that Zheng suffered military attack and yet felt longing, while Chen shared in friendly alliance and yet showed weariness, were both brought about by the virtue of Duke Huan. It has been said that the distinction between a true king and a hegemon lies solely in the sincerity or falsity of their virtue. A true king moves people solely through sincerity, and therefore people's hearts long for him, never forgetting him the longer time passes. A hegemon is different from this: people long for him for scarcely any time before weariness immediately arrives. Why not cite the affairs of Duke Huan of Qi to clarify this? Now, that Zheng was invaded by Chu was because it aligned with the central states (Xia). At that time, Danbo 聃伯 was taken prisoner, and Zheng's troubles were indeed extremely urgent. Had Duke Huan lacked the virtue to bind their resolve, then in desperation they would have taken a reckless course—what choice would they have made? Only because ever since the meeting at Cheng 檉, his concern had been deep, his propriety cautious, and his ambition earnestly set on pacifying the states and repelling the barbarians, Zheng for its part already trusted him. Therefore, though its commander at the three bows before battle might be captured and its five ancestral temples shaken, it would rather perish as a state than be willing to submit tribute to southern Jing [Chu]. Observe the words of Kong Shu 孔叔, who said: "Qi is just now laboring on our behalf; to abandon its virtue would be inauspicious." Alas! Calling it virtue, and moreover keeping their defenses intact in order to await him—their longing can thus be known. In antiquity there was…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
樹破斧之勛而致思皇四國者桓其庶幾矣乎
陳大夫之見執於齊也以誤師也當時盟楚而
歸陳適當孔道矣使桓無闕以携其心則敬共
往來曷二焉惟自服楚以後志驕氣溢漸異曩
時彼陳已竊異之故慮其誅求懼其撫樑寧以
見討而直欲避兵於東夷也觀轅濤塗之言曰
師出陳鄭國必甚病吁策其必病且設謀以誤
之斁可知也古有抱隕淵之懼而永撫有萬方
者桓其少愧矣乎夫以德之勤卽反覆如鄭可
===
使委心於我繼之以怠宇下之陳不免斁心焉
甚矣感人當以誠也此王伯之分也說者謂鄭
之勤也親暱罔棄也仲之斁也執陳之日仲不
在側耶無亦積慮以圖所志惟一楚乎楚服而
臣主德色寢不如昔有以也噫此伯者所以爲
假而管仲君子不爲與
春白狄來襄公十有八年
施夢麟
punctuated:
樹破斧之勛，而致思皇四國者，桓其庶幾矣乎！陳大夫之見執於齊也，以誤師也。當時盟楚而歸，陳適當孔道矣。使桓無闕以携其心，則敬共往來，曷二焉？惟自服楚以後，志驕氣溢，漸異曩時，彼陳已竊異之。故慮其誅求，懼其撫樑，寧以見討，而直欲避兵於東夷也。觀轅濤塗之言曰：「師出陳、鄭，國必甚病。」吁！策其必病，且設謀以誤之，斁可知也。古有抱隕淵之懼，而永撫有萬方者，桓其少愧矣乎！夫以德之勤，卽反覆如鄭，可使委心於我；繼之以怠，宇下之陳，不免斁心焉。甚矣，感人當以誠也！此王伯之分也。說者謂鄭之勤也，親暱罔棄也；仲之斁也，執陳之日，仲不在側耶？無亦積慮以圖，所志惟一楚乎？楚服而臣主德色，寢不如昔，有以也。噫！此伯者所以爲假，而管仲君子不爲與！
春，白狄來。襄公十有八年。
施夢麟
translation_en:
…achieved the merit of the "Broken Axes" (Pofu) ode and caused the four quarters to long for him as their glorious model—did Duke Huan not come close to that! As for the grandee of Chen being seized by Qi, it was because he misdirected the army. At that time, returning after making a covenant with Chu, Chen happened to lie directly along the main thoroughfare. Had Duke Huan lacked no virtue to alienate their hearts, they would have respectfully supplied the passing troops—how could they have been duplicitous? Only after he had subdued Chu did his ambition grow arrogant and his spirit overflow, gradually differing from former times; Chen had already privately noted the change. Therefore, worrying about his exactions and fearing his foraging and provisions [? 撫樑, for 芻糧], they preferred to risk being punished by a punitive expedition and simply wished to divert the troops toward the Eastern Yi. Look at the words of Yuan Taotu: "If the army marches out through Chen and Zheng, our states will certainly suffer grievously." Alas! Calculating that they would certainly suffer, and moreover devising a scheme to misdirect them, shows how weary of him they had become. In antiquity there was one who held the fear of falling into an abyss and forever cherished and possessed the myriad regions—must Duke Huan not feel a little ashamed before him! Indeed, through diligence in virtue, even a vacillating state like Zheng could be made to entrust its heart to us; when followed by indolence, even a sheltered state like Chen could not avoid growing weary at heart. How true it is that moving people must be done with sincerity! This is the distinction between the True King and the Hegemon. Commentators say that the diligence toward Zheng was because Guan Zhong did not abandon intimate allies; as for the weariness toward him—on the day Chen's grandee was seized, was Guan Zhong not by his side? Was it not rather that in accumulating their deliberations and plans, their sole ambition lay in Chu alone? Once Chu submitted, both minister and ruler put on airs of self-satisfaction, and things gradually ceased to be as they were in the past—there was a reason for it. Alas! Is this not why the Hegemon is considered a fabrication of virtue, and why a gentleman would not do as Guan Zhong did?

"In spring, the White Di came." Eighteenth year of Duke Xiang.
By Shi Menglin.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
子獨探其大旨而詞復偉雋是苦心者錄之
考試官教諭程批得聖人意
考試官教諭周批詞旨明確
春秋於外夷交內而深示謹防之意焉蓋防正
而后淫慝之患可弭也經於白狄之來所爲深
致意與昔白狄世處陰山與曲阜不通舊矣一
旦藩飾而來倘亦徼福於周公以踵越裳之遺
意乎君子則曰狄非可朝於魯也而魯何爲受
之蓋中國與夷狄畫疆而居無時可通者故以
===
天子之尊且世僅一見焉以元聖之德且不享
其物焉其所以正防而禁慝固甚嚴也魯也龜
蒙之封無改於舊成襄以來代有失德何政而
格於狄今之來也果款我乎抑嘗我乎未可知
也馳一介而拒之國門斯非魯之所得爲者哉
顧乃位非天子而徒慕柔遠之名德非聖人而
妄徼執贄之獻其亦不自量也已想其受玉於
庭薦器於廟魯之君臣色動亦以爲一時盛美
矣獨不思無故而涉吾之境其漸不可長也非
punctuated:
子獨探其大旨，而詞復偉雋，是苦心者，錄之。
考試官教諭程批：得聖人意。
考試官教諭周批：詞旨明確。
《春秋》於外夷交內，而深示謹防之意焉。蓋防正而后淫慝之患可弭也，經於白狄之來，所爲深致意與？昔白狄世處陰山，與曲阜不通舊矣。一旦藩飾而來，倘亦徼福於周公，以踵越裳之遺意乎？君子則曰：狄非可朝於魯也，而魯何爲受之？蓋中國與夷狄畫疆而居，無時可通者。故以天子之尊，且世僅一見焉；以元聖之德，且不享其物焉。其所以正防而禁慝，固甚嚴也。魯也，龜蒙之封無改於舊，成、襄以來，代有失德，何政而格於狄？今之來也，果款我乎？抑嘗我乎？未可知也。馳一介而拒之國門，斯非魯之所得爲者哉？顧乃位非天子，而徒慕柔遠之名；德非聖人，而妄徼執贄之獻，其亦不自量也已。想其受玉於庭，薦器於廟，魯之君臣色動，亦以爲一時盛美矣。獨不思無故而涉吾之境，其漸不可長也；非
