…[This gentleman] alone has fathomed its main purport, and his diction is moreover magnificent and incisive; he is one who has labored painstakingly, so we record it.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Cheng's comment: He has grasped the Sage's intent.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zhou's comment: The diction and purport are clear and precise.
When outer barbarians enter into intercourse with the interior, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) deeply conveys the intent of maintaining strict precautions. Indeed, only after the defenses are rectified can the perils of licentiousness and evil be forestalled; is this not why the Classic expresses such profound intent regarding the coming of the White Di (Baidi)? In the past, the White Di resided for generations in the Yin Mountains (Yinshan) and since antiquity had no communication with Qufu. When one day they came arrayed as feudatories, were they perhaps seeking blessings from the Duke of Zhou, following in the lingering spirit of the Yuechang? Yet the gentleman says: The Di are not such as may pay court to Lu; why then did Lu receive them? Indeed, the Central States and the barbarians dwell with demarcated borders, and there is no time when they should have free intercourse. Therefore, even with the exalted status of the Son of Heaven, they are granted an audience only once in a generation; even with the virtue of the Great Sage, their goods are not accepted as offerings. The means by which defenses are rectified and evils prohibited are truly most strict. As for Lu, its enfeoffment around Mounts Gui and Meng had not changed from of old, and since the reigns of Dukes Cheng and Xiang, generation after generation had suffered lapses in virtue—by what governance could it have reached and moved the Di? In their coming now, are they truly sincere toward us, or are they testing us? It cannot be known. To dispatch a single emissary to turn them away at the gates of the capital—was this not something within Lu's power to do? Instead, though not holding the position of the Son of Heaven, they vainly coveted the reputation of cherishing the distant; though not possessing the virtue of a sage, they rashly sought offerings presented as ceremonial gifts—how utterly they failed to take their own measure! One can imagine that when they received the jade in the court and presented the vessels in the ancestral temple, the ruler and ministers of Lu were visibly moved, regarding it as a splendid triumph of the age. Yet they alone failed to reflect that for outsiders to cross into our territory without cause is a tendency that must not be allowed to grow; and when [those beyond]…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所及而妄受人之朝其禮不可行也率是爲之
是使異類得接軫於神明之區內外之防紊矣
狡焉得肆乎窺伺之計淫慝之禍滋矣世道之
亂也其何日之有故春秋直書白狄曰來而不
與其朝所以一內外懲淫慝也而譏魯之意至
深切矣惟此義不明然后有與夷狄交婚居羌
胡內塞蓋至於中原多事神州陸沉而后知聖
人謹白狄之意深也彼有閉關謝西域者其庶
幾得春秋之旨
===
禮記
是故樂之隆非極音也食饗之禮非致味
也清廟之瑟朱絃而疏越壹倡而三歎
有遺音者矣大饗之禮尚玄酒而俎腥
魚大羹不和有遺味者矣
李繼韶
同考試官訓導王批體認親切而鎔詞布調
咸歸大雅子殆深於禮樂者
考試官教諭程批和平之音
punctuated:
所及而妄受人之朝，其禮不可行也。率是爲之，是使異類得接軫於神明之區，內外之防紊矣；狡焉得肆乎窺伺之計，淫慝之禍滋矣。世道之亂也，其何日之有！故《春秋》直書白狄曰「來」，而不與其朝，所以一內外、懲淫慝也，而譏魯之意至深切矣。惟此義不明，然后有與夷狄交婚、居羌胡內塞，蓋至於中原多事、神州陸沉，而后知聖人謹白狄之意深也。彼有閉關謝西域者，其庶幾得《春秋》之旨。
《禮記》
「是故樂之隆，非極音也；食饗之禮，非致味也。清廟之瑟，朱絃而疏越，壹倡而三歎，有遺音者矣。大饗之禮，尚玄酒而俎腥魚，大羹不和，有遺味者矣。」
李繼韶
同考試官訓導王批：體認親切，而鎔詞布調，咸歸大雅，子殆深於禮樂者。
考試官教諭程批：和平之音。
translation_en:
…beyond their station and rashly receive the court visit of others—such a rite cannot be practiced. To act along these lines is to allow alien peoples to link their carriage-crossbars within the realm of the spirits and sages, throwing the boundary between inner and outer into disorder; and to let the cunning indulge their schemes of spying and probing, multiplying the disasters of licentious evil. How long could it then be before the way of the world fell into chaos? Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) directly records of the White Di (Baidi) that they "came" (lai), without granting them the term "paid a court visit" (chao), in order to unify the distinction between inner and outer and to chastise licentious evil; its intent in criticizing Lu is most profound and trenchant. Only when this principle became obscured did people later intermarry with the Yi and Di barbarians and settle Qiang and Hu tribes within the inner frontier—until at length the Central Plains were beset with troubles and the sacred land sank into ruin, and only then did men realize how deep was the Sage's intent in guarding strictly against the White Di. As for the one who closed the passes and declined relations with the Western Regions, he came close indeed to grasping the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Record of Rites (Liji)

"For this reason, the height of music does not lie in the utmost indulgence of sound; the rites of banquets and feasts do not lie in the perfection of flavors. The zither of the 'Pure Temple' (Qingmiao) has vermilion strings and widely spaced sound-holes; when one leads the chant and three join in sighing response, there is a lingering sound left unexhausted. In the ceremony of the Great Banquet, plain water is esteemed as the highest libation, raw fish is placed upon the offering-stand, and the great broth is unseasoned; there is a lingering flavor left unexhausted."

Li Jishao 李繼韶

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Wang: His personal comprehension is intimate and genuine, and his casting of diction and arrangement of cadence all return to refined elegance; you are surely one who is deeply versed in rites and music.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Cheng: The sound of harmony and peace.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而致味乎哉是蓋求禮樂于音味之內其機也
淺禮樂皆虛也求禮樂于音味之外其蓄也深
禮樂皆實也君子察此可以明禮樂矣抑考諸
易曰殷薦上帝傳曰告民力之普存則音與味
顧可少與吁記者特爲徇末忘本者戒耳後世
不探其本而徒於鐘鼓籩豆之間求之抑末矣
其如禮樂何哉是故禮樂之興蓋必有中正和
平之蘊者而後可
子云善則稱君過則稱已則民作忠君陳
===
曰爾有嘉謀嘉猷入告爾君于內女乃
順之于外曰此謀此猷惟我君之德於
乎是惟良顯哉
陳治則
同考試官訓導王批人臣忠君之義闡明殆
盡而一結尤見忠悃
考試官教諭程批冲淡中有逸趣
考試官教諭周批沉著醇雅
人臣忠君之化觀諸書而可證也夫事君以忠
punctuated:
而致味乎哉？是蓋求禮樂于音味之內，其機也淺，禮樂皆虛也；求禮樂于音味之外，其蓄也深，禮樂皆實也。君子察此，可以明禮樂矣。抑考諸《易》曰「殷薦上帝」，《傳》曰「告民力之普存」，則音與味顧可少與？吁！記者特爲徇末忘本者戒耳。後世不探其本，而徒於鐘鼓籩豆之間求之，抑末矣，其如禮樂何哉？是故禮樂之興，蓋必有中正和平之蘊者而後可。

子云：「善則稱君，過則稱已，則民作忠。《君陳》曰：『爾有嘉謀嘉猷，入告爾君于內，女乃順之于外，曰：「此謀此猷，惟我君之德。」於乎！是惟良顯哉！』」
陳治則
同考試官訓導王批：人臣忠君之義，闡明殆盡，而一結尤見忠悃。
考試官教諭程批：冲淡中有逸趣。
考試官教諭周批：沉著醇雅。

人臣忠君之化，觀諸《書》而可證也。夫事君以忠，
translation_en:
… so as to produce flavor? For to seek ritual and music within mere sound and flavor is shallow in its working, and both ritual and music become empty; to seek ritual and music beyond sound and flavor is deep in its accumulation, and both ritual and music become substantial. If the gentleman examines this, he can understand ritual and music. Yet if we examine the Book of Changes (Yi), which says, "offering grand sacrifices to the Lord on High," and the Zuo Commentary (Zhuan), which says, "announcing that the people's strength is universally preserved," then how could sound and flavor after all be dispensed with? Alas! The compiler of the Record of Rites (Liji) merely meant this as a warning for those who pursue the branches and forget the root. When later generations do not probe into the root, but merely seek it among bells, drums, bamboo vessels, and wooden platters, that is indeed superficial—what can that do for ritual and music? Therefore, for ritual and music to flourish, there must first be one who possesses the inner store of impartiality, correctness, harmony, and peace.

The Master said: "When there is goodness, attribute it to the ruler; when there is fault, attribute it to oneself—then the people will be stirred to loyalty. The 'Jun Chen' (君陳) says: 'When you have admirable plans and admirable counsels, enter and announce them to your ruler within; and then, complying with them on the outside, say: "This plan, this counsel, is wholly due to our ruler's virtue." Oh! It is in this way that you will be truly良 (good) and顯 (illustrious)!'"

By Chen Zhize 陳治則.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor (xundao) Wang comments: The principle of a minister's loyalty to his ruler is expounded almost exhaustively, and the conclusion especially reveals sincere loyalty.
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Cheng comments: Amid placid simplicity there is a transcendent charm.
Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhou comments: Composed, pure, and elegant.

The transforming influence of a minister's loyalty to his ruler can be verified by examining the Book of Documents (Shu). Now, to serve one's ruler with loyalty…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
臣道也而民皆化之可謂良顯矣雖書詞所稱
奚加焉夫子之意謂夫人臣一身君之輔民之
表也惟不能效忠於君斯不能作忠于民難以
語良顯矣誠知善本人所樂道而况臣之於君
有頌德之義焉故無論君之盛德不敢竊爲已
功即善之在我亦舉而讓諸君焉若曰主上聖
明臣子何庸也過本不當自文而况臣之於君
有引慝之分焉故無論吾之失德不敢曲爲掩
護即過之在君亦舉而任諸已焉若曰臣職曠
===
違天王何愆也如是則於其稱君也可以觀忠
愛焉而民之遵化者咸起夫頌德之忱於其稱
已也可以觀忠謹焉而民之仰承者咸萌夫引
慝之志始焉以一人之忠作萬民之忠既焉合
萬民之忠皆一人之忠若而臣也誠哉其良顯
矣君陳有云嘉謀嘉猷入而告之于內此謀此
猷出而順之于外而以良顯稱焉吾謂在君陳
以忠于爾后者而垂于紀載固示天下以人臣
之極在君子以忠於吾君者而率乎斯民亦可
punctuated:
臣道也，而民皆化之，可謂良顯矣。雖《書》詞所稱，奚加焉？

夫子之意，謂夫人臣一身，君之輔、民之表也。惟不能效忠於君，斯不能作忠于民，難以語良顯矣。誠知善本人所樂道，而况臣之於君，有頌德之義焉。故無論君之盛德不敢竊爲已功，即善之在我，亦舉而讓諸君焉，若曰：「主上聖明，臣子何庸也？」過本不當自文，而况臣之於君，有引慝之分焉。故無論吾之失德不敢曲爲掩護，即過之在君，亦舉而任諸已焉，若曰：「臣職曠違，天王何愆也？」

如是，則於其稱君也，可以觀忠愛焉，而民之遵化者咸起夫頌德之忱；於其稱已也，可以觀忠謹焉，而民之仰承者咸萌夫引慝之志。始焉以一人之忠作萬民之忠，既焉合萬民之忠皆一人之忠。若而臣也，誠哉其良顯矣！

《君陳》有云：「嘉謀嘉猷，入而告之于內；此謀此猷，出而順之于外。」而以「良顯」稱焉。吾謂在君陳，以忠于爾后者而垂于紀載，固示天下以人臣之極；在君子，以忠於吾君者而率乎斯民，亦可
translation_en:
… is the Way of the minister, and when the common people are all transformed by it, he may indeed be called virtuous and illustrious. Even what is praised in the words of the Book of Documents (Shu)—what could be added to this?

The Master's meaning is that a minister, in his own person, is an assistant to his ruler and an exemplar to the people. Only when he fails to devote his loyalty to his ruler is he unable to inspire loyalty in the people, and then it becomes difficult to speak of him as virtuous and illustrious.

If he truly understands that goodness is by nature what people delight in speaking of, how much more so does a minister toward his ruler have the duty of extolling his virtue! Therefore, not to mention that he would never dare to claim his ruler's abundant virtue as his own merit, even when goodness lies within himself, he attributes and yields it all to his ruler, as if to say: "His Majesty is sagely and enlightened; what credit belongs to his subject?" And since faults ought never to be glossed over for oneself, how much more so does a minister toward his ruler have the obligation to take blame upon himself! Therefore, not to mention that he would never dare to artfully cover up his own lapses in virtue, even when the fault lies with his ruler, he takes it all upon himself, as if to say: "Your servant has neglected and violated his official duties; what error has the Heavenly King committed?"

When he acts like this, in the way he speaks of his ruler one may observe his loyal affection, and the people who follow his transforming influence will all be stirred with sincere devotion to extol the ruler's virtue; in the way he speaks of himself one may observe his loyal circumspection, and the people who look up to and follow him will all conceive the resolve to take blame upon themselves. At first, the loyalty of a single man inspires the loyalty of the myriad people; in the end, the combined loyalty of the myriad people is wholly the loyalty of that single man. A minister such as this is truly virtuous and illustrious!

The "Jun Chen" chapter says: "Your fine plans and fine counsels, enter and present them within; these plans and these counsels, go forth and comply with them without," and thus praises him as "virtuous and illustrious." I would say that in the case of Jun Chen, by being loyal to his sovereign and having this handed down in the historical records, he certainly showed the world the ultimate standard for a minister; and in the case of the noble man, by being loyal to our ruler and thereby leading these people, he too may…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
無愧于良顯之風然則爲臣而不以忠自處者
其亦未玩君陳之義云雖然讓善引過忠矣而
面折廷諍非與蓋都俞喜起上臣之至願也繩
愆糾謬諍臣之不得已也人主諒其不得已之
心而上下其交孚矣是故效忠者臣而作忠者
尤在于君
第貳場
論
天下國家之大務
===
葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳 批 天下國家之務有要有本
子能博綜玄覽出入古今經世之術具占其槩矣
同考試官教諭陳 批 不習竅言直攄要指非明
于當世之務者其何能言錄之以式多士
考試官教諭程 批 才情具足機軸圓融
考試官教諭周 批 旨明詞達
凡治之難非其治之難也有本之難有要之難
也非有本不足以
punctuated:
無愧于良顯之風。然則爲臣而不以忠自處者，其亦未玩《君陳》之義云。雖然，讓善引過，忠矣，而面折廷諍，非與？蓋都俞喜起，上臣之至願也；繩愆糾謬，諍臣之不得已也。人主諒其不得已之心，而上下其交孚矣。是故效忠者臣，而作忠者尤在于君。

第貳場

論

天下國家之大務

葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳批：天下國家之務，有要有本。子能博綜玄覽，出入古今，經世之術，具占其槩矣。
同考試官教諭陳批：不習竅言，直攄要指，非明于當世之務者，其何能言？錄之以式多士。
考試官教諭程批：才情具足，機軸圓融。
考試官教諭周批：旨明詞達。

凡治之難，非其治之難也，有本之難，有要之難也。非有本，不足以
translation_en:
…have no cause for shame before the spirit of being "good and illustrious." Thus, one who serves as a minister yet does not conduct himself with loyalty has surely not pondered the meaning of the "Jun Chen" (Book of Documents). Even so, yielding credit for goodness and taking blame for faults Upon oneself is indeed loyalty—yet are not rebuking the ruler to his face and remonstrating at court also loyalty? For harmonious assent and joyful collaboration are the highest aspiration of the finest ministers; correcting faults and rectifying errors are what a remonstrating minister does only when he has no other choice. When the ruler understands the heart of one who acts out of necessity, then sovereign and minister will share mutual trust. Therefore, while it is the minister who renders loyalty, inspiring that loyalty rests above all with the ruler.

Second Session

Discourse

"The Great Affairs of the Empire and the State"

Ye Bingjing 葉秉敬
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen comments: The affairs of the empire and the state have both essentials and fundamentals. You are able to synthesize broadly and observe profoundly, moving freely between antiquity and the present; the general outline of your art of statecraft can all be seen here.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen comments: Without resorting to empty clichés, he directly sets forth the essential points. How could anyone not well-versed in the affairs of the present age speak thus? We record it to serve as a model for the many scholars.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Cheng comments: Fully endowed with talent and sensibility, its structure and development are smooth and well-rounded.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhou comments: The central meaning is clear and the diction is expressive.

In general, the difficulty of governing does not lie in the governing itself; it lies in the difficulty of grasping the fundamentals and the difficulty of grasping the essentials. Without the fundamentals, one cannot…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
執天下之要何以故也四海之廣兆民之衆延
頸舉踵而待命于一人一人坐視而不爲之恤
則恐至于負其望起而徧爲之撫乃遂至疲神
以爲天下勞是故不可以無要操要御詳使天
下不勞而就理非藻飾之所能爲也藉第令事
事而廉之而不勝密物物而察之而不勝明是
尚焉能執其要也乎是故不可以無本知本不
匱知要不殆古之人君其于理道亦籌之熟哉
其所以成務未有不繇此者也朱子稱恤民爲
===
天下國家之大務而繼之治軍省賦歸之心術
紀綱推本考要有味哉其詳言之也可爲世世
法程至明矣嘗試論之天下國家其作室歟要
則樞也本則運是樞以開闔者也其涉川歟要
則舟楫也本則運是舟楫以有濟者也何以明
其然耶聞之曰生民有欲無主乃亂作之君作
之師惟曰其相上帝豈其以一人肆于民上而
淫焉以逞此治之不可以已也而政且鰓鰓然
民且總總然不得其要即欲成務其孰從而成
punctuated: 執天下之要。何以故也？四海之廣，兆民之衆，延頸舉踵而待命于一人。一人坐視而不爲之恤，則恐至于負其望；起而徧爲之撫，乃遂至疲神以爲天下勞。是故不可以無要。操要御詳，使天下不勞而就理，非藻飾之所能爲也。藉第令事事而廉之，而不勝密；物物而察之，而不勝明。是尚焉能執其要也乎？是故不可以無本。知本不匱，知要不殆，古之人君其于理道亦籌之熟哉！其所以成務，未有不繇此者也。朱子稱恤民爲天下國家之大務，而繼之治軍、省賦，歸之心術、紀綱，推本考要，有味哉其詳言之也！可爲世世法程，至明矣。嘗試論之：天下國家，其作室歟？要則樞也，本則運是樞以開闔者也。其涉川歟？要則舟楫也，本則運是舟楫以有濟者也。何以明其然耶？聞之曰：「生民有欲，無主乃亂。」作之君，作之師，惟曰其相上帝，豈其以一人肆于民上，而淫焉以逞？此治之不可以已也。而政且鰓鰓然，民且總總然，不得其要，即欲成務，其孰從而成
translation_en: …grasp the essentials of all under Heaven. Why is this so? Across the vastness of the four seas, the multitudes of millions of people crane their necks and stand on tiptoe waiting for commands from the One Man. If the One Man sits idly watching and does not show compassion for them, it is to be feared that he will fail their expectations; yet if he rises to personally comfort each and every one of them, he will end up exhausting his spirit in toiling for the empire. Therefore, one cannot be without essentials. Holding the essentials to govern the details, causing all under Heaven to come into order without toil—this is not something that mere superficial embellishment can achieve. Suppose one were merely to investigate every single matter—one could not be thorough enough; or examine every single thing—one could not be perceptive enough. How then could one still be able to grasp the essentials? Therefore, one cannot be without the fundamental root. Knowing the root, one is never depleted; knowing the essentials, one is never imperiled. How thoroughly the rulers of antiquity deliberated upon the way of governance! In accomplishing their affairs, there were none who did not proceed from this. Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] declared that showing compassion for the people is the great task of the empire and the state, and followed this with governing the military and reducing taxes, tracing everything back to the ruler's mind-craft and the guiding principles of statecraft. Probing the root and examining the essentials—how meaningful it is that he spoke of this in such detail! That it can serve as a model and standard for generation after generation is utterly clear. Let us venture to discuss it: Is governing the empire and the state not like building a house? The essentials are the door-pivot, while the root is that which operates this pivot to open and close it. Is it not like crossing a river? The essentials are the boat and oars, while the root is that which operates the boat and oars to achieve the crossing. How do we make it clear that this is so? We have heard it said: "The people are born with desires; without a ruler, they fall into disorder." Heaven created for them a ruler and created for them a teacher, solely that he might assist the Supreme Lord; how could it be so that the One Man might act wantonly above the people and indulge himself without restraint? This is why governance cannot be dispensed with. Yet when administrative affairs are so anxiously intricate and the people are so numerous and teeming, if one does not obtain the essentials, even if one wishes to accomplish the tasks of state, from where would one accomplish…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
賦稍稍異矣然而夏之民也寧商之民也殖周
之民也清則又何以至此極也軍農夫而賦什
一民不病征也寧獨不病征而已祗德之禹躋
敬之湯執兢之武為之次第施焉其間也由斯
以談心術本也軍賦要也審矣不省賦而恤民
枵腹而求生也不治軍而省賦反鑑而索照也
不正心術立紀綱而談軍賦蔀日冥表而怪言
影之不見也亦大惑矣知有本與要之若彼察
無本與要之若此慨然師二帝之已事由三代
===
之芳規淵乎其無思澹乎其無為凜乎如履薄
而臨深慓乎若持盈而捧玉罔甘于適罔逸于
遊罔溺志于聲色罔馳心于土木罔狹前人規
罔開後世釁以此陳紀紀必肅以此提綱綱必
振司馬董內方伯治外糜廩之軍不登于籍矣
九賦會徵九式均節朘膏之賦不入于朝矣其
閭閻必且朽貫而藏其父老必且含哺而遊其
農夫市人必且荷鍤而歌其婦人小子必且擊
甕而謠其學士大夫薦紳先生必且褒衣博帶
punctuated: 賦稍稍異矣。然而夏之民也寧，商之民也殖，周之民也清，則又何以至此極也？軍農夫而賦什一，民不病征也。寧獨不病征而已，祗德之禹、躋敬之湯、執兢之武，為之次第施焉其間也。由斯以談，心術本也，軍賦要也，審矣。不省賦而恤民，枵腹而求生也；不治軍而省賦，反鑑而索照也；不正心術、立紀綱而談軍賦，蔀日冥表而怪言影之不見也，亦大惑矣。知有本與要之若彼，察無本與要之若此，慨然師二帝之已事，由三代之芳規，淵乎其無思，澹乎其無為，凜乎如履薄而臨深，慓乎若持盈而捧玉，罔甘于適，罔逸于遊，罔溺志于聲色，罔馳心于土木，罔狹前人規，罔開後世釁。以此陳紀，紀必肅；以此提綱，綱必振。司馬董內，方伯治外，糜廩之軍不登于籍矣；九賦會徵，九式均節，朘膏之賦不入于朝矣。其閭閻必且朽貫而藏，其父老必且含哺而遊，其農夫市人必且荷鍤而歌，其婦人小子必且擊甕而謠，其學士大夫、薦紳先生必且褒衣博帶，
translation_en: … military and tax systems differed slightly. Yet the people of the Xia were tranquil, the people of the Shang flourished, and the people of the Zhou were pure—how then did they reach such utmost perfection? Soldiers were drawn from farmers and taxes were one-tenth of the yield, so the people did not suffer from levies. And it was not merely that they did not suffer from levies: Yu in his reverent virtue, Tang in his ascending respectfulness, and Wu in his steadfast caution implemented their measures in due order throughout that time. Speaking from this perspective, it is clear that the disposition of the ruler's mind is the root, and the military and taxation are the essentials. To show compassion for the people without reducing taxes is like seeking to stay alive on an empty stomach; to reduce taxes without putting the military in order is like turning a mirror backward and looking for a reflection; to discuss the military and taxation without rectifying the disposition of the mind and establishing the threads of governance and great principles is like screening off the sun to darken the gnomon while wondering why no shadow is seen—this too is a great delusion! Knowing how possessing the root and essentials leads to that former state, and observing how lacking the root and essentials leads to this latter state, if the ruler resolutely takes as his model the past deeds of the Two Emperors and follows the fine regulations of the Three Dynasties—abyssal in his thoughtlessness, tranquil in his non-action, awe-inspired as if treading on thin ice or approaching a deep abyss, cautious as if holding a full vessel or clasping jade; never indulging in comfort, never idling in excursions, never drowning his will in music and beauty, never letting his mind run wild on construction projects, never narrowing the plans of his predecessors, and never opening rifts for future generations—then when he sets forth the threads of governance by these means, they will surely be solemn; when he upholds the great principles by these means, they will surely be invigorated. With the Minister of War supervising the interior and the Regional Earls governing the exterior, soldiers who merely waste grain stipends will not be entered on the registers; with the Nine Revenues calculating the levies and the Nine Formulas equalizing and regulating expenditures, taxes that drain the fat and lifeblood of the people will not enter the court. In the villages and lanes, strings of cash will surely rot away in storage; the elders will surely stroll about with food in their mouths; the farmers and townspeople will surely carry their spades on their shoulders and sing; the women and children will surely drum on earthen jars and chant folksongs; and the scholars, grandees, and gentry will surely wear wide robes and broad sashes, …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
安行徐言而無所却顧煕煕乎穆穆乎扇六合
以淳風闥八荒如同室斯誠得當唐虞三代哉
乃無異故其所以成務者有要而有本也辟之
工倕作室津人操舟樞運而楫利何窹力焉也
後治卑卑無足語此周衰而降漢唐已逺不逮
至宋而陵替加焉庸可幾乎朱子所以歔欷感
嘆而三致意也彼其內政不脩外侵孔亟安有
天下阽危若是而上不驚者則亦無得于其本
無見于其要焉耳此可謂不知務矣向令端本
===
而操要以圖大務何至軍驕食冗賦蹙民窮一
折而入于夷哉故夫朱子之未試其言朱子之
深憂也有天下國家之責者誠得其說而行之
則幾矣
表
擬
御製輔臣賛和詩集序
示大學士楊一清等謝表〔嘉靖七年〕姜詵
punctuated:
安行徐言，而無所却顧。煕煕乎，穆穆乎，扇六合以淳風，闥八荒如同室，斯誠得當唐、虞、三代哉！乃無異故，其所以成務者，有要而有本也。辟之工倕作室，津人操舟，樞運而楫利，何窹力焉也？後治卑卑，無足語此。周衰而降，漢、唐已逺不逮，至宋而陵替加焉，庸可幾乎？朱子所以歔欷感嘆而三致意也。彼其內政不脩，外侵孔亟，安有天下阽危若是而上不驚者？則亦無得于其本，無見于其要焉耳，此可謂不知務矣。向令端本而操要，以圖大務，何至軍驕食冗，賦蹙民窮，一折而入于夷哉？故夫朱子之未試其言，朱子之深憂也。有天下國家之責者，誠得其說而行之，則幾矣。

表
擬御製《輔臣賛和詩集序》，示大學士楊一清等謝表〔嘉靖七年〕
姜詵
translation_en:
…walk calmly and speak unhurriedly, without looking back in apprehension. How harmonious, how majestic! Fanning the six directions with pure customs and opening the eight荒wildernesses as if they were a single chamber—this would truly match the ages of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties! This is for no other reason than that the means by which affairs are accomplished possess both the essentials and the fundamentals. Compare it to Master Artisan Chui building a house or a ferryman steering a boat: when the pivot turns and the oar moves smoothly, what need is there to exhaust [?] one's strength?

Later governance was base and unworthy of discussing this. From the decline of the Zhou onward, the Han and Tang already fell far short; by the Song, decline and deterioration grew even worse—how could they come close to it? This is why Master Zhu [Zhu Xi] sighed with deep emotion and repeatedly dwelled upon the thought. When domestic governance was not put in order and foreign invasions were exceedingly urgent, how could the realm be in such perilous danger without the ruler above being alarmed? It was simply that they had neither grasped the fundamentals nor perceived the essentials; this may be called not knowing what is of foremost importance. Had they rectified the fundamentals and grasped the essentials in planning great affairs, how would it have come to the point where the army grew arrogant and rations redundant, taxes became oppressive and the people impoverished, collapsing at a single blow and falling to the barbarians? Therefore, that Master Zhu's words were never put to the test was Master Zhu's profound sorrow. If those who bear responsibility for the realm and the state truly grasp his teachings and put them into practice, they will be near the mark.

Memorial
Imitation of a Memorial by Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing 楊一清 and Others Giving Thanks Upon Being Shown the Imperially Composed "Preface to the Collection of Poems in Praise and Harmony with the Grand Secretaries" [7th year of the Jiajing reign (1528)]
Jiang Shen 姜詵

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導龍批頌而無諂進不忘規深
得人臣對
君之體且其藻繪不煩莊嚴自在直軼唐宋而上之宜錄以式
考試官教諭程批抒思微婉摛詞藻麗讀
之當時賡和之意宛然
考試官教諭周批莊重典則非馳騁浮靡者
嘉靖七年正月某日具官臣楊一清等伏
蒙
聖恩以臣等元旦日恭和
===
===
御製五言律詩彙爲一册仍
親序其端名曰輔臣贊和詩集序
頒示臣等臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首稱
謝者
皇綸晉錫煥
九重奎璧之章
聖德謙光啓千載地
天之泰采菲葑而罔棄
冠琬琰以增榮拜手祗承靦顏知愧竊惟詩
punctuated:
同考試官訓導龍批：頌而無諂，進不忘規，深得人臣對君之體。且其藻繪不煩，莊嚴自在，直軼唐、宋而上之，宜錄以式。
考試官教諭程批：抒思微婉，摛詞藻麗，讀之當時賡和之意宛然。
考試官教諭周批：莊重典則，非馳騁浮靡者。
嘉靖七年正月某日，具官臣楊一清等伏蒙聖恩，以臣等元旦日恭和御製五言律詩彙爲一册，仍親序其端，名曰《輔臣贊和詩集序》，頒示臣等。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首稱謝者。皇綸晉錫，煥九重奎璧之章；聖德謙光，啓千載地天之泰。采菲葑而罔棄，冠琬琰以增榮。拜手祗承，靦顏知愧。竊惟詩
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Long: It praises without flattery and offers words to the throne without forgetting to remonstrate, deeply grasping the proper form for a minister addressing his sovereign. Moreover, its literary ornamentation is not overwrought, and its solemn dignity comes naturally, directly surpassing the Tang and Song dynasties to reach a higher plane. It ought to be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Cheng: It expresses thoughts with subtle elegance and sets forth words with ornate beauty. Reading it, the spirit of exchanging poems in harmony at that time comes vividly to life.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zhou: Solemn, dignified, and governed by classic norms—not the work of one who indulges in unbridled and superficial华丽 (floridity).

On a certain day in the first month of the seventh year of the Jiajing reign [1528], your servants holding full official titles, Yang Yiqing and others, humbly received the Sacred Grace, whereby the five-syllable regulated verses that your servants reverently composed on New Year's Day to match the Imperially Composed poem were compiled into a single volume, with a preface personally written by Your Majesty at its head, entitled Preface to the Collection of Poems by Assisting Ministers Matching in Harmony (Fuchen zanhe shiji xu), and promulgated and shown to your servants. With utmost trepidation and awe, your servants bow our heads to the ground and offer thanks:

The Imperial words are generously bestowed, illuminating a literary work of stellar and jade-like brilliance from the ninefold palace; the Sacred Virtue shines with modesty, opening a thousand years of peace where earth and heaven are in communion. You gather humble greens without discarding them, and crown them with fine jade to add to their glory. Joining our hands in salutation as we reverently receive this, our faces flush with a sense of shame. We humbly reflect that poetry …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
御彝訓罔愆屬當改歲之期適應迎陽之候攄
淵衷而掞藻儼
寶翰之寵頒謂除舊布新象方懸於月令而塞
違昭德念彌切於時幾
睿語春敷特褒耆碩
虛懷夕惕俯望交脩近體聊取夫五言
旨超邃古
殊貺遙傳于一札重侈兼函敦厚溫柔括魯
頌無邪之義丁寧反覆邁衛武抑戒之詞
===
臣等幸際
昌辰叨司台鼎
彤廷曳珮未聞燮理之猷
黃閣演綸久乏論思之益曩自
平臺
召見揮翰分華逮于
講幄周旋賡詩翊學
楓宸垂眷勉報稱而弗前
藻錫頻蕃詎對揚之敢後恭依
punctuated:
御，彝訓罔愆。屬當改歲之期，適應迎陽之候。攄淵衷而掞藻，儼寶翰之寵頒。謂除舊布新，象方懸於《月令》；而塞違昭德，念彌切於時幾。睿語春敷，特褒耆碩；虛懷夕惕，俯望交脩。近體聊取夫五言，旨超邃古；殊貺遙傳于一札，重侈兼函。敦厚溫柔，括《魯頌》無邪之義；丁寧反覆，邁衛武《抑》戒之詞。
臣等幸際昌辰，叨司台鼎。彤廷曳珮，未聞燮理之猷；黃閣演綸，久乏論思之益。曩自平臺召見，揮翰分華；逮于講幄周旋，賡詩翊學。楓宸垂眷，勉報稱而弗前；藻錫頻蕃，詎對揚之敢後？恭依
translation_en:
… the throne, and the constant precepts have been free of transgression. Just at the time of the change of the year, fittingly corresponding to the season of welcoming the returning Yang energy, You have poured forth Your deep thoughts to unfold literary brilliance, and majestically the precious calligraphy has been graciously bestowed. You state that in sweeping away the old and spreading forth the new, the emblems are just now displayed in the Monthly Ordinances (Yueling), while in blocking transgressions and making bright the virtue, Your thoughts grow ever more earnest regarding the timelyincipient moments of action. Your imperial words spread like spring, specially praising the venerable and eminent elders; with an open mind and evening vigilance, You look down in hopes of mutual cultivation. Though the regulated verse casually adopts the five-syllable form, its import surpasses remote antiquity; the extraordinary gift is transmitted from afar in a single note, doubly lavish in a combined case. Sincere, generous, gentle, and mild, it encompasses the meaning of "having no depraved thoughts" in the Odes of Lu (Lusong); earnest and repeated in its injunctions, it surpasses the admonitory words of the "Yi" ode of Duke Wu of Wei.

Your servants have had the good fortune to encounter this prosperous age and unworthily hold charge of the highest ministerial posts. Trailing our girdle-pendants in the Vermilion Court, we have not been heard to offer plans for harmonizing the governance; drafting imperial decrees in the Yellow Pavilion, we have long lacked beneficial counsel in deliberation and reflection. Earlier, from the time we were summoned to an audience at the Flat Terrace (Pingtai), You wielded the brush to share its splendor; coming down to our attendance in the Lecture Tent, we composed matching poems to assist in Your learning. The Maple Hall has bestowed its favor, yet though we strive to repay it worthily, we fail to advance; the ornate gifts have been frequent and abundant—how could we dare to lag behind in responding to and extolling Your grace? Respectfully following …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
洪韻輒獻蕪言雖
大造帡幪一辭莫賛顧
仁風噓拂萬籟齊鳴亦步亦趨瞠乎絕塵之逾
遠斯陶斯咏慢然下里之懷慙豈謂
兼聽芻蕘遂爾聯編
簡袠仍裁首序
標著嘉名
讓虞周於不居氷淵是凜
奬忠良之同道華袞爭輝
===
親灑御題奚止借世南之筆
榮頒近輔無勞登常侍之牀繽紛焉鳳翥龍翔
光騰
黼扆髣髴乎金聲玉振調協宮商匪繡乎鼙帨
之工蓋責以鹽梅之助不圖迂朽有此遭
逢拭目聳瞻彩絢若迷於五色齋心誦法
典刑媲美於六經敢不矢竭寸衷率先百
職都兪吁咈永輸弼直之忱明聽翼為恪
效寅恭之誼
punctuated: 洪韻，輒獻蕪言。雖大造帡幪，一辭莫賛；顧仁風噓拂，萬籟齊鳴。亦步亦趨，瞠乎絕塵之逾遠；斯陶斯咏，慢然下里之懷慙。豈謂兼聽芻蕘，遂爾聯編簡袠，仍裁首序，標著嘉名。讓虞周於不居，氷淵是凜；奬忠良之同道，華袞爭輝。親灑御題，奚止借世南之筆；榮頒近輔，無勞登常侍之牀。繽紛焉鳳翥龍翔，光騰黼扆；髣髴乎金聲玉振，調協宮商。匪繡乎鼙帨之工，蓋責以鹽梅之助。不圖迂朽，有此遭逢。拭目聳瞻，彩絢若迷於五色；齋心誦法，典刑媲美於六經。敢不矢竭寸衷，率先百職；都兪吁咈，永輸弼直之忱；明聽翼為，恪效寅恭之誼。
translation_en: … Your Majesty's grand rhymes, I rashly offered up my crude words. Although the Great Creator shelters all like a canopy, not a single word of mine could add to its praise; yet when the benevolent wind breathes across the land, the myriad pipes sound forth together. Matching step for step and stride for stride, I stare helplessly behind as Your Majesty leaves the dust ever farther behind; delighted and chanting, I am abashed at the vulgarity of my rustic verses. How could I have expected that Your Majesty would deign to listen even to a grass-cutter and firewood-gatherer, and thereupon bind our verses together into a book-wrapper, while further composing a preface at the head and bestowing upon it an auspicious title? Yielding comparability with Yu [Shun] and the Zhou by declining their place, You remain ever cautious as if treading on thin ice or standing by an abyss; praising loyal and worthy ministers who share the Way, Your words vie in brilliance with ceremonial robes of honor. Personally splashing ink for the imperial inscription, how is this merely borrowing the brush of Yu Shinan (虞世南)?Gloriously bestowing it upon Your close grand counselors, there is no need to climb onto the couch of the Regular Attendant. In dazzling profusion, like phoenixes soaring and dragons wheeling, its radiance leaps up from the imperial screen; as if ringing with bronze and vibrating with jade, its melodies harmonize the gong and shang notes. This is not mere embroidery of ornate girdles and kerchiefs, for You charge us with the assistance of salt and plum in seasoning the state. I never imagined that one so pedantic and decayed as I would meet with such an encounter. Wiping my eyes to gaze aloft in awe, the brilliant colors seem to dazzle with the five hues; purifying my heart to recite and model myself upon it, its canons and patterns rival the beauty of the Six Classics. How dare I not swear to exhaust my humble heart and lead the hundred officials—in agreement and objection alike, forever offering up the sincerity of corrective assistance; in clear listening and翼-like [diligent] action, reverently fulfilling the duty of respectful collegiality—…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
上以疇答乎
知遇下求不負其平生伏願
左右惟人
始終典學
法天行健憂勤恒徹於夙宵
與物皆春惠保咸周於遐邇則頌聲交作萬
邦底
嘉靖之隆而儆戒無虞
五位衍靈長之慶臣等無任瞻
===
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叄場
策
第一問
方學龍
punctuated:
上以疇答乎知遇，下求不負其平生。伏願左右惟人，始終典學；法天行健，憂勤恒徹於夙宵；與物皆春，惠保咸周於遐邇。則頌聲交作，萬邦底嘉靖之隆；而儆戒無虞，五位衍靈長之慶。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至。謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叄場
策
第一問
方學龍
translation_en:
… above, to requite Your Majesty's recognition and favor, and below, to seek not to betray the aspirations of our whole lives. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will have only worthy men at Your side and remain devoted to learning from beginning to end; that You will model Yourself on Heaven's unceasing vigor, with anxious diligence pervading morning and night; and that You will share the vitality of spring with all things, extending benevolent protection universally to far and near. Then songs of praise will arise together, and the myriad states will attain the flourishing prosperity of the Jiajing era; admonishing Yourself against complacency, the imperial throne will prolong its auspicious and enduring blessings. Your servants are overwhelmed with boundless awe and earnest trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty. We reverently present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Fang Xuelong 方學龍

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
讀三朝寶訓如宋之孝宗者焉夫貞觀政
要神龍中吳兢所撰也謂唐之極治貞觀
爲最采時政可紀者上之於朝其爲篇目
以四十計蓋箴勸之義備焉傳至宣宗每
拱手斂容而讀之豈不念締造之艱哉顧
勵精未幾旋已怠荒魏謩以盡言罷相孰
與獎魏徵之直王宰緣貴倖求用孰與燭
宇文士及之姦迎軒轅集於羅浮孰與斥
蕭瑀崇釋之謬以故河湟雖復內地騷亭
===
矣唐之政衰矣三朝寶訓天聖中李淑所
撰也始於建隆迄於乾興凡綸音政典悉
著于篇裒而爲事者以百計蓋經緯之謨
具焉傳至孝宗每値進講輒咨詢弗倦豈
非儼羹墻之見哉顧徒飾口耳靡措躬行
外戚家毋得除兩府矣而張說用戚屬棣
樞內侍省毋得預政事矣而甘昇與曾覿
相表裏王昭素嘗以儒術召對便殿矣而
朱熹用道學見疎以故正邪雜進事權旁
punctuated: 讀《三朝寶訓》如宋之孝宗者焉。夫《貞觀政要》，神龍中吳兢所撰也。謂唐之極治，貞觀爲最，采時政可紀者上之於朝，其爲篇目以四十計，蓋箴勸之義備焉。傳至宣宗，每拱手斂容而讀之，豈不念締造之艱哉？顧勵精未幾，旋已怠荒：魏謩以盡言罷相，孰與獎魏徵之直？王宰緣貴倖求用，孰與燭宇文士及之姦？迎軒轅集於羅浮，孰與斥蕭瑀崇釋之謬？以故河湟雖復，內地騷亭矣，唐之政衰矣。《三朝寶訓》，天聖中李淑所撰也。始於建隆，迄於乾興，凡綸音政典，悉著于篇，裒而爲事者以百計，蓋經緯之謨具焉。傳至孝宗，每値進講，輒咨詢弗倦，豈非儼羹墻之見哉？顧徒飾口耳，靡措躬行：外戚家毋得除兩府矣，而張說用戚屬棣樞；內侍省毋得預政事矣，而甘昇與曾覿相表裏；王昭素嘗以儒術召對便殿矣，而朱熹用道學見疎。以故正邪雜進，事權旁
translation_en:
… reading the Precious Instructions of the Three Reigns (Sanchao baoxun) like Emperor Xiaozong of the Song. Now, the Essentials of Governance of the Zhenguan Era (Zhenguan zhengyao) was compiled by Wu Jing 吳兢 during the Shenlong era (705–707). Holding that the pinnacle of governance in the Tang dynasty was greatest during the Zhenguan era (627–649), he gathered contemporary governmental affairs worthy of record and presented them to the court; its chapter headings numbered forty, and the principles of admonition and encouragement were complete therein. Handed down to Emperor Xuanzong, whenever he read it with folded hands and a composed countenance, how could he not have been mindful of the hardships of founding the dynasty? Yet after striving for vigor for only a short while, he soon grew indolent and neglectful: Wei Mo 魏謩 was dismissed as Grand Councilor for speaking out fully—how does that compare with rewarding the forthrightness of Wei Zheng 魏徵? Wang Zai 王宰 sought employment through powerful favorites—how does that compare with discerning the treachery of Yuwen Shiji 宇文士及? Welcoming Xuanyuan Ji 軒轅集 from Mount Luofu—how does that compare with rebuking the fallacy of Xiao Yu 蕭瑀 in revering Buddhism? Consequently, although the He and Huang river regions were recovered, the interior was thrown into turmoil [?], and the governance of the Tang declined.

The Precious Instructions of the Three Reigns was compiled by Li Shu 李淑 during the Tiansheng era (1023–1032). Beginning with the Jianlong era (960–963) and extending to the Qianxing era (1022), all imperial pronouncements and governmental statutes were recorded in its chapters; collected into topical entries numbering in the hundreds, the grand counsels of statecraft were fully present therein. Handed down to Emperor Xiaozong, whenever it was time for the court lectures, he would inquire tirelessly—was this not just like seeing the ancestral models before him in his soup and on his wall? Yet he merely adorned his ears and mouth with it, without putting it into personal practice: consort clans were prohibited from being appointed to the Two Administrations, yet Zhang Yue 張說 was placed in the Bureau of Military Affairs [?] through his status as an imperial affine; the Palace Domestic Service was prohibited from interfering in affairs of state, yet Gan Sheng 甘昇 and Zeng Di 曾覿 colluded from within and without; Wang Zhaosu 王昭素 had once been summoned to an audience in a side palace on account of his Confucian learning, yet Zhu Xi 朱熹 was alienated on account of the Learning of the Way (Daoxue). Consequently, the upright and the wicked were advanced indiscriminately, and administrative authority slipped away…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
落乾道之業替巳大都人情始於銳常卒
於怠采其華常遺其實唐宋二君非真有
恭默思道陟降在庭之心也陽浮慕之耳
宜其假之而遽歸舉之而旋廢矣矧唐以
雜霸爲治而本原弗端宋以忠厚立國而
紀綱弗振卽所以詒謀者不逮商周遠甚
其後嗣又何以觀也洪惟我
祖
宗啓祚
===
列聖紹庥
駿德豐功奠安寓內若乾元之覆幬焉
神謨聖範昭示
後昆若日月之照臨焉
深仁厚澤永庇蒸黔若雨露之滋潤焉
瑤編玉冊之紀
金匱石室之藏非遐逖所能悉窺也而文獻
足徵儀刑如在巍然煥然真克邁三五之
登閎陋唐宋於下風者可歷舉而數矣我
punctuated: 落，乾道之業替巳。大都人情始於銳，常卒於怠；采其華，常遺其實。唐、宋二君，非真有恭默思道、陟降在庭之心也，陽浮慕之耳。宜其假之而遽歸，舉之而旋廢矣。矧唐以雜霸爲治而本原弗端，宋以忠厚立國而紀綱弗振，卽所以詒謀者不逮商、周遠甚，其後嗣又何以觀也？洪惟我祖宗啓祚，列聖紹庥。駿德豐功，奠安寓內，若乾元之覆幬焉；神謨聖範，昭示後昆，若日月之照臨焉；深仁厚澤，永庇蒸黔，若雨露之滋潤焉。瑤編玉冊之紀、金匱石室之藏，非遐逖所能悉窺也。而文獻足徵，儀刑如在，巍然煥然，真克邁三、五之登閎，陋唐、宋於下風者，可歷舉而數矣。我
translation_en:
… slipped away, and the enterprise of the Qiandao era declined. In general, human nature begins with keenness and usually ends in laxity; it plucks the blossoms and usually leaves behind the fruit. Those two rulers of the Tang and Song did not truly possess minds that reverently and silently pondered the Way or sensed the spirits ascending and descending in the court; they merely admired such things superficially and outwardly. It is no wonder that they borrowed them only to quickly abandon them, and raised them up only to soon discard them. Moreover, the Tang governed with an admixture of hegemonic rule so that its fundamental source was not upright, while the Song founded its state upon loyal generosity yet failed to invigorate its discipline and order. Even the counsels they bequeathed fell far short of the Shang and Zhou—what, then, could their descendants look to as a model?

I reflect with awe on how our Imperial Ancestors inaugurated the dynasty's fortune, and how the Successive Sages carried forward its blessings. Their grand virtue and abundant achievements have pacified all within the realm, like the overarching canopy of Primal Heaven; their divine counsels and sagely models illuminate posterity, like the shining down of the sun and moon; their deep benevolence and rich grace eternally shelter the common people, like the nourishing moisture of rain and dew. The records of jade codices and jade tablets, and the treasures stored in golden coffers and stone chambers, are beyond what those in distant quarters can fully peer into. Yet the documents and worthies provide sufficient verification, and their exemplary models remain as if present before us—lofty and resplendent, truly capable of surpassing the sublime heights of the Three Kings and Five Emperors and casting the Tang and Song down into an inferior position, as one may enumerate one by one. Our …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
皇上嗣曆握乾乃益闡揚而光大之崇奉
兩宮敦隆盛典至孝也
日御講幄
躬裁庶政至明也
軫念民瘼
屢詔蠲恤至仁也一時大小臣工罔不濯磨振
奮求無負於
昌期即山海遐陬亦喁喁歌頌矣頃歲
俞輔臣之請以
===
累朝
訓錄分類編摩
便殿講讀之餘時復
進講曰法祖曰創業艱難其大指也曰敬天
曰保民曰勤學曰勵精圖治其急務也曰
謹祭祀曰愼起居以至於正紀綱御夷狄
絲分縷析其條目也簡袠雖繁而指要則
約事類雖夥而條貫可陳
祖
punctuated: 皇上嗣曆握乾，乃益闡揚而光大之。崇奉兩宮，敦隆盛典，至孝也；日御講幄，躬裁庶政，至明也；軫念民瘼，屢詔蠲恤，至仁也。一時大小臣工，罔不濯磨振奮，求無負於昌期；即山海遐陬，亦喁喁歌頌矣。頃歲俞輔臣之請，以累朝訓錄分類編摩，便殿講讀之餘，時復進講。曰「法祖」、曰「創業艱難」，其大指也；曰「敬天」、曰「保民」、曰「勤學」、曰「勵精圖治」，其急務也；曰「謹祭祀」、曰「愼起居」，以至於「正紀綱」、「御夷狄」，絲分縷析，其條目也。簡袠雖繁而指要則約，事類雖夥而條貫可陳，祖
translation_en:
… Sovereign succeeded to the dynastic calendar and grasped the power of Heaven, further expounding and magnifying these legacies. Reverently serving the Two Palaces [the Empresses Dowager] and generously exalting the grand ceremonies—this is supreme filial piety. Daily attending the lecture tent and personally deciding the myriad affairs of state—this is supreme intelligence. Feeling deep sympathy for the distress of the people and repeatedly issuing edicts to grant tax remissions and relief—this is supreme benevolence. At this time, officials great and small without exception polish their conduct and rouse themselves, seeking not to fail this prosperous era; even in distant corners among the mountains and seas, the people look up eagerly and sing praises.

In recent years, His Majesty approved the request of the Grand Secretaries to classify, compile, and study the Ancestral Injunctions and Veritable Records of successive reigns, and outside of the regular lectures and readings in the informal halls, to have them presented and expounded from time to time. "Emulating the Ancestors" and "The Hardships of Founding the Dynasty" are their overarching themes; "Revering Heaven," "Protecting the People," "Diligence in Learning," and "Rousing Vigor to Seek Good Governance" are their urgent tasks; "Carefulness in Sacrifices" and "Prudence in Daily Conduct," all the way to "Rectifying the Laws and Discipline" and "Controlling the Four Barbarians," analyzed down to the finest thread, are their detailed headings. Though the volumes are numerous, their essential meaning is concise; though the categories of affairs are multitudinous, their systematic thread can be set forth. The Ancestors'…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宗之彝訓具是矣猗與休哉與治同道罔不興
其斯之謂乎乃執事猶欲掇要探本圖所
爲芹曝獻者則何以稱焉仰聞我
太祖諭侍臣曰皇天無親惟德是輔使吾後世
子孫皆如成康輔弼之臣皆如周召則可
以祈天永命國祚愈昌我
成祖之訓曰人常慮危迺不蹈危車行於峻坂
而仆於平地者慎於難而忽於易也保天
下亦如御車何可不慎大哉
===
皇言勒法琬琰
列聖之所以繼序不忘者率是道也愚竊觀輔
臣之所獻規
皇上之所延納如曰審官曰理財曰興教化曰
飭武備諸事則宰臣總其綱六卿分其職
臺諫繩其愆
穆清之上第一加意受成焉即以咸熈庶績
永保丕平易易也顧惟
堂陛森嚴則下情靡達
punctuated: 宗之彝訓具是矣。猗與休哉！「與治同道，罔不興」，其斯之謂乎！乃執事猶欲掇要探本，圖所爲芹曝獻者，則何以稱焉？仰聞我太祖諭侍臣曰：「皇天無親，惟德是輔。使吾後世子孫皆如成、康，輔弼之臣皆如周、召，則可以祈天永命，國祚愈昌。」我成祖之訓曰：「人常慮危，迺不蹈危。車行於峻坂而仆於平地者，慎於難而忽於易也。保天下亦如御車，何可不慎！」大哉皇言，勒法琬琰，列聖之所以繼序不忘者，率是道也。愚竊觀輔臣之所獻規、皇上之所延納，如曰審官、曰理財、曰興教化、曰飭武備諸事，則宰臣總其綱，六卿分其職，臺諫繩其愆，穆清之上，第一加意受成焉，即以咸熈庶績、永保丕平，易易也。顧惟堂陛森嚴，則下情靡達；
translation_en:
…The constant instructions of the Imperial Ancestors are all contained herein. Oh, how admirable! "Walking the same path as those who brought order, none failed to flourish"—surely this is what is meant! Yet Your Reverence still wishes to gather the essentials and probe the fundamentals, seeking a humble offering to present to the throne; how then can I match your expectations?

I have respectfully heard that our Grand Progenitor (Taizu) instructed his attending ministers, saying: "August Heaven has no favorites; it aids only virtue. If the sons and grandsons of my later generations are all like Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou, and their assisting ministers are all like the Dukes of Zhou and Shao, then we may pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate, and the dynasty's fortune will grow ever more prosperous." And the instruction of our Accomplished Progenitor (Chengzu) states: "When a person constantly contemplates danger, he does not tread into danger. That a carriage travels safely over a steep slope yet overturns on level ground is because one is cautious in difficulty and careless in ease. Preserving the realm is also like driving a carriage—how could one not be cautious!" Great indeed are these imperial words, inscribed as laws upon fine jade! That whereby the successive sage emperors have carried on the line without forgetting is by following this very Way.

In my humble observation of the remonstrances presented by the Grand Secretaries and received by His Majesty—concerning such matters as examining officials, managing finances, promoting moral transformation, and readying military defenses—the chief ministers oversee the general principles, the Six Ministers divide the specific duties, and the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau correct any faults. Above, in serene and lofty majesty, the Emperor need only pay heed and accept the completed work; thus, to make all achievements shine forth and forever preserve great peace is most easy indeed. Yet, when the court and the throne are sternly set apart, the conditions of those below cannot reach above; …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宮府懸隔則匡拂末繇是在
密勿之中預圖而默省之耳愚請得正言無
諱可乎夫人主一心攻以衆欲一念之好
尚羣情所共趨也喜珍玩卽淫巧者售喜
異端卽詭誕者售猶設侯張的衆盻咸集
鮮弗中矣故監胡元之覆轍則碎水晶宮
漏懲梁宋之迷途則闢釋老異敎是
祖
宗端好尚之家法所當念也自昔高宗之遜志
===
時敏成王之緝煕光明罔非以務學爲急
者學猶植也不以有人而作無人而輟也
一暴十寒其如有萌焉何哉故
御書洪範篇雖
宮中不釋手
命儒臣進講大學衍義雖盛暑不輟業是
祖
宗勤學之家法所當念也天子以天下奉一人
錦衣玉食匪乏供也而曰克儉于家曰愼
punctuated: 宮府懸隔，則匡拂末繇，是在密勿之中，預圖而默省之耳。愚請得正言無諱，可乎？夫人主一心，攻以衆欲，一念之好尚，羣情所共趨也。喜珍玩，卽淫巧者售；喜異端，卽詭誕者售。猶設侯張的，衆盻咸集，鮮弗中矣。故監胡元之覆轍，則碎水晶宮漏；懲梁、宋之迷途，則闢釋、老異敎。是祖宗端好尚之家法所當念也。自昔高宗之遜志時敏，成王之緝煕光明，罔非以務學爲急者。學猶植也，不以有人而作，無人而輟也。一暴十寒，其如有萌焉何哉？故御書《洪範篇》，雖宮中不釋手；命儒臣進講《大學衍義》，雖盛暑不輟業。是祖宗勤學之家法所當念也。天子以天下奉一人，錦衣玉食，匪乏供也。而曰「克儉于家」，曰「愼…
translation_en:
… and when the inner palace and outer court are separated by a wide gulf, there is no way to offer corrective remonstrance; this lies solely in planning beforehand and reflecting silently within the secluded chambers of the palace. May I, in my simplicity, beg leave to speak frankly and without taboo?

Now, the single mind of the ruler is assailed by a multitude of desires, and the predilection of a single thought is that toward which the sentiments of all men rush together. If he delights in rare curiosities, then purveyors of extravagant contrivances find a market; if he delights in heterodoxies, then purveyors of deceit and absurdity find a market. It is just like setting up an archery target and stretching its bull's-eye: the gazes of the multitude all converge upon it, and few fail to hit the mark. Therefore, taking warning from the overturned chariot of the barbarian Yuan, [our Imperial Ancestor] smashed the crystal palace clepsydra; rebuking the lost paths of the Liang and Song, he refuted the heterodox teachings of Buddhism and Daoism. This is the ancestral family law of rectifying predilections, which ought to be borne in mind.

From of old, the humble will and timely diligence of Gaozong [of Shang], and the continuous bright illumination of King Cheng [of Zhou], were in no case anything other than taking devotion to learning as an urgent priority. Learning is like cultivating plants: one does not work at it because someone is watching and cease when no one is there. If there is one day of sunning followed by ten days of freezing, what good will it do even if sprouts appear? Therefore, [our Imperial Ancestor] copied out the "Great Plan" (Hongfan) chapter in his own imperial hand and did not put it down even within the palace; and he commanded Confucian officials to present lectures on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), not suspending his studies even in the height of summer heat. This is the ancestral family law of diligence in learning, which ought to be borne in mind.

The Son of Heaven is served as the One Man by the entire realm; brocade robes and jade delicacies are not lacking in supply. Yet it was said, "able to be frugal in his household," and it was said, "beautifying… [or: be mindful of…]

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乃儉德誠慮夫膏脂易竭意欲難窮作法
於奢將無以維其後矣故惜費效於漢文
則隙地無亭臺之築惡服法於大禹則
後宫有浣濯之衣是
祖
宗敦節儉之家法所當念也伯冏之命曰侍御
僕從罔非正人而無昵憸人之戒尤諄諄
焉彼儇巧之姿日侍左右憑社則玩紀煬
竈則蔽明自匪剛明果斷之主鮮不昵而
===
蕩矣故私請內庾以充奇富則導諛之詰
責必嚴議省大官議覈營卒則掖廷之浮
言罔奪是
祖
宗馭近習之家法所當念也不特此也思
存省之錄則警戒日勤玩
敬一之箴則起居必愼自
深宫燕閒以及
大廷臨御凜若
punctuated: 乃儉德，誠慮夫膏脂易竭、意欲難窮，作法於奢，將無以維其後矣。故惜費效於漢文，則隙地無亭臺之築；惡服法於大禹，則後宫有浣濯之衣。是祖宗敦節儉之家法，所當念也。《伯冏之命》曰：「侍御僕從，罔非正人。」而「無昵憸人」之戒，尤諄諄焉。彼儇巧之姿，日侍左右，憑社則玩紀，煬竈則蔽明，自匪剛明果斷之主，鮮不昵而蕩矣。故私請內庾以充奇富，則導諛之詰責必嚴；議省大官、議覈營卒，則掖廷之浮言罔奪。是祖宗馭近習之家法，所當念也。不特此也，思《存省》之錄，則警戒日勤；玩《敬一》之箴，則起居必愼。自深宫燕閒以及大廷臨御，凜若
translation_en:
… "be mindful of the virtue of frugality"—is truly out of concern that the lifeblood of the people is easily exhausted while human desires are hard to satisfy; if one sets an example of extravagance, there will be no way to sustain what follows. Thus, in emulating Emperor Wen of Han by grudging expenditures, no pavilions or terraces were built on vacant grounds; in taking Great Yu as a model by wearing coarse clothing, washed and re-worn garments were found in the rear palace. This is the family law of the Imperial Ancestors in emphasizing frugality, which ought to be borne in mind.

The "Charge to Bo Jiong" (Bo Jiong zhi ming) says: "Let your attendants and servants all be upright men," and its warning "not to be intimate with artful flatterers" is especially earnest. Those of nimble and cunning disposition attend at the ruler's side day after day; relying on the altar like rats, they trifle with discipline, and standing before the stove, they block the ruler's clarity of vision. Unless one is a firm, discerning, and decisive sovereign, few fail to grow intimate with them and be led into dissipation. Thus, when someone privately requested grain from the inner granaries to amass extraordinary wealth, the reprimand against inducing flattery was unfailingly stern; when proposals were made to curtail the provisions of the Grand Provisioner or to verify the rosters of camp soldiers, baseless talk from the inner palace could not sway the decision. This is the family law of the Imperial Ancestors in controlling close attendants, which ought to be borne in mind.

Not only this: reflecting upon the Record of Self-Examination (Cunxing zhi lu), one grows daily more diligent in vigilance; pondering the Admonition on Reverence and Unity (Jingyi zhi zhen), one is unfailingly cautious in daily conduct. From moments of leisure in the deep palace to holding court in the great hall, be as awed as if…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
列聖之陟降于前焉匪弟諷咏遺編聳動觀聽
而已由是則正人日親而奇袤慆淫之徒
遠矣忠言日進而豫大豐亨之說黜矣庶
職競勸方內禔福而明作惇大之業成矣
蓋天下國家之本在
君身而其機在宥密雖拂士無緣畢其議邇臣
不得闚其忠者惟
明主一獨覺耳獨覺則明通明通則公溥夫是
以恭己南面而宇內太和也故曰王道本
===
于誠意其要只在謹獨執事所謂保泰之
助意在斯乎
第二問
同考試官訓導張 批 辨析古今人物情態殆盡祝以忠
而文思縱橫不竭敬服敬服
同考試官教諭區 批 浩博之學璀璨之詞末歸
重人才樂為吾用尤反覆有情佳士也
考試官教諭程 批 品藻中有確論非經生語
punctuated:
列聖之陟降于前焉，匪弟諷咏遺編、聳動觀聽而已。由是則正人日親，而奇袤慆淫之徒遠矣；忠言日進，而豫大豐亨之說黜矣；庶職競勸，方內禔福，而明作惇大之業成矣。蓋天下國家之本在君身，而其機在宥密。雖拂士無緣畢其議、邇臣不得闚其忠者，惟明主一獨覺耳。獨覺則明通，明通則公溥，夫是以恭己南面而宇內太和也。故曰王道本于誠意，其要只在謹獨。執事所謂保泰之助，意在斯乎！

第二問
同考試官訓導張批：辨析古今人物情態殆盡〔祝以忠〕，而文思縱橫不竭，敬服敬服。
同考試官教諭區批：浩博之學，璀璨之詞，末歸重人才樂為吾用，尤反覆有情，佳士也。
考試官教諭程批：品藻中有確論，非經生語。
translation_en:
… as if the succession of Imperial Ancestors were ascending and descending right before Him—not merely chanting their bequeathed texts to stir the sight and hearing of others. From this, upright men will be drawn closer day by day, while perverse, insolent, and licentious fellows will be kept at a distance; loyal counsel will be presented day by day, while talk of extravagant ease and lavish abundance will be dismissed; the hundred officials will vie in diligence, the realm within will enjoy peace and blessing, and the enterprise of enlightened vigor and generous greatness will be accomplished. For the root of the empire and the state lies in the Sovereign's own person, and its pivotal spring lies in the quiet depth of His mind. Even where remonstrating worthies have no way to exhaust their counsel and close ministers cannot peer in to offer their loyalty, everything depends solely on the enlightened Ruler's solitary self-awareness. When He is solitarily aware, He is clear and penetrating; when He is clear and penetrating, He is impartial and all-embracing; and thus He holds Himself in reverent composure facing south while the whole world enjoys supreme harmony. Therefore it is said that the Kingly Way is rooted in making the intentions sincere, and its essential point lies simply in being watchful over oneself when alone. What Your Excellency calls an aid to preserving great peace—does its meaning not lie right here?

Second Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang: He analyzes the dispositions and circumstances of figures ancient and modern almost exhaustively [Zhu Yizhong 祝以忠], and his literary thoughts range freely and inexhaustibly. Truly admirable, truly admirable!
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Ou: Vast and渊博 learning, brilliant diction; at the end he places the emphasis on men of talent gladly serving our use, turning the point over with particular feeling. A fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Instructor Cheng: Within his appraisals of character there are sound and definitive judgments; these are not the words of a mere examination-hall classicist.

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嚅烏覩所謂名實之指卽使言犂然當明
問亦塵飯塗羹耳執事將無以鄙生爲戲
耶久矣夫名實之難辨也假令名之與實
若左劵之相符則一庸人能辨之又奚俟
於英辟顧抱實者鮮矜名者多車軔與月
旦齊呼腊鼠與璞玉並號荻苗類菉薏苡
似菊虎皮而羊質鳳彩而鵲聲其情貌懸
也且飾名者進則尚實者抑朝有儇巧輕
躁之夫則野有敦朴恬靜之士朝有容悅
===
便佞之黨則野有剛正伉直之人朝有暴
戾貪黷之臣則野有寬大謹廉之輩其負
勝定也皐陶之告舜曰知人則哲能官人
惟帝其難之子產有言人心不同有如其
面蓋自古記之矣請略陳疇昔之槩以復
明問而徐效一得之愚可乎材品不同信
不可以一端盡也何謂名實之相副者伊
尹有莘之農夫也方其秉耒而耕固已希
心堯舜及三聘而出遂建革夏之勳而商
punctuated:
嚅，烏覩所謂名實之指？卽使言犂然當明問，亦塵飯塗羹耳，執事將無以鄙生爲戲耶？久矣夫，名實之難辨也！假令名之與實，若左劵之相符，則一庸人能辨之，又奚俟於英辟？顧抱實者鮮，矜名者多。車軔與月旦齊呼，腊鼠與璞玉並號；荻苗類菉，薏苡似菊；虎皮而羊質，鳳彩而鵲聲，其情貌懸也。且飾名者進，則尚實者抑：朝有儇巧輕躁之夫，則野有敦朴恬靜之士；朝有容悅便佞之黨，則野有剛正伉直之人；朝有暴戾貪黷之臣，則野有寬大謹廉之輩，其負勝定也。皐陶之告舜曰：「知人則哲，能官人，惟帝其難之。」子產有言：「人心不同，有如其面。」蓋自古記之矣。請略陳疇昔之槩，以復明問，而徐效一得之愚，可乎？
材品不同，信不可以一端盡也。何謂名實之相副者？伊尹，有莘之農夫也。方其秉耒而耕，固已希心堯、舜；及三聘而出，遂建革夏之勳，而商…
translation_en:
…mumbling, how could I perceive the purport of what is called reputation and reality? Even if my words were to clearly hit the mark of your discerning question, they would be no more than rice of dust and soup of mud—would Your Excellency not take this humble student to be making sport? Long indeed has it been difficult to distinguish between reputation and reality! Suppose reputation and reality tallied with each other like the left half of a contract, then even an ordinary person could distinguish them; what need would there be to wait upon an enlightened sovereign? Yet those who embrace reality are few, while those who boast of reputation are many. A wheel-chock is acclaimed on a par with a Monthly Critique (yuedan) [?], and a dried rat is called by the same name as uncarved jade; reed shoots resemble green bamboo, and job's-tears look like chrysanthemums; with a tiger's skin over a sheep's substance, or a phoenix's plumage with a magpie's voice, their inner nature and outer appearance are poles apart. Moreover, when those who embellish their reputation advance, those who esteem reality are suppressed: when the court has nimble, artful, frivolous, and rash fellows, the countryside has honest, simple, calm, and quiet scholars; when the court has cliques of accommodating, pleasing, andglib flatterers, the countryside has upright, firm, and straightforward men; when the court has cruel, violent, greedy, and corrupt ministers, the countryside has magnanimous, cautious, and incorruptible sorts—the outcome of who loses and who prevails is thus fixed. When Gao Yao 皐陶 counselled Shun 舜, he said: "To know men is wisdom, to be able to nominate men for office—even the Sovereign finds this difficult." Zichan 子產 had a saying: "Men's minds are different, just as are their faces." Indeed, this has been recorded since antiquity. May I ask leave to briefly set forth a general outline of the past in reply to your discerning question, and then slowly offer my humble, single-minded thoughts?

Talents and character vary, and truly cannot be exhausted from a single angle. What is meant by reputation and reality corresponding to each other? Yi Yin 伊尹 was a farmer of Youshen 有莘. While he held the plow and tilled the soil, he had already set his heart on emulating Yao 堯 and Shun; when he emerged after being thrice invited with gifts, he thereupon established the merit of overthrowing the Xia 夏, and the Shang 商…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
道以隆諸葛亮南陽之隱士也方其抱膝
而吟因巳托志管樂及三顧而起遂樹鼎
足之烈而炎祚再昌此所謂名實之相副
者也何謂有其實而無其名者毛遂自賛
於平原門下皆笑之脫穎而結強楚之援
邯鄲之圍立解韓信寄食於漂母少年且
侮之登壇而畫蹙項之計垓下之師竟殲
此所謂有其實而無其名者也何謂有其
名而無其實者馬謖之在蜀甞奏記孔明
===
曰攻城爲下攻心爲上兵戰爲下心戰爲
上論非不偉也街亭一敗而首領不保殷
浩之在晉謝尚諸人相謂曰淵源不起當
如蒼生何以其出處卜江左興亡望非不
隆也壽陽一挫而身名俱損此所謂有其
名而無其實者也何謂蚤負不美之名而
晚令者王湛名爲癡不爲從子王濟所禮
一日濟與論易多出濟意表復就蟻封盤
馬湛回策如縈而濟馬踣濟乃歎曰家有
punctuated: 道以隆；諸葛亮，南陽之隱士也，方其抱膝而吟，因巳托志管、樂，及三顧而起，遂樹鼎足之烈，而炎祚再昌。此所謂名實之相副者也。何謂有其實而無其名者？毛遂自賛於平原，門下皆笑之，脫穎而結強楚之援，邯鄲之圍立解；韓信寄食於漂母，少年且侮之，登壇而畫蹙項之計，垓下之師竟殲。此所謂有其實而無其名者也。何謂有其名而無其實者？馬謖之在蜀，甞奏記孔明曰：「攻城爲下，攻心爲上，兵戰爲下，心戰爲上。」論非不偉也，街亭一敗，而首領不保；殷浩之在晉，謝尚諸人相謂曰：「淵源不起，當如蒼生何？」以其出處卜江左興亡，望非不隆也，壽陽一挫，而身名俱損。此所謂有其名而無其實者也。何謂蚤負不美之名而晚令者？王湛名爲癡，不爲從子王濟所禮，一日濟與論《易》，多出濟意表，復就蟻封盤馬，湛回策如縈，而濟馬踣，濟乃歎曰：「家有
translation_en:
… the Way of Shang thereby flourished; Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮 was a recluse of Nanyang 南陽, and while he sat clasping his knees and chanting verses, he had already set his ambitions on Guan Zhong 管仲 and Yue Yi 樂毅; when after three visits he rose to take office, he achieved the feat of the tripartite division of the realm, and the fiery fortune of Han prospered once again. This is what is meant by reputation and reality corresponding to one another.

What is meant by possessing the reality without the reputation? When Mao Sui 毛遂 recommended himself to the Lord of Pingyuan 平原, all the retainers laughed at him; yet once the point of the awl emerged from the bag and he secured an alliance with powerful Chu 楚, the siege of Handan 邯鄲 was immediately lifted. When Han Xin 韓信 lived off the charity of a bleaching-woman, even a young ruffian insulted him; yet once he ascended the altar and mapped out the strategy to corner Xiang Yu 項羽, the army at Gaixia 垓下 was utterly annihilated. This is what is meant by possessing the reality without the reputation.

What is meant by possessing the reputation without the reality? When Ma Su 馬謖 was in Shu 蜀, he once submitted a memorandum to Kongming 孔明 [Zhuge Liang] saying, "Attacking cities is inferior, attacking hearts is superior; warfare with weapons is inferior, warfare with hearts is superior." His argument was by no means unimpressive, yet with a single defeat at Jieting 街亭, he could not preserve his own head. When Yin Hao 殷浩 was in Jin 晉, Xie Shang 謝尚 and others said to one another, "If Yuanyuan 淵源 [Yin Hao] does not rise to take office, what will become of the common people?" They divined the rise and fall of the realm east of the Yangtze by whether he came forth or remained in retirement—his prestige was by no means unexalted, yet with a single setback at Shouyang 壽陽, both his person and his reputation were ruined. This is what is meant by possessing the reputation without the reality.

What is meant by bearing an unfavorable reputation early on yet proving admirable later in life? Wang Zhan 王湛 had a reputation for being foolish and was not treated with respect by his nephew Wang Ji 王濟. One day Ji discussed the Book of Changes (Yi 易) with him, and much of what Zhan said went beyond Ji's expectations; when they further wheeled their horses around an ant-mound, Zhan plied his whip as smoothly as a winding cord while Ji's horse stumbled, whereupon Ji sighed and said, "In our family there has been…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
名士三十年而不知魏舒名爲鈍不爲其
叔魏衡所知後爲鍾毓長史毓毎集僚佐
射舒爲點籌偶朋人不足以舒滿數舒發
無不中毓乃謝曰吾之不足以盡卿有如
此射此所謂蚤負不美之名而晚令者也
何謂始被貪濁之名而終著高操者王述
爲宛陵令頗營家具王導以書戒之後乃
改厲所至以清德聞蕭恪爲雍州刺史頗
有賄聲梁武以人間歌謠示之後乃折節
===
所歷以善政稱此所謂始被貪濁之名而
終著高操者也何謂初陷兇惡之名而後
復改行者周處委身盜賊納父老之諫而
自新迄成名士賈淑侵暴邑里感郭泰之
言而自改竟爲善人此所謂初陷兇惡之
名而後復改行者也何謂陽附君子之名
而陰實爲小人者豎刁之事桓公也附於
忠豎牛之蠱叔孫也附於孝郅都寧成之
治郡也附於守職張湯王溫舒之鞫獄也
punctuated: 名士，三十年而不知。」魏舒名爲鈍，不爲其叔魏衡所知。後爲鍾毓長史，毓毎集僚佐射，舒爲點籌。偶朋人不足，以舒滿數，舒發無不中。毓乃謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿，有如此射。」此所謂蚤負不美之名而晚令者也。何謂始被貪濁之名而終著高操者？王述爲宛陵令，頗營家具，王導以書戒之，後乃改厲，所至以清德聞。蕭恪爲雍州刺史，頗有賄聲，梁武以人間歌謠示之，後乃折節，所歷以善政稱。此所謂始被貪濁之名而終著高操者也。何謂初陷兇惡之名而後復改行者？周處委身盜賊，納父老之諫而自新，迄成名士。賈淑侵暴邑里，感郭泰之言而自改，竟爲善人。此所謂初陷兇惡之名而後復改行者也。何謂陽附君子之名而陰實爲小人者？豎刁之事桓公也，附於忠；豎牛之蠱叔孫也，附於孝；郅都、寧成之治郡也，附於守職；張湯、王溫舒之鞫獄也，
translation_en:
… a celebrated gentleman, and for thirty years I did not know it!” Wei Shu 魏舒 had a reputation for being dull-witted and was not appreciated by his uncle Wei Heng 魏衡. Later, when he served as Aide (zhangshi 長史) to Zhong Yu 鍾毓, whenever Zhong Yu gathered his subordinates for archery, Shu acted as the scorekeeper. Once, when there were not enough participants to form the pairs, Shu was used to fill the quota, and every arrow he shot hit the mark. Zhong Yu then apologized, saying, “My failure to fully gauge your talents is just like this archery match!” These are what are called those who early on bore an unflattering reputation yet achieved a fine name late in life.

What is meant by those who initially suffered a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately displayed lofty integrity? When Wang Shu 王述 served as District Magistrate (ling 令) of Wanling 宛陵, he acquired rather a lot of household furnishings. After Wang Dao 王導 admonished him by letter, he mended his ways and steeled himself, becoming known for pure virtue wherever he went. When Xiao Ke 蕭恪 served as Regional Inspector (cishi 刺史) of Yongzhou 雍州, he had quite a reputation for taking bribes. After Emperor Wu of Liang 梁武 showed him the popular ballads circulating among the people, he humbled himself and changed his conduct, becoming praised for good governance in every post he held. These are what are called those who initially suffered a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately displayed lofty integrity.

What is meant by those who at first fell into a reputation for fierceness and wickedness yet later reformed their conduct? Zhou Chu 周處 gave himself over to banditry, but upon accepting the remonstrances of the local elders, he renewed himself and ultimately became a celebrated gentleman. Jia Shu 賈淑 bullied and terrorized his local community, but moved by the words of Guo Tai 郭泰, he reformed himself and finally became a good man. These are what are called those who at first fell into a reputation for fierceness and wickedness yet later reformed their conduct.

What is meant by those who outwardly attached themselves to the reputation of a gentleman while secretly being petty men in reality? In serving Duke Huan 桓公, the attendant Diao 豎刁 attached himself to loyalty; in bewitching Shusun 叔孫, the attendant Niu 豎牛 attached himself to filial piety; in governing their commanderies, Zhi Du 郅都 and Ning Cheng 寧成 attached themselves to the dutiful observance of office; in trying criminal cases, Zhang Tang 張湯 and Wang Wenshu 王溫舒…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
附於執法鄧通之柔媚公孫弘之反覆也
附於恭順此所謂陽附君子之名而陰實
爲小人者也何謂外近小人之名而中實
爲君子者子貢之存魯也近於詐弦高之
却秦也近於誕子囊之全楚也近於畏敵
李牧之防邊也近於縱寇蕭何之請苑也
近於賈譽田叔之焚獄書也近於鬻法狄
仁傑之徘徊女后也近於貪位此所謂外
近小人之名而中實爲君子者也夫名實
===
之相副者人主每憚其名而不樂近之有
其實而無其名者人主每略其實而遺之
有其名而無其實者人主每慕其名而悅
之有蚤蒙不美之名而晚令者人主每因
其蚤而棄之有始被貪濁之名而終著高
操者人主每追其始而斥之有初陷兇惡
之名而後更改行者人主每計其初而絕
之有陽附君子之名者人主不察其陰而
日親之有外近小人之名者人主不探其
punctuated: 附於執法；鄧通之柔媚、公孫弘之反覆也，附於恭順。此所謂陽附君子之名，而陰實爲小人者也。何謂外近小人之名，而中實爲君子者？子貢之存魯也，近於詐；弦高之却秦也，近於誕；子囊之全楚也，近於畏敵；李牧之防邊也，近於縱寇；蕭何之請苑也，近於賈譽；田叔之焚獄書也，近於鬻法；狄仁傑之徘徊女后也，近於貪位。此所謂外近小人之名，而中實爲君子者也。夫名實之相副者，人主每憚其名而不樂近之；有其實而無其名者，人主每略其實而遺之；有其名而無其實者，人主每慕其名而悅之；有蚤蒙不美之名而晚令者，人主每因其蚤而棄之；有始被貪濁之名而終著高操者，人主每追其始而斥之；有初陷兇惡之名而後更改行者，人主每計其初而絕之；有陽附君子之名者，人主不察其陰而日親之；有外近小人之名者，人主不探其
translation_en: … draped itself in the strict enforcement of the law; the soft flattery of Deng Tong 鄧通 and the duplicity of Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 draped themselves in respectful compliance. These are what are called outwardly attaching oneself to the reputation of a superior man while secretly being a petty man in reality. What are those who outwardly come close to the reputation of a petty man, yet inwardly are truly superior men? Zigong 子貢 preserving the state of Lu came close to deceit; Xian Gao 弦高 repelling the forces of Qin came close to fabrication; Zinang 子囊 keeping the state of Chu intact came close to fearing the enemy; Li Mu 李牧 defending the frontier came close to indulging raiders; Xiao He 蕭何 requesting the imperial parklands for the people came close to buying popular praise; Tian Shu 田叔 burning the prison dossiers came close to subverting the law; Di Renjie 狄仁傑 lingering at the court of a female ruler came close to coveting office. These are what are called outwardly coming close to the reputation of a petty man while inwardly being a superior man in reality. Now, as for those whose reputation and reality correspond, the ruler often dreads their reputation and takes no pleasure in drawing near to them; as for those who possess the reality without the reputation, the ruler often overlooks their reality and passes them by; as for those who possess the reputation without the reality, the ruler often admires their reputation and delights in them; as for those who early on suffered an unsavory reputation yet proved admirable in later life, the ruler often discards them on account of their early years; as for those who initially bore a reputation for greed and corruption yet ultimately displayed lofty integrity, the ruler often holds their beginnings against them and rejects them; as for those who at first fell into a reputation for viciousness and evil yet later reformed their conduct, the ruler often reckons by their initial deeds and cuts them off; as for those who outwardly attach themselves to the reputation of a superior man, the ruler fails to examine what they are in secret and grows closer to them by the day; as for those who outwardly come close to the reputation of a petty man, the ruler fails to probe what is within them…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
中而日疎之如此則所用非所材所材非
所用賢否倒置而真似淆亂矣自非人主
神識中涵獨見獨明幾何不徇名而失實
耶何謂獨見見在外者也日月之光也而
浮雲翳之則雲之外有遺燭矣燈火之燄
也而薄帷鄣之則帷之外有遺照矣何謂
獨明明在中者也鑑至空也而形不可欺
以妍媸焉衡至平也而物不可欺以輕重
焉屏嗜慾慎起居則內境清而人主之獨
===
明著矣遠佞倖納諫諍則外蔽撤而人主
之獨見昭矣由是出其獨見獨明以辨天
下之材則名實之相副者必庸而鼎鉉之
佐皆伊葛矣有其實而無其名者必採而
專對仗鉞之臣皆毛韓矣有其名而無其
實者必遠而虛談如馬謖殷浩者不至僨
事矣蚤蒙不美而晚令者必收而隱德如
王湛魏舒者不以蚤而棄矣始被貪濁而
終著高操者必錄而遷善如王述蕭恪者
punctuated: 中，而日疎之。如此，則所用非所材，所材非所用，賢否倒置，而真似淆亂矣。自非人主神識中涵，獨見獨明，幾何不徇名而失實耶？何謂獨見？見在外者也。日月之光也，而浮雲翳之，則雲之外有遺燭矣；燈火之燄也，而薄帷鄣之，則帷之外有遺照矣。何謂獨明？明在中者也。鑑至空也，而形不可欺以妍媸焉；衡至平也，而物不可欺以輕重焉。屏嗜慾，慎起居，則內境清而人主之獨明著矣；遠佞倖，納諫諍，則外蔽撤而人主之獨見昭矣。由是出其獨見獨明，以辨天下之材：則名實之相副者必庸，而鼎鉉之佐皆伊、葛矣；有其實而無其名者必採，而專對仗鉞之臣皆毛、韓矣；有其名而無其實者必遠，而虛談如馬謖、殷浩者不至僨事矣；蚤蒙不美而晚令者必收，而隱德如王湛、魏舒者不以蚤而棄矣；始被貪濁而終著高操者必錄，而遷善如王述、蕭恪者
translation_en: … inner disposition, and distances himself from them day by day. If this is so, then those who are employed are not the truly talented, and those who are truly talented are not employed; the worthy and the unworthy are inverted, and the genuine and the specious are confounded. Unless the ruler harbors a divine discernment within, possessing independent vision and independent clarity, how rarely will he avoid pursuing reputation and losing sight of reality! What is meant by "independent vision"? It is vision directed toward the outside. Take the light of the sun and moon: if floating clouds obscure it, there will be places beyond the clouds left unlit. Take the flame of a lamp: if a thin curtain screens it, there will be places beyond the curtain left unilluminated. What is meant by "independent clarity"? It is clarity residing within. A mirror is utterly empty, and thus forms cannot deceive it as to their beauty or ugliness; a balance scale is utterly level, and thus objects cannot deceive it as to their weight. If he puts aside sensual desires and is cautious in his daily conduct, his inner realm will be pure, and the ruler's independent clarity will be manifest. If he distances himself from flatterers and favorites and accepts remonstrance, external obstructions will be removed, and the ruler's independent vision will shine forth. From this, when he brings forth his independent vision and independent clarity to distinguish the talents of the empire: those whose reputation and reality correspond will surely be employed, and the assistants who bear the tripod of state will all be like Yi Yin 伊尹 and Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮; those who possess the reality without the reputation will surely be selected, and ministers who can answer on their own initiative as envoys or wield the battle-axe as commanders will all be like Mao Sui 毛遂 and Han Xin 韓信; those who possess the reputation without the reality will surely be kept at a distance, and empty talkers like Ma Su 馬謖 and Yin Hao 殷浩 will not reach the point of ruining affairs; those who early on suffered an unsavory reputation yet proved admirable later in life will surely be taken in, and men of hidden virtue like Wang Zhan 王湛 and Wei Shu 魏舒 will not be discarded on account of their early years; those who were initially branded as greedy and corrupt yet ultimately displayed lofty integrity will surely be enrolled, and men who reformed toward goodness like Wang Shu 王述 and Xiao Ke 蕭恪 …

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不以始而斥矣初陷兇惡而後更改行者
必察而自新如周處賈淑者不以初而絶
矣陰爲小人者必疎而豎刁之徒不在左
右矣中爲君子者必親而子貢之流竝見
任使矣如此則所用皆真材而似材者無
因而倖進名不浮其實實必符其名亦猶
養由基之於射雖百發無弗中矣造父之
於御雖千里無弗至矣抑愚有說焉辨天
下之材非難使天下之材樂爲吾用爲難
===
是故愛養不可不至也信任不可不專也
微眚不可不宥也宏美不可不錄也陳軫
貴於魏惠子曰夫楊横樹之即生倒樹之
即生折而樹之又生然使十人樹之而一
人拔之無生楊矣子雖工自樹而欲去子
者衆子必危矣愚觀任事之臣竭力以奉
社稷之役一罹讒口則人主爲之投杼故
有十人之譽不勝一夫之毁是生楊之說
也是故愛養不可不至也王登薦士於襄
punctuated: 不以始而斥矣；初陷兇惡而後更改行者必察，而自新如周處、賈淑者不以初而絶矣；陰爲小人者必疎，而豎刁之徒不在左右矣；中爲君子者必親，而子貢之流竝見任使矣。如此，則所用皆真材，而似材者無因而倖進；名不浮其實，實必符其名。亦猶養由基之於射，雖百發無弗中矣；造父之於御，雖千里無弗至矣。抑愚有說焉：辨天下之材非難，使天下之材樂爲吾用爲難。是故愛養不可不至也，信任不可不專也，微眚不可不宥也，宏美不可不錄也。陳軫貴於魏，惠子曰：「夫楊，横樹之即生，倒樹之即生，折而樹之又生；然使十人樹之而一人拔之，無生楊矣。子雖工自樹，而欲去子者衆，子必危矣。」愚觀任事之臣，竭力以奉社稷之役，一罹讒口，則人主爲之投杼。故有十人之譽，不勝一夫之毁，是生楊之說也。是故愛養不可不至也。王登薦士於襄…
translation_en:
…will not be cast aside because of how they began; those who at first fell into wickedness and violence but later changed and reformed their conduct will certainly be discerned, so that those who renew themselves like Zhou Chu 周處 and Jia Shu 賈淑 will not be cut off because of their beginnings; those who are secretly petty men will certainly be kept at a distance, so that the likes of Shudiao 豎刁 will not be at the ruler's side; and those who are gentlemen at heart will certainly be held close, so that the likes of Zigong 子貢 will all be employed in office. In this way, those who are employed will all be genuine talents, while those who merely resemble talent will have no means of advancing by lucky chance; reputation will not exceed reality, and reality will necessarily match reputation. It will be just like Yang Youji 養由基 in archery, who even in a hundred shots never failed to hit the mark; or Zaofu 造父 in charioteering, who even over a thousand li never failed to reach his destination.

Yet your foolish servant has something further to say: discerning the talents of the world is not what is difficult; making the talents of the world glad to be used by us is what is difficult. Therefore, cherishing and nurturing them cannot be anything less than thorough; trusting and employing them cannot be anything less than undivided; minor faults cannot go unpardoned; and grand merits cannot go unrecorded.

When Chen Zhen 陳軫 was honored in Wei 魏, Huizi 惠子 said to him: "Now as for the willow: plant it sideways and it grows; plant it upside down and it grows; break off a branch and plant it, and again it grows. Yet if ten men plant it and one man pulls it up, no willow will survive. Though you are skillful at establishing yourself, those who wish to remove you are many, so you will surely be in danger." Your foolish servant observes that when officials who shoulder responsibilities exhaust their strength in serving the altars of state, once they fall victim to slanderous mouths, the ruler drops the shuttle on their account. Thus, having the praise of ten men is no match for the defamation of a single fellow—this is the lesson of the living willow. Therefore, cherishing and nurturing them cannot be anything less than thorough.

Wang Deng 王登 recommended scholars to Lord Xiang 襄…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
主襄主以爲中大夫相室諫曰中大夫重
列也今無功而授君其耳而未之目耶襄
主曰我取登旣耳而目之矣登之所取又
耳而目之是耳目人終無已也愚觀在事
之臣察其未宜於民不逮三年量移之可
也有罪亟譴斥之可也旣以爲賢而任之
矣卽宜推心置腹令展布四體詎宜屬耳
目於道路而陰擿觖之是賢士程行於不
肖智者決策於愚人况媚嫉者忌其垂成
闒茸者幸其俱敗使有志之士疾首而事
事是耳目無已之說也是故信任不可不
專也孟孫獵得麑使秦西巴載之持歸其
母隨之啼秦西巴不忍而予之孟孫歸而
求麑弗得怒而逐之居三月復召爲其子
傅曰夫不忍麑又安忍吾子乎愚觀言議
之臣一掛當時之網則執筆者輒游意法
之外而緣飾之務快當事者之心或返編
氓或竄士伍卽使無罪而議調亦復優游
punctuated:
主，襄主以爲中大夫。相室諫曰：「中大夫，重列也。今無功而授，君其耳而未之目耶？」襄主曰：「我取登，旣耳而目之矣；登之所取，又耳而目之，是耳目人終無已也。」愚觀在事之臣，察其未宜於民，不逮三年，量移之可也；有罪，亟譴斥之可也。旣以爲賢而任之矣，卽宜推心置腹，令展布四體，詎宜屬耳目於道路而陰擿觖之？是賢士程行於不肖，智者決策於愚人。况媚嫉者忌其垂成，闒茸者幸其俱敗，使有志之士疾首而事事，是耳目無已之說也。是故信任不可不專也。
孟孫獵得麑，使秦西巴載之持歸，其母隨之啼，秦西巴不忍而予之。孟孫歸而求麑弗得，怒而逐之。居三月，復召爲其子傅，曰：「夫不忍麑，又安忍吾子乎？」愚觀言議之臣，一掛當時之網，則執筆者輒游意法之外而緣飾之，務快當事者之心，或返編氓，或竄士伍。卽使無罪而議調，亦復優游
translation_en:
… Lord Xiang, and Lord Xiang appointed them Palace Grandees (zhong dafu 中大夫). His household steward remonstrated, saying: "Palace Grandee is a weighty rank. Now you bestow it upon men without merit—have you merely heard of them with your ears and not yet seen them with your eyes?" Lord Xiang replied: "When I selected Deng, I had already both heard of him with my ears and seen him with my eyes. If for those whom Deng selects I must again hear of them with my ears and see them with my eyes, then examining men with one's own ears and eyes will never come to an end!" When I humbly observe officials currently in office: if upon inspection one is found unsuited to the people, transferring him appropriately before three years are up is permissible; if he is guilty of an offense, promptly reprimanding and dismissing him is permissible. Yet once he is deemed worthy and entrusted with office, one ought immediately to repose complete confidence in him and allow him to stretch out his four limbs and act freely. How could it be proper to attach one's ears and eyes to gossip along the roads and secretly pick out his faults and dissatisfactions? That would mean worthy men having their conduct measured by the unworthy, and wise men having their plans decided by fools. Moreover, the jealous and envious resent a work nearing completion, while the base and incompetent rejoice when everything fails, causing men of aspiration to attend to affairs with aching heads. This is the lesson of "endlessly examining with ears and eyes." Therefore, trust and delegation cannot but be undivided.

Mengsun caught a fawn while hunting and ordered Qin Xiba to carry it home in a cart. Its mother followed behind crying, and Qin Xiba, unable to bear it, gave the fawn back to her. When Mengsun returned, he asked for the fawn and did not get it, so in anger he drove Qin Xiba away. After three months, he recalled him to serve as tutor to his son, saying: "If this man could not bear to hurt a fawn, how could he bear to hurt my son?" When I humbly observe officials who speak out and deliberate on affairs, once they are caught in the net of the times, those who hold the brush invariably let their intentions roam beyond the law and dress up the charges, striving to gratify the wishes of those in power—so that some are returned to the registers of commoners, and some are banished to the ranks of the soldiery. Even if they are without guilt and are merely recommended for transfer, they are still left to linger idly in…

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
散地困抑而不獲伸孟孫之召秦西巴可
想也是故微眚不可不宥也卞和得玉璞
於荆山獻之厲王玉工曰石也以為誑而
刖其左足武王立又獻之玉工曰石也以
為誑而刖其右足文王立和乃抱璞而泣
於荆山之下不敢獻王使理其璞而得寶
焉愚觀疎逖之臣寧無懷瑾握瑜處隱約
而靡由自見者乎微左右為之先容卒按
劍相盻而莫之收矣卞和之泣玉可鑒也
===
是故宏美不可不錄也人主能盡此四者
而天下之材不樂為吾用者否也此鄙生
一得之愚敢以效之執事執事將無塵飯
塗羹其言乎
第三問
葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳 批 究極音律沿革之故殆
無遺旨即牙曠復生當為鼓掌取之
同考試官教諭陳 批 經生類鮮究心於樂者
punctuated:
散地，困抑而不獲伸，孟孫之召秦西巴可想也，是故微眚不可不宥也。卞和得玉璞於荆山，獻之厲王，玉工曰：「石也。」以為誑而刖其左足。武王立，又獻之，玉工曰：「石也。」以為誑而刖其右足。文王立，和乃抱璞而泣於荆山之下，不敢獻。王使理其璞而得寶焉。愚觀疎逖之臣，寧無懷瑾握瑜、處隱約而靡由自見者乎？微左右為之先容，卒按劍相盻而莫之收矣。卞和之泣玉可鑒也，是故宏美不可不錄也。人主能盡此四者，而天下之材不樂為吾用者，否也。此鄙生一得之愚，敢以效之執事，執事將無塵飯塗羹其言乎？

第三問
葉秉敬
同考試官教諭陳 批：究極音律沿革之故，殆無遺旨，即牙、曠復生，當為鼓掌。取之。
同考試官教諭陳 批：經生類鮮究心於樂者，
translation_en:
…in sinecure posts, frustrated and suppressed without being able to advance; one may well reflect upon Mengsun recalling Qin Xiba. Therefore, minor faults must not go unpardoned. Bian He Bian He 卞和 obtained an uncarved jade boulder in Mount Jing (Jingshan 荆山) and presented it to King Li. The jade carver said, "It is a common stone." Deeming him a deceiver, the king had his left foot amputated. When King Wu ascended the throne, Bian He again presented it. The jade carver said, "It is a common stone." Deeming him a deceiver, the king had his right foot amputated. When King Wen ascended the throne, Bian He clasped the uncarved boulder and wept at the foot of Mount Jing, not daring to present it. The king ordered the boulder to be dressed and polished, and thus obtained the treasure within. As I humbly observe ministers who are distant and estranged, how could there not be among them men who cherish fine jade and hold lustrous gems in their bosoms—possessing great virtue and talent—yet dwell in obscurity and adversity with no means to make themselves known? Without close attendants to speak for them by way of prior introduction, in the end they are met with hands laid on swords and suspicious glares, and no one takes them in. Bian He's weeping over his jade serves as a mirror for reflection; therefore, great excellence must not go unrecorded and unemployed. If a ruler of men can fully practice these four principles, could it ever be that the talents of the empire would not gladly be of service to him? Not so! This is the humble, single insight of a rustic student, which I venture to offer up to Your Excellencies. Will Your Excellencies perhaps not dismiss these words as mere playthings of dust-rice and mud-soup?

Third Policy Question
Ye Bingjing 葉秉敬

title: 萬曆十年浙江鄉試錄
text:
生應鐘比于正音故爲和應鐘生蕤賓不
比于正音故爲謬蓋五音相生至于角位
則其數六十有四隔八下生當得宮前一
位以爲變宮又自變宮隔八上生當得徵
前一位其數五十有六以爲變徵變者與
正比則爲和變者與正不比則爲謬此音
有和謬之略也漢書律歷志天地人及四
時爲七始此合而言之也又以黃鐘爲天
始林鐘爲地始太蔟爲人始此分而言之
===
也蓋黃鐘居子爲天統林鐘居未衝丑爲
地統太蔟居寅爲人統故爲三始姑洗爲
春蕤賓爲夏南呂爲秋應鐘爲冬以三合
四是謂七始此三始七始之略也以七音
因十二律爲八十四調除二變聲不得爲
調以五因十二則爲六十調然二變不調
則冬夏聲闕四時不備蔡子之說非而鄭
譯之議是也此六十調與八十四調之略
也以徑象言之黃鐘長九寸爲乾林鐘長
punctuated: 生應鐘，比于正音，故爲和；應鐘生蕤賓，不比于正音，故爲謬。蓋五音相生，至于角位，則其數六十有四；隔八下生，當得宮前一位，以爲變宮。又自變宮隔八上生，當得徵前一位，其數五十有六，以爲變徵。變者與正比，則爲和；變者與正不比，則爲謬。此音有和謬之略也。《漢書·律歷志》：天地人及四時爲七始，此合而言之也；又以黃鐘爲天始，林鐘爲地始，太蔟爲人始，此分而言之也。蓋黃鐘居子，爲天統；林鐘居未衝丑，爲地統；太蔟居寅，爲人統：故爲三始。姑洗爲春，蕤賓爲夏，南呂爲秋，應鐘爲冬，以三合四，是謂七始。此三始、七始之略也。以七音因十二律爲八十四調；除二變聲不得爲調，以五因十二則爲六十調。然二變不調，則冬夏聲闕，四時不備，蔡子之說非，而鄭譯之議是也。此六十調與八十四調之略也。以徑象言之，黃鐘長九寸爲乾，林鐘長
translation_en:
… generates Yingzhong, which is adjacent to a regular tone (zhengyin) and is therefore called "harmonious" (he); Yingzhong generates Ruibin, which is not adjacent to a regular tone and is therefore called "divergent" (miu). For when the five tones mutually generate one another down to the Jue position, its number is sixty-four. Generating downward across eight positions, one obtains the position just before Gong, which serves as Altered Gong (biangong). Then, generating upward across eight positions from Altered Gong, one obtains the position just before Zhi, whose number is fifty-six, which serves as Altered Zhi (bianzhi). When an altered tone is adjacent to a regular tone, it is "harmonious"; when an altered tone is not adjacent to a regular tone, it is "divergent." This is the general outline of harmonious and divergent tones.

According to the Treatise on Pitch-pipes and the Calendar (Lülizhi) in the History of the Former Han (Hanshu), Heaven, Earth, Humanity, and the four seasons constitute the "Seven Beginnings" (qishi)—this is speaking of them collectively. It also takes Huangzhong as the Beginning of Heaven, Linzhong as the Beginning of Earth, and Taicu as the Beginning of Humanity—this is speaking of them separately. For Huangzhong resides at zi and is the Heaven System (tiantong); Linzhong resides at wei, clashing with chou, and is the Earth System (ditong); Taicu resides at yin and is the Humanity System (rentong). Therefore, they are the "Three Beginnings" (sanshi). Guxian represents spring, Ruibin represents summer, Nanlü represents autumn, and Yingzhong represents winter; combining the three with the four is what is called the Seven Beginnings. This is the general outline of the Three Beginnings and Seven Beginnings.

Multiplying the seven tones by the twelve pitch-pipes produces eighty-four modes (diao); if one excludes the two altered tones as incapable of serving as modes, multiplying the five tones by the twelve pitch-pipes produces sixty modes. Yet if the two altered tones do not form modes, the sounds of winter and summer are lacking and the four seasons are incomplete; thus Master Cai's [Cai Yuanding 蔡元定] theory is mistaken, while Zheng Yi's 鄭譯 deliberation is correct. This is the general outline of the sixty modes and eighty-four modes.
